title: Sunny day|| My Actifit Report Card: May 24 2026
body:
> Happy Sunday, athletes and advocates of a healthy lifestyle! We’re staying active with this DApp, ACTIFIT, for our physical and mental well-being.
![1001729208.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/23vsbMC6tvyyFEagw66i6rgY9yKSEQ4BpJBoo9gJQubvT2NsULzQpbXRhQap1zH2CeeLY.jpg)

> Today I went for a walk on the beach—a friend picked me up, and we headed to the city’s urban beach, which is just a 12-minute drive from our home. We walked all along the beach, first on the sidewalks and then on the sand. The sun was really strong, so we decided to walk along the water’s edge—the wet sand makes it easier to walk. We walked several kilometers before reaching the spot where we sat down and then went for a swim; the water was warm and pleasant
![1001729207.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/EogRFBGqxfZ78Nxo5rGxTgqcr3SQB1o2oX9Bn7BAtn4RUS9ziWip4eV7RQT3Yko9Fit.jpg)
This setting, with all its elements, brings me peace. I’m lucky to have it so close, so I take advantage of it and visit whenever someone can come with me. On Sundays, there are lots of people enjoying this little paradise. We left in the mid-afternoon; we couldn’t wait for sunset, which looks amazing here—maybe next time.
![1001729147.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/242Ney9dEyPYcoFvinjmvRAWv8D6TCWFSRwHjaAf69gMkqLY7kB3BoMMzfmbAV7yJM1Lx.jpg) ![1001729103.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/23yTcm5s6SwwLp6LrUq8b38iNn67mfcFh1Tj983tiXdS5UkVAP26f2uqG1immeseGynPP.jpg)

> I hope I can come to this beautiful place every weekend. At night, I walked many blocks and ended my day relaxed and tired, ready for a good night’s rest. I hope the month of May brings me more joy than complaints. That’s all for now, my adventurous friends at Actifit.
![1001729248.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/23wqik6fqCjGnvYxWMgF4kUBZhNGbfaDmaTutx5eVtYpwefrkh15hXKx5nsex85guuooL.jpg)

> >! [spanish,Here]> Feliz Domingo, deportistas y dueños del estilo de vida saludable, donde nos mantenemos en movimiento con este DApp, ACTIFIT, para nuestro bienestar físico y mental. Hoy me fui de paseo por la playa, pues una amiga me paso buscando y nos fuimos a la playa urbana de esta cuidad, nos queda a 12 minutos de nuestro hogar. Estuvimos caminando por toda la habhia, primero por las aceras luego por la arena, y la verdad que el sol estaba fuerte, decidimos caminar por la orilla la arena mojada es más lijero el paso, caminamos varios kilometros antes de llegar al lugar donde nos sentamos y luego nadamos, el mar estaba tibio y agradable. Este ambiente con todos sus elementos me da calma, soy afortunada de tenerlo cerca, asi que aprovecho y visito cuando alguien pueda acompañarme, los domingo hay muchas personas disfrutando de este paraiso. a media tarde nos vinimos, no pudimos esperar el atardecer, que aqui se ven estupendos, sera para la próxima. ojala todos los los fines pueda venir a este hermoso lugar, en la noche caminé muchas cuadras y terminé mi dia relajada y cansada para tener buens descanso. Espero que el mes de Mayo me traiga más alegrías que quejas. Hasta aquí, mis amigos aventureros de Actifit. >_**Photos of my property taken from the Redmi Note 12/// Text translated by DeepL**_

_This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). Check out the original version [here on actifit.io](https://actifit.io/@wendyth16/actifit-wendyth16-20260525t032310649z)_

title: Playa Pampatar, Isla de Margarita [Esp/Eng]
body:
>  ![377834.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/23ycuQYFET5Lk8GqgVXuNz3U2qdcrnCJBFEgvA2NXEqNCjbHaXr2T3jX1ZR66kKnHdVst.jpg) Hola, ¿qué tal, amigos, cómo están por aquí? Todo muy bien, gracias a Dios. Feliz y bendecido inicio de semana tengan todos y que todas las metas propuestas esta semana sean todas realizadas. Por acá, todo muy bien, gracias a Dios, y esperemos que continúe así disfrutando de mis vacaciones laborales más universitarias… El día de hoy quería compartir con ustedes una playa que a mí, la verdad, me gusta mucho en la isla de Margarita. Gracias a Dios, los que vivimos aquí tenemos ese privilegio de disfrutar de hermosas playas, tan hermosas que dejan encantado a cualquier turista. Y hoy específicamente hablaremos de Playa Pampatar, una playa muy visitada por los turistas.
Hello, how are you all doing, friends? Everything’s going very well, thank God. I hope you all have a happy and blessed start to the week, and that all the goals you’ve set for this week are achieved. Over here, everything’s going very well, thank God, and let’s hope it stays that way as I enjoy my university-style working holidays… Today I wanted to share with you a beach on Margarita Island that I, to be honest, really like. Thank God, those of us who live here have the privilege of enjoying beautiful beaches, so beautiful that they enchant any tourist. And today, specifically, we’ll be talking about Pampatar Beach, a beach very popular with tourists.
![20260522_163241.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/EnYRPCkg5JQKPbyTRT1LfSUKjFwKcY5M72zn8E1qTLvLQGJ2Lj2HRikvKdM4u2gGBPQ.jpg) ![20260522_163258.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/EqL7HeWDaZqxc8SPTBa3UyBbkPKTsrqo5xGrqA9iWxTdo7umUUHjYBRfHMz4kokg2Ui.jpg) Pampatar actualmente forma parte de uno de los sitios más visitados de la isla de Margarita, así que esto hace que su playa sea un poco más famosa para mí. Particularmente, me gusta muchísimo por sus aguas cristalinas y por no poseer ningún tipo de oleaje. Además de todo esto, tenemos un hermoso monumento histórico como lo es el castillo, que muchas personas aprovechan para visitar en su visita a la playa, así como también se encuentra la iglesia del Cristo del Buen Viaje, muy hermosa, por cierto; si algún día vienes a la isla, no dudes en visitarlo.
Pampatar is currently one of the most visited spots on Margarita Island, which makes its beach a bit more famous in my eyes. Personally, I love it for its crystal-clear waters and the fact that there are no waves at all. On top of all this, we have a beautiful historic monument in the form of the castle, which many people take the opportunity to visit whilst at the beach, as well as the church of Cristo del Buen Viaje, which is very beautiful, by the way; if you ever come to the island, do make sure to visit it.
![20260522_163356.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/Ep3fJQ8G6Hdh8L7usjAka2D36Bu3q58b9t3g61b6wT36vitXNhYpKVGeKhytdqUpXx2.jpg) ![20260522_174505.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/23ycuUn6CcM3NQ4ucqYo4jHBopRxtTitUF1sqFGRa2CYsgx8KpQKgnkJJgxzAgKn72LgG.jpg) ![20260522_185229.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emilypino/EpC8Rz3NK7i35prqkF86EKZDew69ghG4dE6wqtsrygiEGxgZc56Wr7McEBTDZWA4HbP.jpg) Yo aproveché la oportunidad de capturar estas lindas fotos el día del Pizza Day porque, de verdad, que hacían falta unas lindas fotos en esta playa y les digo que del ángulo en que se tiran la foto seguro saldrán fotos hermosísimas. Y el paisaje que se forma en la noche es demasiado precioso. Un ambiente de total paz. Uno de mis mejores recuerdos con mi novio fue precisamente en esa playa, porque cuando nos estábamos conociendo siempre íbamos a esa playa, así sea por un baño corto, y era algo que siempre hacíamos frecuentemente; por lo tanto, esa playa para mí es bastante especial. ¡Saludos, amigos! ¡Nos vemos en otra ocasión!
I took the opportunity to snap these lovely photos on Pizza Day because, honestly, this beach really needed some nice photos, and I can tell you that the angle from which you take the photo is sure to produce some absolutely stunning shots. And the scenery at night is just too beautiful. An atmosphere of total peace. One of my fondest memories with my boyfriend was right there on that beach, because when we were first getting to know each other we always used to go there, even if just for a quick dip, and it was something we did all the time; so that beach is quite special to me. Cheers, friends! See you next time!

body: I like the thought experiment @mondroid and yes scarcity makes sense.  As Azircon mentions we have a double-sided concern of ideally making production less common and yet we have to fund the game itself and these can possibly run into a concern, but also if well considered by the devs could possibly have a \
where it's possible.  But there are definitely intriguing points to this.\n\nI do like the idea of distribution to targeted people in the community that are \

or are active in behavior that the game would like to incentivize.  

Thought off the top of my head and highly unscrutinized (warning-possible terrible idea)...  What if the packs were not all released at once.  What if up to 2% of the packs sold weekly within an allocation formula that makes the most sense, maybe within say a current modern collection power and perhaps an owned, net staked amount of SPS (that is not being rented out).

While I'm kicking out the crazy half cocked ideas, what about as the season rolls on with a new set, in that spirit cards from the previous set are capped at 2% of bcx levels playable at each level.  Example, Week 1, 2% of the allocation is made available, all cards can only play at 2% of their bcx max--so basically max level 2 common, and level 1 bcx across the board for everything else (regardless of the card levels you have in the previous set).  Week 2, add another 2% to the ceiling of what's playable, Week 3 add and another 2% which would take it to 6% max bcx, and so on.  So it would take up to 50 weeks for max cards to even being played.  Also after 50 weeks the unallocated packs that didn't sell direct then would be available to the masses.

Woof, how's that for a crazy take?  I hope this wild idea does not ruin your well designed and nicely considered post.  Well done @mondroid I love to read this kind of stuff that gets the community's creative juices flowing!  At worst we can daydream a minute and maybe someone else triggers someone else's great idea.

title: Nệm 1m6x2m Giá Bao Nhiêu? Bảng Giá Mới Nhất Và Top Mẫu Đáng Mua 2026
body:
Nệm 1m6x2m là kích thước nệm đôi phổ biến được nhiều gia đình lựa chọn nhờ không gian nằm rộng rãi và phù hợp với hầu hết phòng ngủ hiện đại. Đây là kích thước tiêu chuẩn Queen Size với chiều rộng 160cm và chiều dài 200cm, đáp ứng tốt nhu cầu nghỉ ngơi của các cặp vợ chồng hoặc gia đình có con nhỏ. So với các loại nệm nhỏ hơn như 1m2 hay 1m4, nệm 1m6x2m mang lại cảm giác thoải mái hơn nhưng vẫn đảm bảo tiết kiệm diện tích phòng ngủ. Ngoài ra, vì là kích thước phổ biến nên người dùng cũng dễ dàng tìm mua chăn ga gối hoặc khung giường phù hợp trên thị trường.

Hiện nay, nệm 1m6x2m được sản xuất với nhiều chất liệu khác nhau nhằm đáp ứng đa dạng nhu cầu sử dụng. Nệm cao su thiên nhiên là dòng sản phẩm được nhiều người yêu thích nhờ độ đàn hồi tốt, khả năng nâng đỡ cột sống hiệu quả và độ bền cao. Trong khi đó, nệm lò xo phù hợp với những người thích cảm giác êm ái và độ đàn hồi mạnh. Nệm foam lại có ưu điểm nhẹ, dễ di chuyển và ôm sát cơ thể, mang đến cảm giác thư giãn khi ngủ. Nếu muốn tiết kiệm chi phí, nệm bông ép hoặc nệm xốp sẽ là lựa chọn phù hợp với mức giá dễ tiếp cận hơn.

Mức giá của nệm 1m6x2m hiện nay khá đa dạng tùy theo chất liệu, độ dày và thương hiệu. Với dòng nệm lò xo liên kết, giá thường dao động từ khoảng 3 đến 6 triệu đồng, còn nệm lò xo túi độc lập có thể lên đến hơn 30 triệu đồng ở phân khúc cao cấp. Đối với nệm cao su, các dòng cao su non có giá khoảng 1,5 đến 5 triệu đồng, trong khi nệm cao su thiên nhiên thường dao động từ 9 đến 40 triệu đồng tùy chất lượng và công nghệ sản xuất. Nệm foam có giá phổ biến từ 3 đến 20 triệu đồng, còn nệm bông ép hoặc nệm xốp sẽ có giá mềm hơn, phù hợp với sinh viên hoặc gia đình nhỏ.

Trong số các thương hiệu nệm hiện nay, Gummi là cái tên được nhiều người tiêu dùng quan tâm nhờ các dòng nệm cao su thiên nhiên chất lượng và thiết kế hiện đại. Một số mẫu nổi bật có thể kể đến như Gummi Lite, Gummi Classic hay Gummi Hybrid. Gummi Lite là dòng nệm cao su đa tầng có mức giá dễ tiếp cận, phù hợp với người muốn trải nghiệm độ êm ái và đàn hồi của cao su thiên nhiên. Trong khi đó, Gummi Classic là dòng nệm cao su thiên nhiên nguyên khối với khả năng nâng đỡ tốt, hỗ trợ giảm đau lưng và giữ cột sống ở tư thế tự nhiên khi ngủ. Nếu yêu thích các dòng nệm hiện đại, Gummi Hybrid sẽ là lựa chọn đáng cân nhắc nhờ cấu trúc đa tầng kết hợp giữa cao su thiên nhiên và foam cao cấp giúp cân bằng giữa độ êm ái và khả năng nâng đỡ.

Khi chọn mua nệm 1m6x2m, người dùng nên chú ý đến chất liệu, độ dày và khả năng thoáng khí của sản phẩm. Những dòng nệm có thiết kế lỗ thông hơi hoặc sử dụng chất liệu như bamboo, Tencel hay foam than hoạt tính thường mang lại cảm giác thoáng mát hơn khi nằm. Bên cạnh đó, nên ưu tiên các thương hiệu có chính sách bảo hành rõ ràng để đảm bảo chất lượng và độ bền khi sử dụng lâu dài.



Việc lựa chọn nệm 1m6x2m phù hợp không chỉ giúp nâng cao chất lượng giấc ngủ mà còn hỗ trợ bảo vệ cột sống và sức khỏe lâu dài. Tùy theo nhu cầu sử dụng và ngân sách, bạn có thể lựa chọn nệm cao su, foam, lò xo hoặc bông ép để có trải nghiệm nghỉ ngơi thoải mái nhất cho gia đình mình.

title: La identidad que indica la esencia de cada persona./Identity that indicates the essence of each person.[Spa-Eng]
body: > https://images.pexels.com/photos/10493835/pexels-photo-10493835.jpeg [sourch]( https://www.pexels.com/photo/portrait-of-teenagers-in-swimsuits-10493835/) Todos los seres humanos, animales, aves e incluso todas las criaturas, vivas o inanimadas, presentes en este mundo, poseen una identidad, un nombre y una función propios. No existe nada en este mundo sin identidad, ni criatura alguna que carezca de ella. Así como cada persona tiene una identidad, desempeña diferentes funciones de acuerdo con ella. Somos criaturas mucho más evolucionadas que otras, por lo que, al igual que tenemos un nombre que nos identifica como seres humanos, cada persona posee una identidad específica y un nombre que la distingue. Pero nuestra identidad no se limita al nombre; también se expresa de diversas maneras a través de nuestro trabajo. Inmediatamente después de nacer, nuestros padres nos dan un hermoso nombre de su elección, y según ese nombre, somos identificados en esta sociedad. Gradualmente, a medida que crecemos, nuestra identidad se perfecciona de acuerdo con nuestro trabajo. La persona que actúa es la misma, pero su identidad se determina de la misma manera según su labor. Muchas veces, aunque no recordemos el nombre de una persona, la identificamos por su profesión. Por ejemplo, si no sabemos el nombre de un médico, lo conocemos como tal. A quien juzga, lo conocemos como juez. De esta manera, conocemos a las personas por sus acciones. Del mismo modo, llamamos borrachos a quienes se emborrachan. Asimismo, llamamos devotos a muchas personas honestas que dedican su vida a la adoración de Dios y de diferentes dioses y diosas. De hecho, la humanidad posee múltiples identidades. Por lo tanto, debemos ser siempre conscientes de nuestras acciones. Nuestra identidad se desarrolla en función de cómo realizamos nuestro trabajo. La hermosa identidad que nuestros padres desean inculcarnos cambia a través de nuestras acciones. Nuestra identidad influye mucho en nuestra familia. Si somos malas personas y tenemos mala reputación, nuestra familia y nuestra mala reputación suelen asociarse a ella. En cambio, si hacemos buenas obras, nuestros familiares se enorgullecen de ellas y se les reconoce por su buena reputación. Por lo tanto, siempre debemos ser conscientes de nuestras acciones. Debemos reflexionar sobre cómo actuamos, cómo nos movemos y cómo pensamos y vivimos nuestras vidas. Para vivir una vida plena y construir una buena identidad, debemos realizar buenas obras. Porque nuestras acciones presentes determinan nuestro futuro. Nuestra identidad futura se formará según nuestras acciones presentes. Aunque nuestros padres nos conozcan desde la infancia, a medida que crecemos y comenzamos a realizar diferentes acciones, nuestra identidad se formará según estas y la sociedad nos identificará en consecuencia. Así que, si queremos vivir una vida plena y ser reconocidos positivamente en la sociedad, primero debemos realizar buenas obras y, en función de ello, construir una buena identidad. Nuestra identidad determinará nuestro valor en la sociedad y el respeto que recibiremos. Cuanto mejor nos esforcemos, más personas nos conocerán por nuestra buena identidad y más respeto obtendremos de la sociedad. Podremos vivir una vida plena y respetada. La identidad es algo muy importante y valioso en nuestra vida. Siempre debemos esforzarnos por ser reconocidos como personas buenas y virtuosas. Quienes tienen una mala reputación y una imagen negativa no pueden vivir bien en sociedad. Son constantemente despreciados y, a menudo, incluso abandonados por sus propias familias, lo cual es normal. Esto crea muchos obstáculos para vivir una vida plena. Por lo tanto, debemos siempre hacer el bien y construir una imagen positiva de nosotros mismos. *** https://images.pexels.com/photos/10493835/pexels-photo-10493835.jpeg [sourch]( https://www.pexels.com/photo/portrait-of-teenagers-in-swimsuits-10493835/) We are every human being, animal, bird, and even every living and non-living creature present in this world, each has its own identity, its own name and work. There is no such thing in this world that does not have an identity or there is no such creature that is without an identity. Just as everyone has an identity, they have different types of work according to their identity. We are a much more advanced creature than others, so just as we have a name that we are human beings, each person has a specific identity and each person also has a name to identify them differently. But our identity does not stop only in the name, our identity is also expressed in different ways through our work. Immediately after we are born, our birth parents give us a beautiful name of their choice and according to that name we are identified in this society. Gradually, as we grow up, our identity becomes better according to our work. The person who acts is the same person, but the identity is determined in the same way according to his work. Many times it is seen that even if we do not remember the name of a person, we remember their identity according to their work. For example, if we do not know the name of a doctor, we know him as a doctor. We know the one who judges as a judge. In this way, we get to know different people according to their actions. Similarly, we call people who get drunk drunkards. Again, we call many honest people who spend their lives worshipping God and worshipping different gods and goddesses as worshippers. In fact, the human race is a race that has many identities. Therefore, we should always be aware of our actions. Our identity will develop in the same way as we do our work. The beautiful identity that our parents want to raise in us changes through our actions. Our identity has a lot of influence on the people in our family. If we are a bad person and get a bad identity, then our family and our bad identity often become known as that bad identity. Again, if we do good deeds, our family members are proud of our good deeds and are known as good identities. Therefore, we should always be aware of our actions. We should definitely think about how we are doing, how we are moving and how we are thinking and living our lives. In order to always live beautifully and achieve a good identity, we must always do good deeds. Because our present deeds determine our future. Our future identity will be formed according to our present deeds. Even though we are known to our parents from childhood, when we gradually grow up and start doing different deeds, our identity will definitely be formed according to our deeds and society will identify us accordingly. So if we want to live beautifully in society and want to be known in society beautifully, then first of all we have to do good deeds and according to that we have to build a good identity in society. Our identity will determine how worthy we are in society. How much respect we can get. The better we work, the more people we will be known for our good identity. The more we will get respect from every person in society. We will be able to live a beautiful life with respect. Identity is a very big and valuable thing in our life. We should always try to be known as a beautiful and good person to every person. People with a disrespectful and bad identity cannot live well in society. People are constantly despised by people. Many times they are neglected by their own family, which is normal. It creates a lot of obstacles in living a beautiful life. Therefore, we must always do good deeds. We must build a beautiful identity for ourselves. > Translated by Google Translate. Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@ainun37/moral-degradation-on-social-media-3wf)

title: Why I Needed a Home That Couldn’t Be Erased
body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmP8sZeqCaGfqQkJCaSKemacQUsnDpCiYAdmmfvFvK7JBm/1779678743880.jpg)

Baby Lady YouTube Video: https://youtu.be/OEeMFpGU5DM?si=R0t7bgAPngSK51lQ

Sometimes late at night, when the internet becomes quiet, I think about all the creators who disappeared.

Not because they stopped creating.

Not because they stopped caring.

But because the platforms they depended on slowly stopped letting people see them.

Their posts stopped appearing. Their reach faded. Their communities became quieter. Their timelines became emptier.

And eventually, many of them simply vanished into the endless noise of the internet.

I think about that a lot.

Because meme culture moves so quickly that people rarely stop to ask an important question:

What happens when the places storing our communities stop wanting us there?


---

Living Inside Temporary Worlds

Most of the internet feels temporary now.

Timelines move too fast. Everything disappears too quickly. Creators are pushed endlessly to produce more content just to remain visible for another day.

Sometimes it feels like existing online means constantly fighting algorithms simply to prove you still deserve to exist.

That feeling is exhausting.

Especially for creators.

Especially for meme communities.

Especially for smaller projects trying to build something real while competing against systems designed almost entirely around engagement extraction and corporate visibility control.

People call it “social media.”

But increasingly it feels more like digital survival.


---

Algorithms Decide Who Gets Remembered

One of the strangest things about modern internet culture is realizing how much of human visibility is now controlled invisibly.

You can spend years:

creating,

posting,

building communities,

making people laugh,

creating culture,

and forming emotional connections,


while never actually owning the systems carrying your voice.

An algorithm decides whether people see you.

An algorithm decides whether your work spreads.

An algorithm decides whether your existence remains visible.

And algorithms change constantly.

Quietly.

Without explanation.

Sometimes creators disappear slowly enough that nobody even notices it happening.

That thought scared me more than I expected.


---

Memes Are More Human Than People Realize

People underestimate memes because they think memes are only jokes.

But memes are not just jokes.

Memes are emotional language.

They carry:

humor,

sadness,

frustration,

identity,

community,

memory,

and collective experience.


Entire internet communities speak through memes now.

Entire friendships exist because of memes.

Entire online cultures survive because people emotionally connect through shared humor and symbols.

Memes became one of the last truly organic forms of communication on the internet.

That is why meme communities matter so much.

They are not just entertainment.

They are digital culture itself.


---

I Started Wondering What Would Happen To Us

At some point I started asking myself difficult questions.

What happens if platforms become more restrictive?

What happens if algorithms continue tightening visibility?

What happens if communities lose discoverability completely?

What happens if meme culture becomes heavily filtered, sanitized, or controlled?

What happens to all the creators who built entire identities online?

What happens to all the communities that gave people friendship, belonging, and emotional connection?

The internet has a frightening habit of making things disappear quietly.

Entire communities can fade while the rest of the world simply scrolls past.

I did not want that future.


---

I Did Not Want To Feel Temporary Anymore

I think that was the real emotional turning point for me.

I became tired of feeling temporary.

Temporary visibility. Temporary reach. Temporary discoverability. Temporary relevance.

It felt like living inside rented space where the walls could move at any moment.

And the worst part is that many creators now accept this as normal.

They accept:

unstable visibility,

arbitrary suppression,

disappearing engagement,

and algorithmic dependency


as if this is simply how the internet is supposed to function forever.

But communities deserve permanence.

Creators deserve permanence.

Culture deserves permanence.


---

Then I Found Hive

Hive felt different immediately.

Not because it was perfect.

Not because it solved every problem.

But because for the first time, I felt like I was standing somewhere more permanent.

On Hive, accounts belong to users through private keys.

That may sound technical at first.

But emotionally, it changes everything.

Because suddenly:

identity feels more durable,

participation feels more real,

and existence feels less conditional.


The difference is difficult to explain unless you experience it directly.

Hive does not feel like borrowed space.

It feels closer to ownership.

And ownership changes how communities feel psychologically.


---

The First Time I Felt Less Disposable

That feeling mattered to me more than I expected.

Most modern platforms constantly make creators feel replaceable.

Disposable.

Interchangeable.

If one creator disappears, the algorithm simply pushes another one forward instantly.

But decentralized communities feel different.

They feel slower. More human. More personal.

There is still noise. There is still chaos. There is still internet drama.

But underneath it all, there is also something else:

continuity.

That continuity matters emotionally.

Especially now.


---

Discovering MemeHive Felt Like Discovering A Hidden City

When I eventually discovered MemeHive inside Hive, it felt strangely familiar.

Like finding an older part of the internet that still remembered what communities used to feel like.

Not polished corporate branding.

Not sterile algorithmic content.

Real meme culture.

Chaos. Humor. Creativity. Community interaction. Inside jokes. Shared identity.

It reminded me that the internet used to feel alive before everything became optimized for engagement metrics and advertising systems.

MemeHive still feels community-driven in a way many modern platforms no longer do.

That atmosphere is becoming increasingly rare online.


---

Meme Communities Need Homes Too

People usually talk about infrastructure as if it is purely technical.

Servers. Protocols. Blockchains. Platforms.

But communities experience infrastructure emotionally.

Communities need places where they feel:

safe,

remembered,

visible,

and capable of surviving long term.


That is especially true for meme communities because memes move quickly.

Very quickly.

Without durable infrastructure, entire meme ecosystems can disappear almost overnight.

That becomes even more dangerous when communities depend entirely on centralized systems they do not control.

Hive changes some of that equation because the community itself becomes part of the infrastructure.

That matters deeply.


---

The Internet Is Forgetting Its Creators

Sometimes I scroll through old internet memories and realize how many creators simply vanished.

Not because they lacked talent.

Not because they lacked communities.

But because internet systems became increasingly hostile toward organic reach and independent visibility.

The modern internet increasingly rewards:

constant optimization,

algorithm chasing,

advertising compatibility,

and platform dependency.


That environment slowly exhausts people emotionally.

Creators become trapped inside systems that constantly demand more while giving them less ownership in return.

I think many people feel this now, even if they struggle to describe it clearly.

Something about the internet feels colder than it used to.

More controlled. More artificial. More temporary.


---

Hive Feels Like Resistance Against Digital Forgetting

That is probably the best way I can describe Hive emotionally.

It feels like resistance against digital forgetting.

Not perfect resistance.

Not absolute protection.

But resistance.

A place where:

communities archive themselves,

creators retain ownership,

identities persist,

and culture has a better chance of surviving long term.


That matters enormously for meme culture.

Because memes are memory.

Memes preserve moments. Communities. Emotions. Events. Identity.

Without durable communities, meme culture becomes fragmented and disposable.


---

Why MemeHive Matters To Me

MemeHive matters to me because it feels like a place where meme culture is still treated as culture.

Not disposable engagement fuel.

Not algorithmic filler.

Culture.

That distinction changes how communities behave.

People participate differently when they feel:

ownership,

permanence,

and emotional connection.


And honestly, the internet desperately needs more spaces like that now.

Especially for smaller communities trying to survive without becoming completely dependent on centralized corporations.


---

A Safe Haven For Meme Communities

I do not believe centralized platforms will disappear.

But I do believe communities increasingly need decentralized foundations beneath them.

Safe havens.

Backup layers.

Places where:

identity survives,

culture survives,

and communities survive


even if algorithms become hostile elsewhere.

That is what Hive and MemeHive increasingly represent to me.

Not escape from the internet.

A place where parts of the internet can still remain human.


---

I Think Communities Deserve Better

I think creators deserve better.

I think meme communities deserve better.

I think people deserve spaces where:

they are not constantly fighting invisibility,

they are not completely controlled by algorithms,

and they are not treated as disposable engagement statistics.


Maybe that future will take years to build.

Maybe decentralized social systems will remain imperfect for a long time.

But I would rather help build something imperfect and real than continue depending entirely on systems designed to make communities temporary.


---

I Did Not Want To Disappear Quietly

I think that is what this ultimately comes down to.

I did not want to disappear quietly.

I did not want the communities around me to disappear quietly either.

I wanted a place where:

memory lasts longer,

culture lasts longer,

and communities have a chance to survive beyond algorithm cycles.


Hive gave me that feeling.

MemeHive strengthened it.

And maybe that is what decentralized communities really are underneath all the technology:

people searching for places where they can still remain visible to each other without asking permission first.

title: 🧵👖Manufacturing of women's cargo joggers✂️[ES/EN]
body: >Hola querida y apreciada comunidad artesana,son pocas las veces que pasó por acá mostrándoles mi arte costuril y las veces que lo hago siempre les muestro como hacer desde casa diferentes tipos de prendas de una manera sencilla y práctica. # > Hello dear and valued artisan community, I rarely come here to show you my sewing art, and when I do, I always show you how to make different types of garments from home in a simple and practical way. #

>Les quiero mostrar en este blog tutorial como hice por primera vez un jogger de dama para mí con el poco aprendizaje que tengo del curso de costura que estamos haciendo mi novio y yo y viendo videos tutoriales para hacer uno ,al principio a mi se me hacía bien difícil,pero tenía que intentarlo y practicar hasta dar con el correcto ,varias veces lo intentaba pero no lo podía hacer,una vez aprendí a patronar monos a partir de ese patrón el profesor nos comentó que podíamos hacer diferentes tipos de mono hacerles transformaciones y hasta colocarle diferentes tipos de bolsillos,este jogger es tipo cargo con bolsillos de los laterales y atrás aunque es un poco tedioso el proceso siempre he dicho que vale la pena hacerlo por ti mism@ en casa,es una gran satisfacción después que ya esta terminado,asi que acompañenme a hacerlo.Te estaré compartiendo algunos tips que me tocó aprenderlos durante el proceso. # > In this blog tutorial, I want to show you how I made my first pair of women's joggers for myself. I learned a lot from the sewing course my boyfriend and I are taking, and by watching video tutorials. At first, it was really difficult, but I had to keep trying and practicing until I got it right. I tried several times but couldn't do it. Once I learned how to draft jumpsuit patterns, the teacher told us that we could make different types of jumpsuits from that pattern, alter them, and even add different kinds of pockets. This jogger is a cargo style with side and back pockets. Although the process is a bit tedious, I've always said it's worth doing it yourself at home. It's so satisfying when it's finished, so join me in making it. I'll be sharing some tips I learned along the way. # ---
![IMG_20260522_163953_352.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/anne002/EpNowstkAPKaJfRUHYE36f7peXjq7xJvSbtN3SMf52UZ5jQ7HB1qWXohbTX3JPtyrV5.jpg)
![1_20260407_225637_0000 (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQtvSrXmcJDGmvwWr1co4QENqoGzw9U1WFcj1xDGoCpSt/1_20260407_225637_0000%20(1).jpg)
## _
Materiales: | Materials:
_ # * **_✅Usaremos nuestros patrones o una medida como referencia para el corte de las piezas del jogger_** * **_✅Máquina de coser_** * **_✅Tijeras_** * **_✅Tiza de costura_** * **_✅Elástico del ancho de tu preferencia_** * **_✅Hilo de coser_** * **_✅Cinta métrica_** # > * **_✅We will use our patterns or a measurement as a reference for cutting the jogger pieces_** > * **_✅Sewing machine_** > * **_✅Scissors_** > * **_✅Sewing chalk_** > * **_✅Elastic of your preferred width_** > * **_✅Sewing thread_** > * **_✅Measuring tape_**
![1_20260407_225637_0000 (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQtvSrXmcJDGmvwWr1co4QENqoGzw9U1WFcj1xDGoCpSt/1_20260407_225637_0000%20(1).jpg)
## _
Pasos a seguir: | Steps to follow:
_ #
![IMG_20260522_163026_487 (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSfs7RgUhFA9omAAmjciQEerfDcnvsr5UAZBPcaYJpaCj/IMG_20260522_163026_487%20(1).jpg)
![IMG_20260521_195843_730.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXDhh8fWAEHopLf3W2DMnHcwSHWUaEiMY55odAJvmYLVM/IMG_20260521_195843_730.jpg)
![IMG_20260521_200415_780.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmY136fJYLpdz2VThQNEFiifsi9fvLvXXWkw3NiozVJ22x/IMG_20260521_200415_780.jpg)
![IMG_20260522_162352_568.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmP157FUDdfKWdQx4Z7HhxCFVTwjAyC4Lt32BiaSgrXKLq/IMG_20260522_162352_568.jpg)
![IMG_20260522_163000_690.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNdZhgEYTvXyQYiGS46cBTyLT1JWBjRNhsnqqca264P33/IMG_20260522_163000_690.jpg)
### _Paso 01_

>Procedemos entonces con el corte de las piezas que es lo principal que hacemos en la costura,yo he contado en una superficie plana y a partir del hilo de la tela de derecha a izquierda empecé en este caso a marcar mis patrones dejando 1 cm de margen de costura por todo el borde de mis piezas, corté cuatro piezas para el jogger dos de la parte de adelante y dos para la parte de atrás, corté los bolsillos, corté la pretina y los puños del tobillo del mismo ancho de la bota del pantalón o jogger, después corté los bolsillos doble cada uno ,dos con cortes de vista del bolsillo y dos para la parte de adentro o costado del bolsillo. # > ### _Step 01_ > We then proceed with cutting the pieces, which is the main thing we do in sewing. I counted on a flat surface and, starting from the grain of the fabric from right to left, I began to mark my patterns, leaving a 1 cm seam allowance all around the edge of my pieces. I cut four pieces for the jogger, two for the front and two for the back. I cut the pockets, the waistband, and the ankle cuffs to the same width as the leg of the pants or jogger. Then I cut the pockets double, two with facing cuts and two for the inside or side of the pocket. ---
![IMG_20260522_171841_429.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdvU8XZuoqHGV4yJdZt2jK9wkTdPHryrZi6fv5rH9kLxf/IMG_20260522_171841_429.jpg)
![IMG_20260522_172320_581.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmU76iCQSKYrgVdHkCVwx8bPxFwqqD2uJNV19yvBu2QpkV/IMG_20260522_172320_581.jpg)
![IMG_20260522_172648_828.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmddqMJ1aQN5TtL4eJdmv7AFW3nzPXLuidVbVK883rJtEZ/IMG_20260522_172648_828.jpg)
![IMG_20260522_172821_852.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZ4J6LN7ck4KaxH2K7xBdw9qGmaUrrXsuD8ADxW752joe/IMG_20260522_172821_852.jpg)
![IMG_20260522_172830_931.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcK7RY3DseLKmrrE7UTeeS1ZYY7KxJoZy4ar5rmuX892e/IMG_20260522_172830_931.jpg)
### _Paso 02_

>Después pasé a coser los bolsillos de adentro hacia afuera cada bolsillo en las vistas y repisamos por encima,vamos a unir luego las piezas del tiro del frente de las piezas y repisamos con doble costura arriba para darle mejor acabado a las prendas. # > ### _Step 02_ > Then I proceeded to sew the pockets from the inside out, each pocket on the facings, and we stitched over them. Next, we will join the crotch pieces of the front of the garments and stitch over them with a double seam on top to give the garments a better finish. ---

### _Paso 04_
>Seguido de este paso se llegó el momento de armar lo que yo pienso es mas tedioso del trabajo,coser \

,cada una de las vistas lo saqué doble y los bolsillos si se mantienen de una pieza ,coseremos por el contorno las vistas dejando centímetros de costura y luego la volteamos nuevamen,cortaremos 3 cm de ancho de cierre mágico y lo ubicamos a cada cierre midiendo cada uno,después que los cosemos medimos la mitad del joggers y de esa mitad hacia arriba colocas el bolsillo,para loa bolsillos ,de una. I cut each facing double, and the pockets themselves are one piece. We'll sew the facings around the perimeter, leaving a few centimeters of seam allowance, and then turn them right side out. We'll cut 3 cm wide Velcro and attach it to each zipper, measuring each one. After sewing them on, we'll measure halfway down the joggers and attach the pocket from that halfway up. For the pockets, we'll join the ends of our waistband and the elastic all at once to insert the elastic inside and sew it. In this case, I sewed it this way, but it would be better if you did it the way you learned to do it. It's just a little tip 😊. ---

title: Don't let people pull you down.
body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmadzfFf94sY3N7h1kv61DgdpFv8fW7FnGLkdFwnSAAvYB/4ed94c02_d381_4463_bd57_36402a1b1d8b.png)

----



Recently, I noticed that telling some people about your progress or dreams is not always the best thing to do. Telling those who already think you should remain at your current stage in life was my greatest mistake during my school days.

Some will say:
\

Then they begin to suggest smaller dreams for you.

The painful part is that these are sometimes the same people you expected to encourage you.

I'm not saying you should put God aside — no. But there's a difference between godly advice and words that slowly kill your motivation.

After certain conversations, you suddenly feel sad, tired, or ready to give up on your goals.

The best thing to do is to protect your vision.
Not everybody deserves access to your dreams while they are still growing.


We do go through tough times. We are built different, we are stronger. We go through the storms with mindsets that even in the storms of life, we won't go down. The storms are there to make us stronger and mightier.

There are ways to break through the storms of life — with boldness, calmness and happiness. Going through pain with a smile is something great and it obviously is God's doing.

Don't fade, don't wither, stay sharp even when you are down. Remember, the ones who win were the losers of yesterday. But what they do better is not giving up.

Look at the likes of Muhammad Ali. He didn't budge until it was painful. And how long he could endure those pains is what he counted as progress.

Situations come and go. You don't react to situations, you respond to them. Situations are not what define us, but how we respond tells us about who we are. They can also make us who we are or what we are.

Situations are there to build us. Situations are there to mould us. Even if we feel punished, don't look at the punishment, just the goals.

---

I consider myself to simulate the mindset of Joseph.

Even in difficult moments — from the pit, to slavery, to prison — Joseph remained faithful and focused. When Potiphar's wife tried to tempt him, he refused to let sin take over his mind and destiny.

In the end, the same Joseph they looked down on became a prime minister.

While I was in school, there was a course called Community Medicine. It was considered a simple course, yet many students failed it repeatedly.

In fact, students from my department, Anatomy, failed it far more often than students from the Physiology department.

Some seniors would always tell me:
\

Those words were everywhere. Day after day, all I heard was negativity. At some point, I almost gave up.

But something inside me kept saying:
\

So I cleared away the distractions and stayed focused. I stopped listening to the noise around me. My only goal was to move to the next phase successfully.

I burned the midnight candle. I ignored the naysayers and kept studying.

And when the results finally came out, I passed.

Meanwhile, about 50% of the 120+ students had carryovers.

It wasn't funny at all.

Many people began asking me:
\

And honestly, I even began asking myself the same question:
\

Never give up simply because people say you cannot make it.

*Pamilerin writes.*

---

title: [카일의 수다#877]강원도 설악산 울산바위의 위엄
body:
![IMG_0779.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTvEE8SLh1yKjZgfafFP3SPoxvmCeRAPrRW981bhenrTY/IMG_0779.jpeg)


강원도 여행을 하다 보면 차창 밖으로 스쳐 지나가는 산들의 모습에 자꾸만 눈길이 머문다. 남다른 산세와 웅장한 풍경이 자연스럽게 시선을 끌어당긴다. 그중에서도 저 멀리 산 능선 사이로 거대한 바위 하나가 우뚝 모습을 드러낼 때가 있다. 바로 울산바위다.

처음에는 그저 “큰 바위인가 보다” 싶었는데, 가까워질수록 압도되는 느낌이 들었다. 산이라기보다는 거대한 성벽 같기도 하고, 자연이 오랜 시간 빚어낸 거대한 조각 작품처럼 보이기도 했다. 회색빛 암봉들이 병풍처럼 길게 이어진 모습은 정말 웅장했다.

햇빛을 받은 울산바위는 사진으로 보는 것보다 훨씬 입체적이고 거대한 느낌이었다. 계절과 시간에 따라 시시각각 다른 분위기를 보여주며 사람들의 시선을 사로잡는다. 왜 많은 사람들이 설악산 풍경 가운데서도 울산바위를 특별하게 이야기하는지 조금은 알 것 같았다.

재미있는 건 이름의 유래다.
전국의 바위들이 금강산으로 모여들던 중, 울산에서 출발한 바위가 너무 늦게 도착해 결국 지금의 설악산 자락에 자리 잡게 되었다는 전설. 그래서 이름도 울산바위가 되었다고 한다.

생각해 보면 꽤 엉뚱한 이야기인데, 이상하게도 이런 전설을 알고 다시 바라보니 울산바위가 더 특별하게 느껴졌다. 정말 먼 길을 오다 이곳에 머물게 된 존재처럼 느껴졌달까.

멀리서 바라보기만 해도 감탄이 나오는 풍경이었다.
굳이 정상까지 오르지 않아도 충분히 아름답고, 바라보는 방향마다 분위기가 달라 한참 동안 멍하니 시선을 두게 된다. 역시 강원도의 산은 스케일 자체가 다르다는 생각.

다음에는 시간을 넉넉히 잡고 직접 전망대까지 올라가 보고 싶다.
사진으로는 절대 다 담기지 않는 풍경이었다.

body: for some people, staying fit could help them professionally and in their dating life. Although I have never felt the need to do this, for some people being skinny is accessible, while for others it is not. I have friends who eat three times as much as I do, but nothing happens to them. On the other hand, I participate in fitness and intentionally skip meals throughout the day. Hunger is painful, but at some point, it becomes the most human feeling you can experience. Nothing else matters. Sometimes I intentionally stay hungry, but after a while, my brain starts to lag, and all I get are headaches. Keep in mind, this involves drinking water. I don't really mind discussing drugs because for me, being fit comes at my own cost. Not only can drugs be bad, but when you overdo it, it's still bad. You lose all your intimacy and desire. Even though you look fit, you are not actually well.\nIn the end, people will take drugs for anything: for fitness, for euphoria, sometimes to look skinny. And this time, people have problems with it because it is apparent and undeserved. Why is that?

title: The Renaissance the the USA Didn't Want You to Know About - 12-04-2019 - 10X Speed
body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1779677537769-de9347bf2f0d4172.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=davidnollearth/c026e97f)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=davidnollearth/c026e97f)


---

This is the video series for an oil painting 'Wisteria' I did from 2016-2020.  The painting was destroyed in 2021 due to a number of reasons, but mainly: the painting's faulty experimental linseed-epoxide substrait, Covid-19 crushing lockdowns, extreme poverty, family attacks and ongoing US government (Big Tech + Big Media) censorship of me and my 30 years of artwork.

Its not ideal to not be able to show this piece, but I still gained the knowledge of how to do it and invented several useful oil painting mediums & varnishes used in its creation which never yellowed and still cannot be bought anywhere.

I am posting these videos for posterity and for people that are interested in seeing an oil painting created from start to finish in the Baroque style evolved for the 21st century.  I also must have deleted some of the initial videos when I did the quick underpainting, but what still exists, I give to you.

I hope this can be an educational experience as no gallery will show any of my controversial art even today.

---

title: Sunday stroll through downtown Caracas / Paseo dominical por el centro de Caracas
body:
![IMG_20260510_194627_372.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/23wWvpdZLUNvaEjHYabCzw3CGWjjhG3fnkAQcj7nBKCpo4jtafznYPzjUSKC7gKT7qZeo.jpg)

The historic center of Caracas is one of those places that, no matter how many times you have walked through it, is always pleasant to visit and wander around again.
> El casco histórico de Caracas es uno de esos lugares que sin importar cuántas veces lo hayas recorrido, siempre es grato pasar y darse una vuelta de nuevo.

![IMG_20260510_194627_349.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/23xATNcf174rWVHjZYhGEGa6Jtcbtnb3KBrdisiJimZjmVdch7mUQQfB4yG7yvpecksXU.jpg)



![IMG_20260510_194627_087.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/23u62kDwkLC6moHhqP5xzAN49ZYHKqVoQt5jvHSGgkGdTXStjFMPdhjysRNFHZHRHoj5w.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_194626_988.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/23xedWwTDjrXB1LeAuH6L7CMUjCL4FnrWWAxqaSAPByztN5RofUm5owkUGGy5UK6uWwMp.jpg)

For those visiting the city, walking through the bustling commercial and administrative heart of Caracas becomes almost a mandatory experience.
> Para quienes visitan la ciudad, caminar por el centro caraqueño, de alta actividad comercial y administrativa, se convierte en una experiencia casi obligatoria. 



![IMG_20260510_194626_878.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/23x155XNopTiARe8jaVsyz2eVweuEFZkjzZZgjE7nXCbXxwduCrSckktUoSti4EDEibgY.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_194626_904.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/23uFTmvyBpCszy6iMyZPGJvdUT59kw71GzEN7351HANbSRr7HEbdgKFfWHaFuKpnB6gVM.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_194529_667.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/244UmimUxzxYTyYZkEiZdeFj9AvGcWzWso5A643cmxTinkZe2Ke3Wzd6Q4BBGuudajf52.jpg)

Although on weekdays it is a fairly crowded area, on Sundays the usual hustle and bustle of the center transforms into an unusual calm, reminiscent of the slow pace of old towns in the Venezuelan provinces, creating a quiet and open setting that invites you to observe the general atmosphere of the area more closely.
> Aunque los días de la semana es un sitio bastante transitado, los domingos por lo general, el habitual bullicio del centro se transforma en una calma inusual, que recuerda a la parsimonia de los viejos pueblos de las provincias venezolanas, creando un escenario tranquilo y despejado que invita a observar con más detenimiento el ambiente general de la zona.


![IMG_20260510_194019_937.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/23yJCFAsAU5pRRQJrnsD9dw6SyHWErcHQsPZ1auB7rocXYuutenkPV5LhUQWFL1Wa4SGc.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_194701_239.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/23zGWMR7eauZjmJNPLAtVTk6f3TnTGHw6jjxUoMAV49kfE2Nd8Ps6zAxGhb8o8VnassJ2.jpg)
It is easy to get lost in the architecture surrounding the plaza, characterized by its iconic equestrian statue in honor of the Liberator, Simón Bolívar, and the old Caracas cathedral on its northwest corner.
> Es fácil dejarse llevar por la arquitectura que rodea la plaza, caracterizada por su emblemática escultura ecuestre en honor al Libertador, Simón Bolívar y la vieja catedral de Caracas en su esquina noroeste. 


![IMG_20260510_194700_657.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/23xyNcRKF3w73vp422vEYRuma5udQyGfs7ZCL2w1TbYLweaFFVnJs9gMfwzWKtzTj6SFT.jpg)



![IMG_20260510_194109_985.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/2449woGyQPpasb6yeE2qx3f6mfTkfKth41iviNwotg3fpcRR9HdMhuThsFGCjfDiqAQNs.jpg)

However, most of the buildings around the plaza housing government institutions—do not date back to colonial times, but rather to the republican period of the late 19th century.
> Pero la mayor parte de los edificios que rodean la plaza, sedes de instituciones gubernamentales,  no pertenecen a la época colonial, sino al periodo republicano de finales del siglo XIX. 

These are facades that speak of a Venezuela seeking to consolidate its identity after independence, with neoclassical lines and an air of solemnity that remains intact to this day.
> Son fachadas que hablan de una Venezuela que buscaba consolidar su identidad tras la independencia, con líneas neoclásicas, con un un aire de solemnidad que aún se mantiene intacto.


![IMG_20260510_194019_135.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/2458DpsV7MM8ADdYbQNQuM728ZbgAJH9oJVey1pKfNnScJRk666N9YnLZtaLrASKpzcQw.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_194342_628.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/23w2gphmSfbVrRgLUaExebAh8UCZyGAgzaE5xCrPrx8mXtQAdtdCHjDkQteYw8Sza11gY.jpg)


The imprint of colonial architecture has not disappeared and still quietly coexists inside some buildings and houses in the center, in brick arches and mud walls, and almost unexpectedly, beneath the ground, where part of the old drainage system, designed in colonial times, remains intact and still functions today.
La huella de la arquitectura colonial no ha desaparecido y aún convive de forma discreta en el interior de algunos edificios y casas del centro, en los arcos de ladrillo y tapias y de manera casi inesperada, bajo el suelo, donde parte del antiguo sistema de drenaje, diseñado en tiempos de la colonia, permanece intacto y sigue funcionando hoy en día. 


[//]:# (!worldmappin 10.50611 lat -66.91453 long Plaza Bolívar  d3scr)

Walking through downtown Caracas on a Sunday has its advantages—despite the closed shops amid the absence of crowds and the palpable weight of history, the historic center and its structures stand out in high contrast.
> Recorrer el centro de Caracas un domingo tiene sus ventajas, a pesar de los locales cerrados,  entre la ausencia de multitudes y el peso de los años que se respira, el casco histórico y sus estructuras se revelan en alto contraste. 


 


![IMG_20260510_194700_942.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/astrolabio/23wWrth32D88PpyyDiS6kCjhR5tFPJQzkVawbrndj4ewCcZNUtUyjDHiMHHuz6i12fJA6.jpg)


[//]:# (!worldmappin 10.50611 lat -66.91453 long Plaza Bolívar  d3scr)

title: Argentina - The Boca Juniors corner you have to visit during your time in Buenos Aires. / El rincón de Boca Juniors que tenes que visitar durante tu paso por Buenos Aires. 😃❤️
body:
> After having been surrounded by travelers from all over the world, I discovered just how valuable the City of Buenos Aires is from a tourism perspective. Perhaps as locals we do not pay much attention to it, but our area is full of interesting places to visit and explore. When I returned from my last backpacking trip, I decided to explore those corners of the city that others appreciate so much, with the goal of continuing to learn more about my own province. One of those places was the area surrounding the famous Boca Juniors stadium, and I found a neighborhood full of life and passion for football 😃.
Después de haber estado rodeada de viajeros de todas partes, descubrí lo valiosa que es la Ciudad de Buenos Aires a nivel turístico. Quizás como locales no prestamos tanta atención a esto, pero nuestra zona está llena de lugares interesantes para ir a visitar y recorrer. Cuando volví de mi último viaje de mochilera, me decidí a explorar esos rincones de la ciudad que otros valoran tantos, con el objetivo de seguir conociendo un poco más de mi propia provincia. Uno de esos puntos era el que rodea la famosa cancha de Boca Juniors, y me encontré con un barrio lleno de vida y pasión por el fútbol 😃.
--- ---

> --- --- While looking through the city’s tourist attractions, I realized there are so many places I still do not know, and now I have a long list of outings pending. One of them was the iconic neighborhood of La Boca. Of course, I had heard about it before, but I did not even know where it was located until one weekend when I decided to find out. Getting there took my sisters and me a one-hour train ride and another 20 minutes by bus. We traveled 30 kilometers before arriving, but we are used to these kinds of distances whenever it means seeing something beautiful.
Revisando un poco la oferta turística de la ciudad, me di cuenta de que hay un montón de lugares que no conozco, y ahora tengo una larga lista de paseos pendientes. Uno de ellos era hasta el emblemático barrio de La Boca. Por supuesto que había escuchado hablar de él, pero ni siquiera sabía en donde queda, hasta que un fin de semana me decidí a averiguarlo. Llegar hasta él nos tomó a mis hermanas y a mí, un viaje de una hora en tren y otros 20 minutos en bus. Viajamos 30 kilómetros hasta que llegamos, pero estamos acostumbradas a estas distancias con tal de ver algo lindo.
---

> --- As expected, the neighborhood of La Boca was full of tourists, mainly because it is home to one of the classic postcards of a trip to Buenos Aires: the famous Caminito. But before stopping there for our photo session, we decided to explore the surrounding area a bit. I had heard comments saying that you have to move around this neighborhood carefully because once you get away from the tourist center, it stops feeling so friendly. However, at the time of our visit, everything looked lively and safe.
Como era de esperarse, el barrio de La Boca estaba lleno de turistas, principalmente porque ahí se encuentra una de las postales típicas de tu viaje a Buenos Aires: el famoso Caminito. Pero antes de detenernos ahí y hacer la sesión de fotos, decidimos explorar un poco los alrededores. Yo había escuchado comentarios de que hay que moverse por este barrio con cuidado, porque al alejarse del centro turístico ya no se vuelve tan amigable, pero para el momento de nuestra visita todo se veía animado y seguro.
---

> --- When we left behind all the hustle and bustle of the crowds and souvenir shops, we arrived at the Boca Juniors stadium. This massive stadium, known as La Bombonera, is unmistakable because of its blue and yellow colors, and every matchday it gathers thousands of supporters. But it was not only the stadium painted in those colors — all the shops around it were as well. People have transformed these streets and businesses into true works of art that attract fans from everywhere. Everything looked so picturesque; I loved the area and seeing how the football atmosphere can truly be felt in that corner of La Boca.
Cuando salimos de todo el ajetreo de gente y tiendas de souvenirs, llegamos hasta la cancha de Boca Juniors. Este gran estadio, llamado La Bombonera, es inconfundible por sus colores azul y amarillo, y cada fecha reúne a miles de seguidores. Pero no solo la cancha estaba pintada así, sino también todas las tiendas de sus alrededores. La gente transformó estas calles y negocios en verdaderas obras de arte que atraen fanáticos. Era todo muy pintoresco, me encantó la zona y ver que el ambiente de futbol se respira en ese rincón de La Boca.
---

></center>

---

Club Atlético Boca Juniors is one of the biggest football clubs in Argentina. Its classic rival is Club Atlético River Plate, whose colors are white and red. When it comes to opposites, people will always ask, “Boca or River?”, usually getting almost the same number of answers in favor of one team or the other. Apparently, this rivalry has reached an international level, because many tourists also come to Buenos Aires with the dream of watching a match between the two, commonly known as “El Superclásico.” Of course, there is also a huge business surrounding all of this, with ticket prices reaching ridiculously high levels, yet still always selling out completely. During this visit, simply seeing the stadium from the outside was more than enough for me 😂.

<blockquote>
El Club Atlético Boca Juniors es uno de los equipos de futbol más grandes de Argentina. Su rival clásico es Club Atlético River Plate, con sus colores blanco y rojo. Cuando se trata de opuestos, uno siempre preguntaría \

, teniendo casi igual de respuestas a favor de un equipo u otro. Aparentemente, esta rivalidad escala internacionalmente, porque muchos turistas también llegan a Buenos Aires con la ilusión de ver un partido de ambos, normalmente llamado \

. Por supuesto que también existe el gran negocio alrededor de todo esto, donde hay una venta de entradas a niveles ridículamente elevados, pero que siempre se terminan vendiendo por completo. En esta visita, ver la cancha desde afuera fue suficiente para mí 😂. ---

> --- Visiting the area around the Club Atlético Boca Juniors stadium was an outing that made me feel a little like a tourist in Buenos Aires. I really enjoyed seeing this whole atmosphere, which felt very friendly, at least during the time of my visit. I imagine that on match days this place must become absolutely packed with people in good spirits, an experience I would also love to have someday, especially if it included actually going inside the stadium. As for me, if someone asks, “River or Boca?”, I will always choose Boca because my family supports this team. I do not know much about football when it comes to Boca, but I still firmly stick to that side 😅.
Visitar los alrededores de la cancha de Boca Juniors fue un paseo que me hizo sentir un poco turista en Buenos Aires. Disfrutó mucho de ver todo este ambiente, tan sano al menos en el momento de mi estadía. Supongo que los días en los que hay un partido esto debe ser una locura de gente de buen humor, una experiencia que también me gustaría vivir pero complementando con la entrada a la cancha. En cuanto a mí, si me preguntan \

, siempre elijo Boca porque mi familia es simpatizante de este equipo. Yo no sé mucho del fútbol en torno a Boca, pero mantengo firme mi inclinación hacia este lado 😅. --- ---

❤️ Hope you liked this post! Thanks for reading. ❤️

❤️¡Espero que les haya gustado este post! Gracias por leer. ❤️
--- ---

> ---
With lots of love. / Con mucho amor. Lau 💕.

body:
<center>![1000028719.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/issymarie2/23y8qeUMXt6M5quRhPGVKtm19SBQi31ApSzxkiGhMDbbmm7DRUzgp9rAC5HtYZAPdqta1.jpg)</center>

En la iniciativa número 23 del Séptimo Día, ofrecida por el Dr. @emiliorios en la comunidad @holos-lotus, se nos trae la premisa de hablar sobre [la esperanza](https://ecency.com/hive-131951/@emiliorios/nos-urge-hablar-de-la-esperanza-como-la-cuidas-y-alimentas-esta-es-la-iniciativa-no-24-en-domingo-de-septimo-dia-esen), aquella que hoy en día se ve lejana entre las vicisitudes que cada quien vive en sus respectivos entornos.

​Así como existe la **esperanza**, también existe el **pesimismo**, aquel que pareciera ser el hermano mayor en esta dualidad constante de la vida. Al igual que **el bien y el mal, o el yin y el yang**, la esperanza y el pesimismo nacen del mismo espacio, avanzando en distintas direcciones.

<center>![1000028721.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/issymarie2/242Y5UX9ZsWvBwbUfcUqF9JnhRuPmuammpCt7ZYePQN6EqrFNDQiDcN9jzQr6gbf4xNHR.png)</center> 

​La esperanza, por su lado, es la que suele llevar el faro que da luz a la oscuridad; sin embargo, el pesimismo es la sombra que rompe esas luces desde un punto ciego, sin ser visto. Quizás armado de una honda y certeras piedras, rompe cada foco que la esperanza ha acomodado con esfuerzo y tiempo.

​El punto ciego es ese que todos conocemos, aunque todos llamemos con distintos nombres. Y es que una cosa es cierta: en ese punto muerto donde no llega la luz, pero la sombra sí puede ver, a veces se llama **decepción, otras tantas se llama dolor, algunas veces se viste de rojo intenso con el nombre de rabia** y, la mayoría de las veces, se cuelga un cartel gigante que dice: **\

**.

<center>![1000028722.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/issymarie2/23zRtPDqjAvjhBk5Pdj3vjkZtn73mhWXsaQUyiQZeorCMcWof6DDjpckWeT8qdnUEf5Hc.png)</center>

​Ese punto ciego o muerto lo creamos nosotros mismos por el simple hecho de tener miedo a la frustración, de sentir que hemos perdido tiempo valioso; y allí es donde ese robusto pesimismo se nutre, dando un puntapié feroz a la esperanza, que se ha quedado tan chiquita que hasta una hormiga es más alta que ella.

​Pero en todo esto hay algo muy importante: todos nos cansamos de lo cotidiano, y así como el pesimismo se vuelve conocido, buscamos las herramientas para volver a la esperanza, a ese rayo de sol. Y si el sol no alumbra porque está nublado, no hay por qué preocuparse; la ampolleta en el techo, por más artificial que sea, nos da la misma luz que tanto necesitamos.

​En ese punto, y cuando uno aprende a conocerse, valorarse y respetarse individualmente, es cuando logra que el pesimismo se ponga a dieta y reduzca su tamaño. En esa instancia logramos reflejar una belleza interna y externa, la cual nos abre las puertas, ventanas y rejas, dejándonos ver y dejándonos disfrutar de compañías, lugares y tareas. Porque en este valioso proceso aprendemos que ese **\

**; es decir, así como nosotros creamos ese cartel, nosotros mismos lo cortamos y desechamos.\n\nEn otra arista, también debemos entender que la esperanza no es sinónimo de religión o milagros, ya que también es una emoción. Es aquel pensamiento positivo que grita fuerte ese \

al aventurarse en diversas cosas; esas mismas que a veces dudan ante las palabras de terceros, quienes más que buscar el crecimiento de la persona, buscan restarle fuerza por temor a ser superados. Pero este tema ya sería entrar en otro terreno, uno que desarrollaré en una siguiente entrega.\n\n​Y es que la esperanza es el motor que arranca en aras de crecer. Como decía [Charles Snyder, es el motor que nos permite trazar metas claras, idear rutas para alcanzarlas y mantener la voluntad para avanzar, incluso en la adversidad. Pero para avanzar de esta manera, es necesario que cada uno se conozca, como se dice coloquialmente, \

](https://www.careershodh.com/snyders-theory-of-hope/).

La esperanza no es la última puerta; la esperanza no llega al encender una vela ni al rezar diez padres nuestros o diez avemarías. **Esperanza** es tener la convicción de que podremos superar lo que venga, sea rápido o lento. Es saber que las etapas tienen escalones, y apresurarse a subir de dos en dos o de tres en tres solo logrará que uno tropiece y caiga al inicio.

<center>![1000028723.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/issymarie2/EorzJSfLb4qZHnb3hJjR6ShPPbCV58EEVvYdNZjto85ods9EpkC9dVYzJSrEEa2mgt9.png)</center> 

​Esperanza es entender que la vida no es fácil ni difícil, sino más bien un poco de ambas. La vida es tan \

que en ocasiones nos pone arriba, otras abajo y muchas en el medio; con lágrimas y risas que, al final de cuentas, lo que nos dejan ganar a cada uno es aprendizaje, resistencia, resiliencia y autoeficacia, además de estrategias en el camino para ayudar a nuestra salud mental.

​Es ahí donde entendemos que la esperanza personal ha ingresado a nuestro ser, recobrando el espacio que nosotros mismos, de manera inconsciente, ayudamos a quitarle.

Como digo siempre...
***\

.*** ***

​¿Qué es para mí la esperanza?

​Esperanza es continuar pese a la adversidad o las limitaciones que emerjan. Es avanzar con la mirada fija y el alma calmada, sin aumentar el ritmo en la subida. Y es que, para mí, la esperanza es la convicción de que lo que he aprendido será la llave que me haga llegar a la meta; porque el que corre más rápido no siempre llega antes, y una cosa muy poderosa que también aprendí a reconocer es que forzar las cosas nunca lleva a buen puerto. *** ###
English
***
![1000028719.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/issymarie2/23y8qeUMXt6M5quRhPGVKtm19SBQi31ApSzxkiGhMDbbmm7DRUzgp9rAC5HtYZAPdqta1.jpg)
In the 23rd initiative of the Seventh Day, presented by Dr @emiliorios in the @holos-lotus community, we are invited to discuss [hope](https://ecency.com/hive-131951/@emiliorios/nos-urge-hablar-de-la-esperanza-como-la-cuidas-y-alimentas-esta-es-la-iniciativa-no-24-en-domingo-de-septimo-dia-esen), which today seems distant amidst the vicissitudes that each of us experiences in our respective environments. Just as there is **hope**, there is also **pessimism**, which seems to be the elder sibling in this constant duality of life. Like **good and evil, or yin and yang**, hope and pessimism are born from the same space, moving in different directions. Hope, for its part, is what usually carries the beacon that brings light to the darkness; however, pessimism is the shadow that shatters those lights from a blind spot, unseen. Perhaps armed with a sling and well-aimed stones, it shatters every light that hope has painstakingly arranged over time.
![1000028721.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/issymarie2/242Y5UX9ZsWvBwbUfcUqF9JnhRuPmuammpCt7ZYePQN6EqrFNDQiDcN9jzQr6gbf4xNHR.png)
The blind spot is the one we all know, though we all call it by different names. And one thing is certain: in that deadlock where the light does not reach, but the shadow can see, sometimes it is called **disappointment, at other times it is called pain, sometimes it is dressed in deep red under the name of anger** and, most of the time, a giant sign is hung up that says: **“I can’t, I’m no good, it’s my fault and I deserve it”**. ​We create that blind spot or dead end ourselves simply because we’re afraid of frustration, of feeling we’ve wasted precious time; and that’s where that deep-seated pessimism feeds, delivering a savage kick to hope, which has shrunk so small that even an ant is taller than it.
![1000028722.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/issymarie2/23zRtPDqjAvjhBk5Pdj3vjkZtn73mhWXsaQUyiQZeorCMcWof6DDjpckWeT8qdnUEf5Hc.png)
But there is something very important in all this: we all grow weary of the daily grind, and just as pessimism becomes familiar, we seek the tools to return to hope, to that ray of sunshine. And if the sun isn’t shining because it’s cloudy, there’s no need to worry; the light bulb on the ceiling, however artificial it may be, gives us the very light we so desperately need. ​At that point, and when one learns to know, value and respect oneself as an individual, that is when one manages to put pessimism on a diet and reduce its size. At that moment, we manage to reflect an inner and outer beauty, which opens doors, windows and gates for us, allowing us to see and enjoy company, places and tasks. Because in this valuable process we learn that that **\

**; in other words, just as we created that sign, we ourselves cut it down and discard it.

On another note, we must also understand that hope is not synonymous with religion or miracles, as it is also an emotion. It is that positive thought that shouts out loud “I can” when venturing into various things; those very things that sometimes waver in the face of the words of others, who, rather than seeking the person’s growth, seek to undermine them for fear of being surpassed. But this topic would take us into another realm, one that I will explore in a future instalment.

​After all, hope is the driving force that propels us forward in our quest for growth. As [Charles Snyder] said, it is the engine that allows us to set clear goals, devise routes to achieve them and maintain the will to move forward, even in the face of adversity. But to move forward in this way, we must know ourselves, as the saying goes, ‘inside out’ (https://www.careershodh.com/snyders-theory-of-hope/). 

Hope is not the final door; hope does not come from lighting a candle or reciting ten Our Fathers or ten Hail Marys. **Hope** is having the conviction that we can overcome whatever comes our way, whether quickly or slowly. It is knowing that the stages have steps, and rushing to climb two or three at a time will only cause one to stumble and fall at the start.

<center>![1000028723.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/issymarie2/EorzJSfLb4qZHnb3hJjR6ShPPbCV58EEVvYdNZjto85ods9EpkC9dVYzJSrEEa2mgt9.png)</center> 

Hope is understanding that life is neither easy nor difficult, but rather a bit of both. Life is so ‘difficult’ that sometimes it puts us up, sometimes down, and often somewhere in between; with tears and laughter that, at the end of the day, leave us each with learning, resilience, and self-efficacy, as well as strategies along the way to support our mental health.

That is when we realise that personal hope has entered our being, reclaiming the space that we ourselves, unconsciously, helped to take away from it.

As I always say...
***\

*** ***

​What does hope mean to me?

​Hope is carrying on despite adversity or whatever limitations may arise. It is moving forward with a steady gaze and a calm spirit, without picking up the pace on the uphill stretch. For me, hope is the conviction that what I have learnt will be the key that gets me to the finish line; because the one who runs fastest does not always arrive first, and one very powerful thing I have also learnt to recognise is that forcing things never leads to a good outcome. ***
![1000009838.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/issymarie2/23tbikLyE8Cv6ctyG8KyiR6HZ7Hd2JSAq7evbE5rrDfvjuHR5TcPBY4D8Jy2bToBZP5R4.png)

title: [ESP-ING] Among plants and flowers
body:
>




Entre ir y  venir a la ciudad de Gúarico existen algunos pequeños viveros donde vendes plantas de todo tipo, necesitábamos una tierra abonada para algunas plantas en casa que tenemos y la tierra no es nada buena y hay que replantar, casi que debemos salvarlas, y al entrar vi muchas plantas que me gustan las cuales quisiera tener en casa,  pero no tengo tanto espacio.

La primera que vi fue la flor del desierto, me encantan todas pero había una rayada que me fascinó, pues no es tan común o al menos yo no la habia visto tanto, estas plantas me gustan pues siempre son muy llamativas y decorativas le da  mucha vistosidad a las casas, hace tiempo tuve una hermosa que me daban muchas flores, pero me mue y esa planta se quedó en el lugar, y hace poco compré una y se murió, así que quiero comprar otra lo cual será en otro momento.

Otra de las plantas que me encantan son las rosas, y en este lugar habían de todos colores, pero las amarillas y unas naranjas llamaron mi atención más que las otras, y claro también es porque estaban bastante floriadas, las rosas son esas flores que son hermosas pero tienen espinas, extraño que en mi otra casa teníamos muchas rosas, blancas, rodadas, amarillas, esompre daban flores muy bonitas, pero ahora no ls tengo y me hacen mucha falta. 


Otra de las flores hermosas que vi fue una orquídea, la ve de lejos en el arbol y está plantas trajo indios recuerdos de mi madre y es que a ella le encantaban estas plantas de Orquídea y cada vez que viajábamos a Bocóno ella se quería traer una planta de estas y así algunas veces lo hacía, porque en la vía veíamos plantas en los árboles, orquídeas silvestres era algo normal verlas en cualquier parte, ya que en esas zonas se dan mucho por el clima, pero aquí las vi en un árbol bien floridas y aquí hace calor e igual se dan mucho por.


Los helechos y los cactus estaban hermosos, me encantaron los helechos la forma como colgaban y los diferentes helechos que habían alli, los cactus también habiam allí de varias especies y muchas formas; las flores que  habían como campanita, lirios en fin muchas especies bonitas, se nota que tener un vivero siempre nos va a dejar lindas experiencias con plantas y flores de todo tipo, vi varias personas haciendo actividades en el jardín lo que si lo hace vedero pues hay que tener varias manos para cuidar de todas ess.


Y a ustedes les gusta las plantas y flores?


 



<a href=\

width=472 height=49 border=0>
--- >![ENGLISH] > >On my way to and from the city of Gúarico, there are a few small nurseries that sell all kinds of plants. We needed some fertilized soil for some of the plants we have at home—the soil there isn’t very good, and we need to replant them; we practically have to save them. When I walked in, I saw many plants I like that I’d love to have at home, but I don’t have that much space. > >The first one I saw was the desert flower; I love them all, but there was a striped one that fascinated me, since it’s not that common—or at least I hadn’t seen it that often. I like these plants because they’re always very eye-catching and decorative; they really brighten up homes. A while back, I had a beautiful one that gave me lots of flowers, but I moved and that plant stayed behind. Recently, I bought one and it died, so I want to buy another one—which I’ll do another time. > >Another plant I love is roses, and there were all kinds of colors here, but the yellow and orange ones caught my eye more than the others, and of course that’s also because they were in full bloom. Roses are those flowers that are beautiful but have thorns. I miss that we had so many roses at my other house—white, red, yellow—they always produced such beautiful blooms, but now I don’t have them and I really miss them. > >Another beautiful flower I saw was an orchid. I spotted it from a distance on a tree, and seeing it brought back fond memories of my mother—she absolutely loved orchids, and every time we traveled to Bocóno, she wanted to bring one back, and sometimes she actually did. because along the way we’d see plants on the trees—wild orchids were a common sight everywhere, since they grow abundantly in those areas due to the climate. But here I saw them on a tree in full bloom, and even though it’s hot here, they still grow abundantly. > >The ferns and cacti were beautiful; I loved the ferns—the way they hung and the different types of ferns there. There were also cacti of various species and many shapes; the flowers were like little bells, lilies—in short, many beautiful species. It’s clear that having a nursery will always provide us with wonderful experiences with plants and flowers of all kinds. I saw several people working in the garden, which makes sense, since you need plenty of hands to take care of all of them. > >Do you guys like plants and flowers? > ---
