body.title: ​Sin filtros ni réplicas / Without Filters or Replicas
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQzMcve7T2GLMgBmogRaiiwvzX81FwNRWfZo8F3V5oNUG/1779651651664.png)

Nacemos siendo un lienzo en blanco, pero el mundo, con la prisa de los días, insiste en prestarnos bocetos ya dibujados por otros. Nos entrega moldes, colores premezclados y caminos trazados.
​Por eso, el arte de ser original no consiste en inventar un color nuevo, sino en tener el valor de tomar el pincel con mano firme y pintar nuestras propias luces y sombras, incluso cuando el cuadro no se parezca en nada a lo que el resto espera ver.

<center>• • •</center>

[*​We are born as a blank canvas, but the world, in the rush of the days, insists on lending us sketches already drawn by others. It hands us molds, pre-mixed colors, and pre-mapped paths.​That is why the art of being original does not consist in inventing a new color, but in having the courage to hold the brush with a steady hand and paint our own lights and shadows, even when the picture looks nothing like what the rest expects to see.*]

​<center>• • •</center>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbAmfESpdTZ3YBd3Hor4XZCpPE9PXR5U5fCupaRPrWAiR/1779650462051.png)

​<center>• • •</center>

​Para dar vida a este lienzo, el artista debe buscar sus herramientas en su propia naturaleza, allí donde el ruido del mundo no logra marchitar la raíz. Ser original no es usar tintas artificiales; es pintar con el agua clara de nuestra verdad, con la fuerza de las tormentas que hemos superado y con el aroma fresco de los lugares donde fuimos felices.

<center>• • •</center>

[*To bring this canvas to life, the artist must seek their tools within their own nature, right where the noise of the world fails to wither the root. Being original is not about using artificial inks; it is about painting with the clear water of our truth, with the strength of the storms we have overcome, and with the fresh scent of the places where we were happy.*]

​<center>• • •</center>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmd6ky6ei8fa4eWtwuXrzWFwbNwMhpMi1KF8ZiaELWSyrX/1779650568983.jpg)

​<center>• • •</center>

​Nuestra paleta de colores se alimenta de las cosas más sencillas: la calidez de un recuerdo, la textura de un instante de paz y la delicadeza de saber mirar el mundo con el asombro de un niño. Crear desde ahí es permitir que la vida brote con sus propios colores, sin moldes ni filtros.

<center>• • •</center>

[*Our color palette feeds on the simplest things: the warmth of a memory, the texture of a moment of peace, and the gentleness of knowing how to look at the world with the wonder of a child. Creating from there is allowing life to bloom with its own colors, without molds or filters.*]

​<center>• • •</center>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWDirsqAwmp8EpQ8Qrx7vXfBgd89ZhSR4NeYPzwsbUqBm/1779650832101.jpg)

​<center>• • •</center>

​Sin embargo, como en toda disciplina, el proceso de creación requiere paciencia y templanza. Esculpir la propia identidad no es un acto limpio ni perfecto; está lleno de borrones, de días en los que dudamos del diseño y de noches donde parece que nos hemos equivocado de rumbo.

<center>• • •</center>

[*However, as in any discipline, the process of creation requires patience and resilience. Sculpting one's own identity is not a clean or perfect act; it is full of smudges, of days when we doubt the design, and of nights when it feels like we have lost our way.*]

​<center>• • •</center>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfCaSrwk39CtTuojiFhEC9p6X4P8uT4qdXzmxr1T2JJEc/1779652269664.jpg)

​<center>• • •</center>

​Pero es precisamente en esos dobleces, en las texturas que dejan los errores corregidos y en la resistencia a no dejarnos desdibujar por el ruido externo, donde la obra muestra su verdadera belleza. Ser original es un proceso vivo que se trabaja a diario, un lienzo que se transforma con cada decisión consciente.

<center>• • •</center>

[*But it is precisely in those folds, in the textures left by corrected mistakes, and in the resistance against letting ourselves be blurred by external noise, where the artwork shows its true beauty. Being original is a living process that is worked on daily, a canvas that transforms with every conscious decision.*]

<center>• • •</center>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV4nmZPhDwgZjpbPBbpJXta8STd26sUCPA6vREi2XiUVi/1779654409944.jpg)

<center>• • •</center>

​Al final, cuando aprendemos a habitar nuestra propia esencia, llega el momento de plasmar la firma. Dejar nuestra marca en el mundo no es una búsqueda de aplausos, sino el acto generoso de entregar nuestra verdad.

<center>• • •</center>

[*In the end, when we learn to inhabit our own essence, the time comes to place the signature. Leaving our mark on the world is not a quest for applause, but the generous act of delivering our truth.*]

​<center>• • •</center>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmccM27Hs3WXAsRSH5WLDoFBhsf2taJWFYDuNqGmHUmQpu/1779653645709.jpg)

​<center>• • •</center>

​La firma final de este arte es la alegría de sentirnos plenos y la paz de saber que somos auténticos. Es la certeza de que, en un universo lleno de réplicas, nuestra existencia dejó una huella única, un destello propio e imborrable que nadie más habría podido plasmar.

<center>• • •</center>

[*The final signature of this art is the joy of feeling fulfilled and the peace of knowing that we are authentic. It is the certainty that, in a universe full of replicas, our existence left a unique mark, a spark of our own, timeless and unforgettable, that no one else could have ever painted.*]

<center>• • •</center>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSyge2b9KgcmtSqKULtdBtHqXEy3iMZbnadN1vGDKSVzB/1779652311782.jpg)

<center>• • •</center>

​Y para ti... ¿qué es lo más difícil y lo más hermoso de vivir sin moldes ni filtros? Me encantaría que lo compartieras conmigo hoy.

<center>• • •</center>

[*​And for you... what is the most difficult and the most beautiful part of living without molds or filters? I would love for you to share it with me today.*]

<center>• • •</center>

​📌 Las fotografías presentadas en este post son de mi propiedad física y autoría. Para complementar la estética visual de la publicación, me apoyé en la creación de algunas imágenes asistidas por Nano y Banana 2.0. Asimismo, la imagen de portada fue editada y diseñada por mí utilizando la plataforma de Canva.

📌[*The photographs presented in this post are my own property and authorship. To complement the visual aesthetics of the publication, I relied on the creation of some images assisted by Nano and Banana 2.0. Additionally, the cover image was edited and designed by me using the Canva platform.*]

body.title: Beyond the Red Bars: Rethinking Chinese Land Ownership and Student Visas in America
body.body:
<center> https://img.leopedia.io/DQmWa7ZTnTxNUP8JSpd2xYNAScfk1ALE7sUR2KjNSi5TS7U/Screenshot_20260524-205803.jpg 
[Source](https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1E9CJGvhX2/)</center>

The first instinct you are going to have is actually to be outraged by what you are looking at. Whenever you are looking at this image, especially the bold red bars that is shouting that Chinese actually own a lot of entities and properties in the United States of which the United States has little to nothing in China. Chinese own 247,336 acres of US farmland and the number of Chinese students in America is 261,000 and more.

Why this number might outrage you as a person or trigger you and make it look as if one country gets access to the other country hits the wall but once the emotions are settled down it is time to look into the data if it is true or not. Content like this is meant to trigger us, especially the people that want to make America great again. It is a clear narration of exploitation which people are open to.

Though there is a side of truth in this, the relationship between China and America is asymmetrical. China heavily restricts foreign land ownership and tightly controls foreign influences while the United States is a liberal country and is historically open to everyone which gives it its own name, the land of opportunities. Though this analysis at the top plays two crucial dimensions which is the scale and the context but what it actually means is that Chinese is linked to close to 250,000 acres of land in the United States which is used for agricultural purposes.

That is very huge but when you look at it in the bigger picture that America has 1.2 billion acres of agricultural land and this means that China only has 3-4% of privately held agricultural land. Chinese interest accounts for well under 1% of that foreign owned slice which is around 0.03% of total agricultural land. Then it starts to calm down a little and look at things from another perspective.

Though the graphics may seem so bogus but that is not the case here. This doesn't mean that there is no risk for the American populace, farmland are very sensitive infrastructure and they determine the lot in the country's economic and agricultural landscape. I know he is screaming as if China is buying up American land but that is not true.

Students on the other hand have long been the largest international group in the United States, I mean the Chinese people. While we have very few Chinese in the United States, the gap is purely wide but it is not purely policy. It is just the difference in China's family aggressive pursuit of US degrees.

Why fewer Americans see studying in China as essential to their career and lives? So yes, relationship is the main cause of this, it is not a matter of dominance. This begs the question, should an open society stay open even when its partners are not? When it comes to national security, preventing strategic land grabs, near bases, ports, critical infrastructure or key food supply is something that makes up one of the three issues when it comes to the relationship between China and the United States. Also to be able to reciprocate too.

If America can't buy land or study freely in China, should China entities have broad access in the United States too? Then the third one is the identity. If a country is closing its borders and its system against people of other nations, why can't America also tighten its own borders against people from other nations? Though Donald Trump is actually making efforts to make America great again by making sure a lot of people are shut off so that the American populace can have a lot of opportunities in their hands to take some heaps part, they argue that the real agricultural threat is not Chinese hoeing very minute land, but relentless consolidation of farmland into fewer and fewer hands. So you might be thinking, what should we allow then? There should be a targeted restriction, not a total ban, on buying and use of land for agricultural purposes for outsiders and there should be a lot of transparency, which is very important.

The United States can reciprocate if what it's driving at makes a lot of sense. Though treating students as spies are not actually true, there should be a separation between students and spies because you cannot say someone is coming to study in your country and automatically that makes them a spy. That is not true.



Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@timscreative/beyond-the-red-bars-rethinking-chinese-land-ownership-and-student-visas-in-america-2wr)

body.title: Knowing the Almighty: The LORD works righteousness and justice for all the oppressed. Psalm 103:6
body.body: The Book of Psalms teaches that God is wise and all-powerful, and that in contrast to this are the freedom and imperfections of men; that is why the sapiential Book begins with the Psalm of the Two Paths, the Almighty rewards the sensible men and punishes fools. The divine providence and the entire historical development of the Bible turn around this spiritual problem.\nAnd Psalm 103, which is partly a song of praise and partly a didactic hymn, reminds the Bible readers of this great spiritual contrast: God is merciful, loving, always ready to forgive, but men with their weaknesses repeatedly fall into error again and again.\nThis is why the Psalm begins with these words: \

Psalm 103:2-4.\nPraising God for his wonders is one of the most excellent things, but it is also important to remember that the Lord does not forget his people and those who fear him with all their heart; that is why the hymn wisely reminds to the devotees of the Bible: \

Psalm 103:6.
This phrase from the Psalm is a reminder of the salvation accomplished by the prophet Moses. The Hebrews lived oppressed in Egypt, and through God's righteousness and Moses' courage, the chosen people began their journey to the promised land. But it is also a reminder of the work done by the judges, Israel's first aristocracy. When the Israelites forgot their God, then oppression arose from their enemies, and so the Israelites cried out for God's help, and he, in his love and mercy, sent judges who saved them; judges like Samson and Samuel were a great example of this.
Psalm 103 is a reminder of God's glory and how the Lord, with gifts like mercy and love, redeems and saves humanity, especially the humble and oppressed. Knowing and singing Psalm 103 is a way to recognize the glory of God and how, through the fear of God, men can be blessed.
![Knowing the Almighty. The LORD works righteousness and justice for all the oppressed. > 

Saludos, gamers que dan vida a #Splinterlands. Hoy les traigo un post especial de algunas batallas que gané y una que perdí con elegancia para que disfruten al máximo, ya sea viendo las fotos de cómo empecé y cómo terminé o viendo la batalla completa compartida a través del enlace de Splinterlands.


> Greetings, gamers who bring #Splinterlands to life. Today, I bring you a special post featuring some battles I won and one I lost gracefully, for your enjoyment. You can either view the photos of how I started and how I finished, or watch the full battle shared via the Splinterlands link.

<center>![sep.2026.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pannavi/23tbPXTf1bvy4jaGNjptgQFy5gWYhWKJKS8g2jUuibSPhe56BuNS1C7amKtxLNKAEqeKn.png)</center>


<center>![1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pannavi/23wWkS7Z36YNe1Uwb6Unqa3MWTCRw2v72KJMmcH6auXohiXv1ERTxhb2W6k12km44dkzC.png)</center>


<div class=\

> Y es que no todo se trata de comprar cartas para mejorar en las partidas. La mayoría de mis posts, esos que comparto aquí con ustedes, tratan de eso, pero casi nunca les muestro las partidas que tengo. Son muy pocas las veces que lo he hecho, así que este post es especial porque no sólo hablo de una batalla sino de 4 en total donde gano 3 de ellas y una la pierdo con mucho estilo. > It's not all about buying cards to improve your performance in matches. Most of my posts, the ones I share here with you, are about that, but I rarely show you the matches I play. I've only done it a few times, so this post is special because I'm not just talking about one battle, but four in total, where I win three and lose one with a lot of style. ***

Batalla 1 - Battle 1

*** |![2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pannavi/23uFW8SA6x4DPuEc8dh8vSxCjR9izSkGrpBiRtQVYq4ypBSnnapUo3V1VmcxNPxojZsFG.png)|![3.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pannavi/EoGyrAKqRNuudhGMwST2DLFBkeZnN6AKprfZBgqXzt8rieUGhKuhc4idHUjBGYFA4sG.png)| |-|-|

> La primera batalla que les comparto, fue una muy interesante que me tocó jugar con el invocador de agua. Básicamente, ambos teníamos seleccionadas las mismas cartas, pero en diferente orden, por lo que entendí que no importa qué carta uses; para asegurar la victoria debes usar estratégicamente tus cartas, posicionándolas en lugares específicos que te permitirán ganar. Si deseas ver la partida completa, puedes pinchar el siguiente [ENLACE](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_faab6cceb8991a78cf7b422869da1ada). > The first battle I'm sharing was a very interesting one, I played with the Water Summoner. Basically, we both had the same cards selected, but in a different order, so I realized that it doesn't matter which card you use; to secure victory, you must use your cards strategically, positioning them in specific locations to win. If you want to see the full match, you can click the following [LINK](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_faab6cceb8991a78cf7b422869da1ada). ***

Batalla 2 - Battle 2

*** |![4.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pannavi/23u66vhUsApMKgipNbWKn3pBn1YDYhes5Xmz2Xj3h94r5hNBbKb5fzjxNX22mYSLM76yo.png)|![5.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pannavi/23uQvaKa16cuGsUPBJGitTRpr2aLsHLJ2UpCDsHqckLXxfnZjmLChXimEUbafCYczo9Fx.png)| |-|-| Para esta segunda batalla lo que me dio ventaja fue el nivel de mis cartas. En esta pelea se puede ver que tanto el oponente como yo usamos exactamente las mismas cartas y en las mismas posiciones, pero lo que me brindó la ventaja desde el inicio fue el nivel de mis cartas, sobre todo el del duende. Si deseas ver la partida completa, puedes pinchar el siguiente [ENLACE](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_a4cb0b863d1c91dd6b22936f15f4f6f6). > In this second battle, my advantage lay in the level of my cards. You can see that both my opponent and I used the exact same cards in the same positions, but what gave me the edge from the start was the level of my cards, especially the goblins'. If you'd like to see the full match, you can click the following [LINK](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_a4cb0b863d1c91dd6b22936f15f4f6f6). ***

Batalla 3 - Battle 3

*** |![6.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pannavi/23tmN626qiTBh7Brbpy9wByFe4g5usw23iuXh1Mod8wp9QfEkfbC3N2p5fUEg5UcXiuKP.png)|![7.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pannavi/23tvkkPKiSPo6QY6MKUZnV434z4RRffaNm3NjvPCWhkPkZ6kos3SfULFtxYJiLRT4QZQe.png) |-|-|

> La derrota, pero qué derrota. Aquí vale la pena ver esta pelea, ya que los poderes que venían extras con la batalla en sí me permitieron usar mis cartas a todo dar. Aunque perdí, me dio gusto saber que le di la pelea hasta mi último aliento a este contrincante y que lo llevé al límite. Si deseas ver la partida completa, puedes pinchar el siguiente [ENLACE](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_b5c4f28aad64744cf3d44b0fb3171566). > Defeat, but what a defeat! This fight is definitely worth watching, as the bonus powers that came with the battle itself allowed me to use my full potential. Although I lost, I was happy knowing that I fought this opponent until my last breath and pushed him to his limits. If you want to see the full match, you can click the following [LINK](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_b5c4f28aad64744cf3d44b0fb3171566). ***

Batalla 4 - Battle 4

*** |![8.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pannavi/23uQP5V9HLWvR1XsKssgvVJPscDhfbSLYCt9Usy6B6hz2RKHtpp3S2wza1PFKACSL3zDP.png)|![9.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pannavi/23tRzSvHrj56eyibwZVvYt8FH6zqzSfSdJtxHC7rDRVopcYxSnfqSDGimWiqvkTLkfBoJ.png)| |-|-|

> La batalla final. Una de mis favoritas porque así en general es que me gusta ganar a mi. Que el enemigo me deje casi intocable, con todas mis cartas completas y más aún que sea en el modo moderno. Simplemente este oponente no tuvo vida conmigo. Si deseas ver la partida completa, puedes pinchar el siguiente [ENLACE](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_04a19c2a0e911e5217330ee4da2a65d4). Si llegaste al final de mi post, te doy las gracias infinitas por haberlo leído. ¡Hasta una próxima publicación! 🌸 > The final battle. One of my favorites because that's generally how I like to win. When the enemy leaves me almost untouchable, with all my cards intact, and even better, when it's in Modern mode. This opponent simply had no life against me. If you'd like to see the full match, you can click the following [LINK](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_04a19c2a0e911e5217330ee4da2a65d4). > > If you made it to the end of my post, thank you so much for reading it. body.title: Some Days Are Just Wet!
body.body:
![Gradient Modern Business Youtube Thumbnail (57).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bruno-kema/23xySu8Ziz5SqsAtS8ab3c9Vw3TJRCZxhaaWnCQykiksAPuxAtGs9Rd3WNwPbT6oq9D6X.png) ***
![2dk2RRM2dZ8gKjXsrozapsD83FxL3Xbyyi5LFttAhrXxr16mCe4arfLHA37mQtCuynkak9C9VAyTtPNZ193z3v9HzUXNRYfNBKpop4B452wXWGAr95ns7Froa3QYr2tHe7aDsDXTJuz6E8PeAV3edWS3NGxHQJHC9xJn9eUpGW.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bruno-kema/23uEz3qUu1cpWPYjmp2LnK1i4RcXoAhocX2Rzpq9uYyMScovNm77MZBozX7i1NM59BnSf.png) This has been a very wet weekend for me. And boy, I’m already tired, I swear! We’re now in the thick of the rainy season, and it’s that time of the month when the night before we’re to go out, we take a look at the weather forecast, so we’d know for sure if we should go out with an umbrella, wear a raincoat, or a rainboot. Or for extreme cases, take them all! It’s not raining every day yet, but from how this past week was, I can tell you that it’s now most likely every month at least for the rest of this rainy season. I’ve gotten all my sweaters close by, because based on multiple experiences, e no dae hard for the weather to change. So, however the wind blows, I’m always covered. ![2dk2RRM2dZ8gKjXsrozapsD83FxL3Xbyyi5LFttAhrXxr16mCe4arfLHA37mQtCuynkak9C9VAxm3nacdB7gLmLiZLuYVhHeNsRgxL6WKJoam3hs2B7ZLAp2jwaLFEwoAbLKzAfpv2DhtyvHbJunTbU58RMbxtkvefNK4qj8EA.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bruno-kema/23uQkLUmr2XGp8UpLcdtKeQrWDNnK5jemLpyFynqgRKtzZaqtByEwcX3DoUEyB8Pwi9DN.png) Here in my area, it’s been raining all weekend! Not consistent rainfall, but it’s rained every day since Friday! Friday was by far the worst, it started in the morning and didn’t stop until late in the day. Streets were flooded, and transportation costs increased. It was that point where you no longer cared what you had to pay, you simply wanted to get home. So, if the drivers asked for your kidneys, you’d most likely have handed them over happily. But then, Saturday came around, and we also got rain. It was a bit heavy, but it mainly served to irritate everyone. It didn’t do a lot of damage. The kind of rain that falls, and all you feel is anger, not because of the flood, or because of the hitch in your plans, but simply because you know it will just stress you when going home. And that stress is something that you just don’t want to be bothered with. So yeah, it can be quite infuriating. ![IMG_20230601_151955~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bruno-kema/23u5vyA77YHf5RBKE928nSnMDaruysviNmGZoQjwjqKXRBP5GJwp2xoKeC7X9cwsQvXhc.jpg) And now, today is Sunday, and it has rained yet again! This time, it rained in the morning, when I was preparing to go to mass. It was quite the deceptive rain because it made me believe that I had a shot, but just before I left the house, it opened up and fell heavily for about an hour. We got some clear skies, but the rain returned hours later in the evening. That fell for quite some time as well. And since then, there has been no more rain. I believe it’s done for the week! Of course, there will be more rain during this coming week, and I’m already getting ready for it. In time, we’d be in the 7-day rain, the one where it will rain constantly for seven days. The one where houses in major parts of Lagos will be covered in water. The ones where many people will be stranded because the only mode of transportation for them will be to swim. Yeah… we’re slowly getting there! Well, it’s all good. Let’s get the rains started!!! ![IMG_20240503_082130~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bruno-kema/23wfhuyXMUmf3CdVAiGkt1xRHW5enU4Cxz4s5AzBwB7KKPf4pCHRxVueUwWvZEr4M3NPQ.jpg) ***
Thank you for reading. Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments below, I would love to know what you’re thinking. Till we meet in the next post.
***

body.title: If Fluffy Was A Web - PhotoFeed Contest Macro Photography 171
body.body:
A couple of weeks ago, I was at a family friend's compound garden, getting some utazi leaves. You know, in some village compounds, there's usually this patch at the front or back yard where leaves like ukazi (wild spinach), uziza (piper guineense), uziza (bush buck, Gongronema latifolium), and herbs grow for daily cooking. You'd also find tree plants growing there, mainly as natural trellises or support for the vines to climb on. 

So, it was while pulling one of the long utazi runners or stems, as some people call it, that I spotted the spiderweb between the vines and stopped to avoid damaging it.

I abandoned the utazi, and what followed was about five minutes of phone yoga, just to capture the spiderweb. Zoom in, zoom out, flip the phone upside down, hold my breath, and all. Lol. 

I tried all tactics just to keep the lens steady enough for the camera to lock focus on those fine silk strands of the web. The breeze wasn't even helping matters. It kept catching the spiderweb, making it dangle and sway between the vines.  

> It was funnily frustrating. Argghh! 😂 

However, my patience paid off. At the end, I was able to get some clear shots. 




![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbN5YqB3ELVRco9q2ffciHPM7udSpy7vBu54rwQ3S2tXp/1779655478514.jpg)

***

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXNavvboo11C1vMyhL7JcAtN6F6Fz3KUvQ24fhDw7ntzC/1779655478680.jpg)

***

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUUkJ5WxWyah9cLoXhfcv2zMGmS4HdZiYQB4X4Wx7ihse/1779655478803.jpg)





They're not perfect, though. If you zoom in, you’ll see a bit of motion blur, but they're just manageable. 





This spiderweb is really spot on. Not the usual tight, silky spiral you see in most webs. Look at the fine, clean radial lines and the fluffy white disk in the middle - just looking like cotton or loose fibers. Don't you think? 

Honestly, I think I nailed the shots. Or do you think otherwise? I'd love to know.

**Author's Photos**

body.title: Exode Testers Report   RAIDS
body.body:
Hello again !! Welcome to the seventh Exode Testers Report RAIDS.

This report will present a basic description of the game play, then some writing about some of the testing issues and finally an attempt to provide a brief technical description of what testing is.

**RAIDS**

Raids is the first implementation of PvP in Exode. Being the first PvP interaction with Exode cards, there was a lot of work and still is, some work to be done on balance. Testing involved exploring each card and it's specific traits, evaluating if those traits help with combat, implementing an initial combat scenario and checking results. Results being a long text log of each action, for each facet of combat and mission resolution, all done by manual reading of the output data logging.

This game play is PvP. Players are grouped into teams, 2 vs 2 or 3 vs 3, depending on participation. The objective is to be in control of the sectors at the end of the season with enough points to have more than the other team. Each player is presented a screen with two areas to put team members in (cards, like challenges) and a nine sector map. Each sector on the map has a point value, meaning if your team controls it at the end of the season, those points are awarded. A sector can also have a mission, which resolves as is done in challenges.

The player sends in cards which will enable the mission to be successful. At the same time, the team may need a battle configuration to take on incoming or \

teams. The new addition to missions is control points or pips. These are awarded when the mission is successful and the number of pip are the number of times your rolls beat the requirement. In order for the other team to gain control they must beat the pip count of the current controller. Putting this all together, we have combat and possible missions for each of the 9 sectors. In order to gain control you may have to coordinate your team so that it will be able to fight and have skills to complete the mission. This new game play has provided some extra fun for players as they get to compete and discover new ways that their collection can be used. This is also the first game play where players get to interact and plan the actions as a team.

Here, proto26 has written article with screenshots: https://peakd.com/hive-155862/@proto26/exode-finishes-its-first-pvp-raid-season

Testing began much like challenges, some API calls to invoke various base functions of Raids. A call to generate the Raid, a call to set the teams and the members, a call to send a player's card selections to sectors, a call to resolve the round and a call to save the results of a round. So to set up a test it takes (2 + (2 # players) + 1 + 1 ) 3 calls to finish a Raid season. All tests created were done manually, as I could not figure out a way to automate generation in a reasonable time. Plus the development was taking place as testing was being done. This means that it is hard to produce a test environment for something that is in such flux / change. The current document [Raid Rules](https://exodegame.com/wiki/doku.php?id=challenge-raid) was the product of 3+ weeks of development and testing. An iterative process with bugs and feedback affecting both development and testing. An important thing to note is that the API calls go around all game UI and there is no filtered card selection for me to choose from. This means I have to know what is valid and only pick valid cards, which is an added complication when writing a test case.

At the start tests were easy to make as the valid card set is limited and basic functions could be tested with 2 vs 2 teams during a first round. During the first round, you do not have to worry about card choices other than adding a card twice. Using 2 vs 2 teams was limiting in some cases where I wanted more teams going into a battle than a 2 man team has. A 3 vs 3 test case for the first round was not too bad to create and gave more coverage than could be done with less teams. Moving a 3 vs 3 test case to the second round showed how complicated it gets. With the cards from the first round not usable in the next rounds, I had to keep track of used cards for each player's two teams. Getting all teams set for the second round took ~5 hours. Getting all the teams set for the third round took ~8 hr. This was quite taxing on my brain and really tired me out. In the end the 3 vs 3 test enabled many checks to be made. Once initially created, it was quite easy to change a couple cards here and there for further testing.

The following is an example of a test.  It uses the commands defined in the python test bench, so should be kind of readable by anyone:

SET SEC1 1
SET SEC2 2
SET SEC3 3
SET SEC4 4
SET SEC5 5
SET SEC6 6
SET SEC7 7
SET SEC8 8
SET SEC9 9
SET SCOUT 0
SET STRIKE 1
SET ID combat6
SET_LOG_LEVEL 3
SET_RAID_ID $ID
SET_CHALLENGE_SEED 567987
SET_RAID_EXSEED 1234

GEN_RAID

SET_RAID green sckoarn,blockmonster,raudell
SET_RAID purple doubleozero,veryanprime,tyrnis
-- Raid_id, side, Player, team, Sector, cards
SEND_RAID_PLAYER $ID green blockmonster 0 $SEC2 exode_card_077_SyndicateAyumi,exode_card_065_SyndicateGeisha_ThirdSister,exode_card_074_SyndicateLeader,exode_card_070_SyndicateEquipmentAutoBlaster
SEND_RAID_PLAYER $ID green blockmonster 1 $SEC3 exode_card_081_RebelGeneral,exode_card_079_SyndicateYakuzaSniper,exode_card_080_TheKumicho,exode_card_069_SyndicateShipBlackLotus
SEND_RAID_PLAYER $ID green sckoarn 0 $SEC2 exode_card_077_SyndicateAyumi,exode_card_065_SyndicateGeisha_ThirdSister,exode_card_074_SyndicateLeader,exode_card_070_SyndicateEquipmentAutoBlaster
SEND_RAID_PLAYER $ID green sckoarn 1 $SEC3 exode_card_081_RebelGeneral,exode_card_079_SyndicateYakuzaSniper,exode_card_080_TheKumicho,exode_card_069_SyndicateShipBlackLotus
SEND_RAID_PLAYER $ID green raudell 0 $SEC2 exode_card_077_SyndicateAyumi,exode_card_065_SyndicateGeisha_ThirdSister,exode_card_074_SyndicateLeader,exode_card_070_SyndicateEquipmentAutoBlaster
SEND_RAID_PLAYER $ID green raudell 1 $SEC3 exode_card_081_RebelGeneral,exode_card_079_SyndicateYakuzaSniper,exode_card_080_TheKumicho,exode_card_069_SyndicateShipBlackLotus

SEND_RAID_PLAYER $ID purple doubleozero 0 $SEC2 exode_card_077_SyndicateAyumi,exode_card_065_SyndicateGeisha_ThirdSister,exode_card_074_SyndicateLeader,exode_card_070_SyndicateEquipmentAutoBlaster
SEND_RAID_PLAYER $ID purple doubleozero 1 $SEC3 exode_card_081_RebelGeneral,exode_card_079_SyndicateYakuzaSniper,exode_card_080_TheKumicho,exode_card_069_SyndicateShipBlackLotus
SEND_RAID_PLAYER $ID purple veryanprime 0 $SEC2 exode_card_077_SyndicateAyumi,exode_card_065_SyndicateGeisha_ThirdSister,exode_card_074_SyndicateLeader,exode_card_070_SyndicateEquipmentAutoBlaster
SEND_RAID_PLAYER $ID purple veryanprime 1 $SEC3 exode_card_081_RebelGeneral,exode_card_079_SyndicateYakuzaSniper,exode_card_080_TheKumicho,exode_card_069_SyndicateShipBlackLotus
SEND_RAID_PLAYER $ID purple tyrnis 0 8 exode_card_077_SyndicateAyumi,exode_card_065_SyndicateGeisha_ThirdSister,exode_card_074_SyndicateLeader,exode_card_070_SyndicateEquipmentAutoBlaster
SEND_RAID_PLAYER $ID purple tyrnis 1 9 exode_card_081_RebelGeneral,exode_card_079_SyndicateYakuzaSniper,exode_card_080_TheKumicho,exode_card_069_SyndicateShipBlackLotus

RAID_RESOLVE 1

EXIT


Some of the more interesting issues were \

, like Kumicho. When should the transactor explode and how much damage does it do depending on the conditions triggering the explosion. Fireworks is an explosion weapon as well and some proof of explosions was specifically tested. As it turns out, even with characters that are very good, the player collection size has an affect on how really powerful character cards are. The introduction of research and buildings also introduces some variance between players. Due to all of the bonus from collection and research it is very difficult to say that a balance point has been reached. I think it will be very interesting to see more Raid seasons and how the all resolve.

**Testing**
This may not be for everyone, but some said they could not fully understand what was stated in a previous post.
Testing is the act of proving something is what it is expected to be. This does not mean the proven thing is correct in the end. What??? If the expectations are not correct and it is proven that the object you are testing meets those expectations, then the testing was correct. That may sound crazy or not but, testing is a way to increase the probability that what ever is produced meets some specification or requirement. For instance the universal specification of USB computer interface is something you could use to test against. A known standard with real requirements across a number of technical areas. (electrical, mechanical, data signalling)

In many cases a fully defined specification is not available as the item being developed, is in the development stage, but still needs testing to assist with quality and correctness. This level of testing is more like Development assistant than testing against specifications. In the case of Exode, the development effort is one thing and takes time to create and do very basic testing. After developing something within the Exode environment, we know is random, it is very time consuming to develop and run large numbers of tests on new features. Large numbers of tests are required as the system is random, and because of this, it is very hard to cover everything. Though I have done some testing the current players are also testing through game play. This testing is very valuable as the player is attempting to complete the mission using their card collection. The cards used and choices made by players are good for uncovering any real game play issues.

As an example, the last testing done was to ensure that the cards on a specific list of \

cards never show as challenge rewards. A simple check was created to test for the condition after each mission generation. Then some 1500 tests were run to see if the issue ever shows up. A small fraction of what might be generated, showed no failures.

I hope you enjoyed this little view into the background testing of the Exode Raids production.

Best.

body.title: A Peaceful Night In Ruteng City — The Quiet Beauty Of Flores After Dark
body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmec3L4SDjfyPJDD6nd5yfiuGAa98ePHsmBesCML7ibV91/1000706201.webp 

Not every beautiful place needs bright skyscrapers or crowded nightlife.
Sometimes…
the most unforgettable atmosphere comes from simplicity itself.
Recently, I captured this short night video around Motang Rua, one of the central areas in Ruteng City, Flores — and honestly, moments like this remind me why small mountain towns can feel more peaceful than many modern cities.
🎥 Watch the full video here:
https://3speak.tv/shorts?v=yordan96/eg9m6716

The Calm Side Of Flores At Night
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmX2WMLg9G7kWoKQ15GJcUA6iDLZigq51YqWBS8R578oeL/1000706185.jpg 
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdhtGKmT8M9C714T8FJBtKFpMrTguorwbvnQboFK8fGBU/1000706204.jpg 


Ruteng is located in the highlands of Flores, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia.
Because of its mountainous location, the city has:
cool air
peaceful roads
green surroundings
and a slower rhythm of life compared to larger cities.
At night, the atmosphere becomes even more calming.
The lights quietly reflect through the streets while the cold mountain air creates a feeling that is difficult to fully explain through photos alone.

Motang Rua — The Heart Of Daily Life In Ruteng
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmcrRDFHawHdsuG31b82hbfmrA6NW8EGmSQV6TAyqDheJ3/1000706190.jpg 
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmZPvCu5F7GRYW6aTLWmqUcaWJBaw2ivgjZrQtCa7hEgTt/1000706189.jpg 
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmZY4h95V1pciUspAwq5oLtatDTbJo7DCnaXPmwENnug9K/1000706191.jpg 

Motang Rua is one of the most familiar and active areas in Ruteng.
During the day, this area is filled with:
local transportation
small businesses
shops
food stalls
and daily community activities.
But at night, everything feels softer and more relaxed.
People slowly return home.
The roads become quieter.
And the city feels peaceful in a very natural way.
Personally, I think this is the kind of atmosphere many people around the world are quietly searching for today.
Not noise.
Not pressure.
Just peace.
Why Small Cities Like Ruteng Feel Different
Modern life often moves too fast.
People constantly chase:
deadlines
traffic
stress
notifications
and endless distractions.
But places like Ruteng remind us that life can still feel slow and human.
The simplicity here becomes part of the beauty.
Even something as simple as:
city lights
cool night air
motorcycles passing quietly
or people gathering peacefully
can suddenly feel meaningful.

Flores Is More Than Beaches And Tourism
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmeJy3w7pdaHY6vrb15Nx2ZsYmex1pPVPBVy1ZAqJBpwmf/1000706195.jpg 
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmWQTdpaoNR3vfy2UsGJzEUZRbdeEfKRVevQTSfbMTUgtu/1000706197.jpg 
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVfvJoPEjJqKgdCTeGRUXYPFjbWcmhVf2yKEtfiC95EJa/1000705439.png 

When many people think about Flores, they immediately think about:
Komodo Island
Padar Island
Pink Beach
or Kelimutu Lake.
But personally…
I think the soul of Flores is also found in its small towns and everyday atmosphere.
Ruteng offers something different:
authentic local culture
peaceful mountain scenery
fresh air
and a slower way of living.
And sometimes, those simple experiences become the most memorable part of traveling.
Why Travelers Should Experience Ruteng At Night
If you ever visit Flores, I genuinely recommend spending time in Ruteng not only during the day — but also at night.
Walk slowly through the city.
Feel the cold mountain air.
Listen to the quiet atmosphere.
Because some places are not meant to impress people loudly.
Some places quietly calm the mind instead.
And in today’s stressful world…
that feeling becomes increasingly valuable.
Final Thoughts
This short video may look simple.
But sometimes simple moments carry the strongest atmosphere.
Ruteng at night reminds me that peace still exists in many corners of the world — especially in places where nature, community, and simplicity still live together naturally.
And honestly…
that may be one of the most beautiful things a traveler can experience.

body.body:
>

For some, snails are a delicacy, but for others, 
they're too exotic or unpleasant to even consider trying.
 
However, in recent years, the popularity of snails has been on the rise. This festival, celebrated on May 24th, is an excellent opportunity for both snail lovers and those trying them for the first time.

> Para algunos, los caracoles son un manjar, pero para otros, algo demasiado exótico o desagradable como para siquiera considerar probarlos. Esta festividad se celebra el 24 de mayo y es una excelente oportunidad tanto para los amantes de los caracoles como para quienes los prueban por primera vez.

Humans have been eating land snails for a very long time. This practice dates back thousands of years, to prehistoric times. They were a delicacy for the wealthy in ancient Rome, but were consumed as food throughout Europe. The species eaten was Otala lactea, and specimens of this species have been found in buildings in Morocco constructed during the Roman era. While the practice of eating snails is very old, the word \

body.title: The Receipt Book
body.body:
Right from time Mama Chisom was never a fan of banks.

She did trust one back in 1994, but it went on to disappoint her by swallowing four years of her savings. All she got back in return was a handwritten note of apology. After that incident, she kept her money in three places which are a tin behind a fake wall in her bedroom, the hem of one of her old church wrappers, and the memory of every single transaction she had ever carried out.

She barely wrote things down. She did not need to. She had a very sharp memory as that of an elephant.The market stall has been hers for thirty-one good years. Fabric, Ankara, guinea brocade, Swiss lace, the material for owambes and weddings. She knew every supplier but make, by voice, even by the specific way each one tried to cheat her, and she knew what everything in her stall was worth. Customers as far from the the local governments to buy from come to buy from her. Not really because she was the cheapest — she actually was not — but because she was honest about what she was seeking, which in that market was rarer than the lace.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdv7H5cwDbYcyxe1xc7GBDP6vQccEYqYmSc3UgXG1JGma/bd6dc02f-7103-416c-8c18-71bfe72569cf.jpeg 

Her neighbour at the market, someone who dealt on spare part named Bello, once said that Mama Chisom could look at a piece of fabric and tell you it’s thread counts, it’s country it originated from, it’s wholesale price, and the moss of woman who wove it.Of course he was exaggerating, but not by much. So when her daughter Chisom came to take over the stall for a week while Mama Chisom went to her sister’s burial in Enugu, everyone assumed the handover would be smooth.

But everyone was wrong.

She has never, not once in her adult life, sold fabric.

“It’s one week,” her mother had said, as she packed her bags. 

“The prices are write on the tags. If someone argues, don’t argue back. Just smile and maintain the price. And don’t sell credit for anyone — I don’t care who they say they are, I don’t care if they say they know me. No credit.”

“But mommy I have an MBA—“

“The fabric does not care about your MBA my dear.”

Mama Chisom zipped her bag finally. “I’ll be back Friday.”

She was gone before Chisom could respond, which was what Chisom suspected to be intentional.

The first three days were fine. Chisom sold fabric. She counted change. She smiled at customers and stuck to the prices on the price tag just as her mother had instructed. She called her mother twice a day with updates, and her mother listened and said _good_ in the tone that meant _I am waiting for you to tell me what you did wrong._

Nothing went wrong. Not until Thursday afternoon when a woman came in. She was around her fifties. She wore a wrapper printed with small flowers and carried a handbag that looked faded. She walked straight to the back of the stall where the Swiss lace was kept and began to feel the fabric.

“How much is this one?” she asked, without looking up.

Chisom checked the tag. “Eighty-five thousand.

”The woman laughed. “My dear, I buy from your mother before you started attending secondary school. That fabric is sixty-five.”

“The tag says eighty-five.”

“The tag.” 

The woman finally looked up. She observed Chisom for a moment. 

“You’re her daughter. The one with the overseas certificate.”

“Yes ma.”

“Hmm.” She looked back at the fabric. “Tell your mother Alhaja Rasidat was here. She’ll sort out the price when she returns.”

“Ma, my mother said no credit —“

“This is not credit. This is a standing arrangement. We have been doing business since 1998. Your mother knows.” 

Chisom hesitated. Something told her that she should not let the fabric leave the stall. But Alhaja Rashidat was already gathering the gathering the fabric like it was hers.

“I’ll come back with full payment Monday,” she said.

And then she was gone, moving through the market crowd with the fabric tucked under her arm, before Chisom had fully decided what to do.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmPVJ5jjKk9jVLw3cZMtc6TPjwABhLQibHAJBQF4tFhbeV/67f10470-52e5-4aef-888b-3ce8783e9623.jpeg 


Chisom stood in the stall confused.

Later that evening she called her mother. She almost didn’t, but she did eventually. 

“Mummy. Someone came. A woman called Alhaja Rashidat. She took a bolt of Swiss lace.”

Silence.

“She said you have a standing arrangement,” Chisom continued immediately. “She said she’d pay Monday. The tag said eighty-fine thousand but she said the price was sixty-five —“

“What lace?” her mother asked.

“The cream one. With the —“

“Chisom.” Her mother’s voice had gone very quiet. “That lace is one hundred and ten thousand. I had the tag proved wrong. I was going to fix it when I came back.”

Chisom sat down.

“And Alhaja Rashidat,” her mother continued, “has not bought from me in two years. We had a disagreement. There is no standing arrangement.”

“Mummy —“

“Did you write a receipt?”

The question hit differently than it should have. 

“I…no. You didn’t say to —“

“I always write a receipt. Every transaction. I have receipt books going back twenty-two years in that stall. That is why nobody can tell me a lie about what we agreed and what we didn’t agree.”

Chisom closed her eyes. The MBA from Coventry felt, at that moment, very far away.

“Where are the receipts books?” she asked. 

“Bottom drawer. Left side. Behind the ankara samples.”

Chisom found them. They were ordinary receipt books — the carbonless kind, the flimsy duplicate paper. They were twenty-two of them, stacked and ordered by year, each one filled with her mother’s handwriting. Dates, names, items, amounts, sometimes a small note in the margin — _owes from March, paid in full, asked for discount, I said no.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdLYP8zkBtcif5Wht2JuuJZHm2PKt15ncr4QTfXvQpk7o/b16e5d15-974b-49db-b091-a0578d1043bc.jpeg 


Chisom sat on the small stool behind the counter and opened the most recent one. Page after page of transactions. A living record of thirty-one years of commerce, kept not because anyone told her to, not because tax authorities required it, but because Mama Chisom understood with a certainty that required no MBA, that memory was not enough. _You think you will remember everything,_ Chisom could almost hear her saying. _You won’t. Write it down. The paper doesn’t forget._She turned to the last used page. Her mother’s most recent entry was the Tuesday before she left — a bolt of guinea brocade, six yards, a woman’s name Chisom didn’t recognize, the amount, and the margin, a single word: _reliable _Chisom sat with the receipt book in her lap for a long time.

Then she took a fresh page and wrote Thursday’s date at the top. She wrote _Alhaja Rashidat._ She wrote _1 bolt Swiss lace, cream._ She wrote the amount — one hundred and ten thousand, the real price — and she wrote _taken without payment, no prior arrangement confirmed._
Then she took out her phone and photographed the page.

Evidence, her mother would say. Always have evidence.

Alhaja Rashidat came back Monday. Not to pay — Chisom has not seriously expected her to. She came back with the fabric under her arm and a story about it being the wrong shade, and she set it in the counter with the smooth confidence of someone who had done this before and gotten with it before.

“Your mother will understand,” she said. “We go way back.”

“I know,” Chisom said.

She placed the receipt book on the counter, opened to Thursday’s page.
Alhaja Rashidat looked at it.

“I have the photograph as well,” Chisom said. 

“And my mother is on her way this morning.”

The confidence all of a sudden wiped off from Alhaja Rashidat’s face. 

“You are your mother’s daughter,” she said finally. 

“Yes ma,” Chisom said. “I am.”

Alhaja Rashidat picked up the fabric. She folded it slowly and set it back in its place on the shelf reluctantly.

Then she straightened her wrapper, picked up her old handbag, and walked out of the stall without another word.

Chisom watched her go.

Then she sat back down on the stool, picked up the receipt books, and turned to a new page.

She would need to figure out the right format. Her mother had a system — items on the left, amounts on right, notes in the margin — and it would take some getting used to. But she has for hours before her mother’s bus arrived, and there has been three customers since morning, and she had written receipts for none of them.

She started from the beginning. The carbon paper smudged slightly under her pen. She pressed harder. The paper doesn't forget, her mother had said. Neither, Chisom was beginning to understand, did the market.

When Mama Chisom arrived that evening — dusty from the road, heavy with grief from the burial, moving with the slow deliberateness of a woman who had buried someone she loved — she found her daughter behind the counter with the receipt book open in front of her, writing up the last transaction of the day.

She stood in the entrance of the stall and watched. She didn't say anything. She set down her bag and looked at the receipt book and looked at her daughter's bent head and the careful, concentrated way she was forming the letters.

Then she sat down on the second stool — the one she kept for long afternoons — and she let out a breath that seemed to come from somewhere very deep.

\

she said.

Chisom shifted.

Her mother leaned over, looked at the page, and without a word took the pen from her daughter's hand and corrected the column alignment with three precise marks.

Then she handed the pen back.

\

she said.

Chisom continued.

Outside, the market began to wind down for the evening — generators switching off one by one, voices dropping to the quieter register of people packing up. The lights in the fabric stalls made everything warm and orange. Somewhere nearby someone was frying akara and the smell drifted in, comfortable and familiar.

Mother and daughter sat side by side in the stall, one of them who had spent thirty-one years learning that proof matters, and one of them who had just begun to understand why.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmNwMHqsGH9fsZMapmSuzzb7hv72v8jVQP7xsKPQuRCaUF/2b66a359-761c-48e8-9413-083b2277eb4a.jpeg 


The receipt book lay open between them.

The paper, as always, remembered everything.

Por mi parte, fui a apoyarlos y a realizar mi entrenamiento correspondiente, los vi salir a todos en sus distintas distancias y lo más lindo fue que me encontré con @karlaaviles y después de que vimos a nuestros compañeros salir, nosotras nos fuimos a realizar nuestro entrenamiento, aprovechamos las calles cerradas y corrimos juntas, en el trayecto, nos encontramos con otra compañera del equipo, la acompañamos un rato, hasta que una chica se cayó y entre las dos y otros corredores que por allí pasaban, la ayudamos a levantar y la dejamos en manos de la policía para que la atendieran, le vi algún que otro raspón, espero que solo haya sido eso y haya terminado su carrera bien. 

Nosotras continuamos nuestra ruta, echando cuentos como que si no nos hubiéramos visto en años y desbloqueamos una nueva zona de FC, la zona chisme 🤣 estuvo muy, muy buena. 

Casi finalizando nuestro entrenamiento, nos conseguimos a otra compañera y también la animamos para que terminara su carrera, ya que le falta poco más de 1 km para culminar, nosotras terminamos, nos tomamos fotitos y disfrutamos junto a nuestros compañeros sus logros 🥳🥰 

Y así pase una buena mañana del sábado, dónde dude varias veces si salir a correr o hacerlo el domingo, pero que bueno que salí, la compañía fue de las mejores 🥰

Sigamos enfocados y haciendo lo que amamos 💚

> Hello, friends of the world. Hello, Hive friends, beer lovers, and all those who appreciate the delicious things in life. Today is Sunday, a perfect day to drink and share a delicious beer with you in HIVE's most delicious initiative: #beersaturday.

> I don't know what the weather is like in your countries, but here in Venezuela, specifically in Cumaná, the city where I live, the heat is unbearable. Because of this, it's necessary to have a beer every day to stay hydrated and beat the heat. And that's exactly what I did. I went to a liquor store, and although they didn't have the Polar Negra, which is my favorite, we decided to order a Polar Light.
> Polar Light is a lager-style beer brewed and distributed by Empresas Polar. It's smooth, pale yellow, with a white head that dissipates quickly, 4% alcohol, refreshing, and low in calories.

> I've mentioned before that this is the most popular and best-selling beer in Venezuela, even more so than Polar Negra. Being a mild beer with little bitterness, it's easy to drink, perfect for everyone and for Cumaná's hot climate. We each had three and then left, feeling cooler and happier.

> After having two beers and refreshing ourselves, we gathered strength to continue with all the joy in the world. body.title: El secreto de la eterna juventud está en el alma
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRCXLLUeRAof5gRnMccULwenXwsAUb4TDJC3s9jBG7qQr/1779652044491.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZBbnaXY2auZiLrZ3v2q89KWB9wc8eJycaKBX69B4C5fw/1779652205337.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbA1DtMFgh6R3mHAzorXTsLufN7rUBS3ovtAJywJkPsEa/1779652205378.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfB8edFZqpCVW74rihAvnbHVPvBTKEewCCH5LUSEP9cF9/1779652205419.jpg)


¡Hola! Qué gusto saludarlos en este momento tan especial y lleno de cariño, que estamos compartiendo aquí, dándole forma a este homenaje tan hermoso para Alfredita que recién cumplirá 97 años.

<div align=\

>✨ ══✿══╡°˖✧✿✧˖°╞══✿══ ✨

Hay una línea invisible donde el cuerpo cede, pero el alma se rebela. Ella cruzó esa línea hace mucho tiempo, no para avanzar hacia el invierno, sino para dar la vuelta y regresar al principio, a ese lugar sagrado donde se es niña para siempre, su juventud actual no es un capricho del destino ni un simple rasgo de su carácter; es un pacto directo entre su fe y su libertad. Ella se niega a dormirse porque el mundo tiene demasiado color como para mirarlo con los ojos cerrados. Mientras el tiempo insiste en inclinar los hombros de los hombres, ella desafía las leyes de la gravedad y de los años, definitivamente es sorprendente verla mirar la copa de un árbol y, en lugar de calcular la sombra para recostarse un rato, ella calcula el ascenso para subir a el y probar sus frutos. Hay un vigor extraordinario, casi místico, en sus piernas que no se cansan de caminar y en sus manos que aún encuentran alegría en los oficios diarios, transformando la rutina en una forma de agradecimiento vivo. Cuando sube, cuando camina, cuando limpia, no está cumpliendo una tarea: está celebrando que está viva. Su secreto no es un misterio para ella, con la sencillez de los sabios, lo resume en una sola verdad absoluta: «Todo esto me lo da Dios». Y se nota, hay una gracia divina en la forma en que habita su cuerpo, una ligereza que solo poseen quienes han aprendido a entregar sus cargas al cielo, su fuerza no proviene de la carne, sino de una fuente inagotable de gratitud que la renueva cada mañana. Pero quizás su mayor milagro no es su asombrosa energía física, sino la generosidad de su presencia, ella es un refugio andante, no importa quién se acerque, jamás encuentra el silencio frío de la indiferencia; siempre hay una palabra en su boca, un saludo, un consejo o una bendición tejida con hilos de ternura. Es un alma profundamente agradable, de esas que sanan los lugares con solo sentarse en ellos, su alegría no es ruidosa ni artificial; es la paz de quien ha vuelto a ser niña porque ya no tiene nada que demostrarle al mundo. Verla es entender que la vejez es solo una convención humana, ella camina por la tierra con los pies firmes, pero con el corazón suspendido en una infancia eterna, sostenida por la mano del Creador, recordándonos a todos que la vida no se mide en los años que se acumulan, sino en el vigor con el que el alma decide seguir viviendo. ​

>
Qué bonito es poder compartir con esta hermosa comunidad las bendiciones que Dios nos regala día a día. 

Nos vemos muy pronto para seguir compartiendo más vivencias e historias que nos llenan el alma. ¡Un abrazo enorme y que Dios los bendiga grandemente!

body.title: ¡¿5 meses de producto?! - Gel limpiador facial de Barunu - Reseña [SPA/ENG]
body.body: > **ESPAÑOL** Les muestro esta joyita, que amé, amo y seguiré amando. Este es el Gel limpiador facial de Barunu, con Aloe Vera y Acido Salicílico perfecto para pieles grasas, con tendencia a acné. Quiero comenzar comentarles sobre la marca, diciendo lo que promete el producto y, su precio, para luego darles mi reseña y experiencia honesta. Todos los productos de BARUNU nacen del Aloe Vera (Sábila), gracias a la cantidad de nutrientes que se encuentran en los cristales de la planta, siendo esta rica en vitaminas, aminoácidos y minerales. Sabemos que esta planta es muy usada en cosméticos o recetas caseras. Pues, BARUNU tiene una gran variedad de productos de excelente calidad y este Gel, no es la excepción, contiene Aloe Vera (Sábila) como base y además Acido Salicílico, el cual ayuda con los poros dilatados limpiándolos desde adentro y regula la producción de sebo o grasa de la piel. En este caso el Gel limpiador ayuda a hidratar reparando la barrera cutánea mientras la limpia a profundidad regulando la producción de grasa. Suena a maravilla, sobre todo para pieles mixtas o grasas como la mía, cabe destacar que esta marca tiene 3 Geles limpiadores según el tipo de piel y cuidado que mereces, en mi caso he usado solo dos y este fue el primero que compré para probar la marca. En Farmatodo tiene un precio de 10$ y contiene 280 ml. Este producto llegó a ser viral en Tiktok un tiempo y era difícil conseguirlo, en mi caso lo fue y siempre encontraba el verde turquesa que es para todo tipo de piel, pero el naranja por sus otros componente es ideal para pieles como la mía, me tocó buscar por la mayoría de las sedes cercanas de Farmatodo hasta encontrarlo, era el único que había y ya ni recordaba el precio cuando lo tomé y al pagar me quedé tiesa jajajaja 10$ me pareció mucho para algo que tal vez ni me iba a durar, pues es un gel y comparado con una barra de jabón asocié que la duración era muy poca.

> **ENGLISH** Let me show you this little gem that I loved, love, and will continue to love. This is Barunu’s Facial Cleansing Gel, with aloe vera and salicylic acid—perfect for oily, acne-prone skin. I want to start by telling you about the brand, what the product promises, and its price, and then give you my honest review and experience. All BARUNU products are derived from Aloe Vera, thanks to the abundance of nutrients found in the plant’s gel, which is rich in vitamins, amino acids, and minerals. We know this plant is widely used in cosmetics and homemade recipes. Well, BARUNU offers a wide variety of high-quality products, and this gel is no exception. It’s formulated with Aloe Vera as its base and also contains Salicylic Acid, which helps with enlarged pores by cleansing them from the inside and regulating the skin’s sebum or oil production. In this case, the cleansing gel helps hydrate and repair the skin barrier while deeply cleansing it and regulating oil production. It sounds wonderful, especially for combination or oily skin like mine. It’s worth noting that this brand offers three cleansing gels tailored to your skin type and the care you deserve; in my case, I’ve only used two, and this was the first one I bought to try the brand. At Farmatodo, it costs $10 and contains 280 ml. This product went viral on TikTok for a while and was hard to find. In my case, it was—I always came across the turquoise one, which is for all skin types, but the orange one, because of its other ingredients, is ideal for skin like mine. I had to search through most of the nearby Farmatodo locations until I found it; it was the only one they had, and I didn’t even remember the price when I picked it up. When I went to pay, I froze—hahaha—$10 seemed like a lot to me for something that might not even last, since it’s a gel, and compared to a bar of soap, I figured it wouldn’t last very long. --- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amatorrs/AJL7K3UPaqwRTirGKxUiPA4jJqk45KEtSXMD9xicoNSppSeg7KMoyxWgYne4ojF.png)
[Fuente de imagen](https://barunu.com/producto/gel-limpiador-hidratante-con-aloe-y-acido-salicilico/) En la imagen dice 235 ml, pero el que compré dice 280 ml
![photo_2026-05-24_16-24-34.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amatorrs/Eq12W3mgAnGjRKjEeP5mLcRXmbL438kHMVsDVE4a17Rt24mZzivNUDz8Nsx3kUM4RRB.jpg)
![Divisor.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amatorrs/48FDvGhme6ZfCsCs15pruz9iTPxNLHix8kdTySMyVEDco5tqZgVFdcTwjUPsoCnTyN.png)

> Ahora sí lo que nos interesa jajaja al principio con la primera lavada (cabe destacar que al volver de mi casa luego de comprarlo lo primero que hice fue usarlo jeje) pues no creo mucha espuma ni tuve la sensación de que estuviera limpiando mi piel, lo cual me decepcionó, pero al enjuagar y mirar el resultado quedé maravillada, pues mis poros se veían limpios y algo pequeños a comparación de como ya venia de la calle (también resalto que yo sudo en exceso y la grasa en mi piel es una locura jajaja), otra cosa que noté fue la textura que deja, bastante mate pero la piel se siente hidratada y fresca, no deja para nada esa sensación de templanza que tienen otros jabones principalmente en barra. Mientras más lo usaba mejor era la regulación de sebo y por ende menos acné, ya antes había usado Acido salicílico en gel y sabia que el contenido de este limpiador me iba a funcionar, pero no sabia a que grado, la sensación de frescura es muy buena, pero si admito que casi no hace espuma a menos que repitas el procedimiento y por eso puedes pensar que no está haciendo efecto, aunque los resultados en tu piel se sienten y se ven enormemente. Otra cosa que noté es lo mucho, mucho que me duró. Casi los 5 meses y sé porque no duró más jajaja, pues al gustarme tanto lo compartí un tiempo con mi hermana al punto que se enamoró del producto y se compró el suyo propio (estábamos juntas en vacaciones, ella vive lejos), a mi hermana si le duró los 5 meses y algunos días lo cual nos pareció una excelente inversión por la calidad, resultados y duración del producto. También supe que algunos familiares usaron mi jabón creyendo que era para manos, mala idea dejarlo en el lavamanos teniendo visitas :c.

> Now, onto what we’re really interested in, hahaha. At first, with the first wash (it’s worth noting that when I got home after buying it, the first thing I did was use it, hehe), it didn’t lather much, and I didn’t feel like it was actually cleaning my skin, which disappointed me. But when I rinsed it off and saw the result, I was amazed— because my pores looked clean and somewhat smaller compared to how they looked when I came in from outside (I should also mention that I sweat a lot and the oiliness of my skin is crazy, haha). Another thing I noticed was the texture it leaves behind—quite matte, but my skin feels hydrated and fresh. It doesn’t leave that tight, dry feeling that other soaps, especially bar soaps, tend to have. The more I used it, the better it regulated my oil production, which meant less acne. body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTJKG1o2KTprcia3wFmrAYyfFyNTXg1hBamUsxjwnRGGb/_dsc6732_copia.jpg)


* * *

The photos 📸 are my entry to the #monomad contest from @monochromes and @brumest.

* * *




Hello hivers.

Street photography has always felt like an honest way of looking at the world to me. There are no poses and no absolute control, just small moments that appear and disappear within seconds. Sometimes a single glance, a shadow, or someone walking quietly is enough to tell an entire story.

Today I went out with my camera without a clear destination, simply letting the streets speak for themselves. Between the noise, movement, and everyday chaos, I found those little moments that usually go unnoticed. Maybe that is the magic of street photography, learning to see beauty where others only see routine.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVM4L5DKtbNfqsDufUuWgFjX5jrBHv9Lv73zRRXXxgq7r/_dsc6731_copia.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXPhVHBU2brWQUdkUdKjgcGQdE2QJK24YXdHbxF85xPpW/_dsc6733_copia.jpg)

Saludos hivers.

La fotografía de calle siempre me ha parecido una forma honesta de mirar el mundo. No hay poses, no hay control absoluto, solo pequeños instantes que aparecen y desaparecen en segundos. A veces basta una mirada, una sombra o una persona caminando en silencio para contar toda una historia.

Hoy salí con la cámara sin un destino claro, simplemente dejando que la calle hablara por sí sola. Entre el ruido, el movimiento y el caos cotidiano, encontré esos pequeños momentos que normalmente pasan desapercibidos. Y quizás ahí está la magia de este tipo de fotografía, en aprender a ver belleza donde otros solo ven rutina.

body.body:
As always, an extraordinary analysis, thank you.

First of all, I wanted to point out that LeoThreads is the short-form content feature of InLeo (the app), which also publishes to the blog.

When I started reading and you mentioned that we would be surprised, I thought to myself, \

and boy, was I wrong! 🤣

It catches my attention that rewards don't carry that much influence. It would be interesting to analyze that topic further, for example, the migration from one dapp to another due to the votes they distribute.

In that sense, the PeakD data surprised me, since they never vote for individual users, but rather for project curation reports. On the other hand, InLeo is the one that votes with higher amounts, but Ecency is the one that votes for the highest number of users. I know many users switch dapps looking for those votes, even publishing through them while continuing to interact on PeakD or Hive Blog.

Liketu used to vote quite a bit and had a good amount of HP, but they did a power down. It would be great to know if that power down led to a decrease in retention, marking the beginning of abandonment or migration toward others.


![imagen.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/danielvehe/Eos578ytEu72QVrpoUdBN8WujWNTR2TCqNcg5uU3QJXHa9HJfr3DWWidGC93b7Y76CJ.png)



![imagen.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/danielvehe/23xexRx7cisjvEmPxkx9RHyxhr67cjhdxyoGNN2z3RTzzfd7ffsGgkeZqMk5sUC6LWbL5.png)



![imagen.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/danielvehe/23xVY7gV4TThbQGFADt3CYeM7KCrbkySAiV2eWVTbL8yXw34aca86q9w2QFVb5k9sDc8Y.png)



![imagen.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/danielvehe/EoySrRA1jCDtVSjYVpC5uzoSVQzLS2KvkUFYFLC5bcLebiTMVaTGwiLKwMzxY92njui.png)
[Sourse](https://peakd.com/hive-189306/@rutablockchain/how-projects-are-voted-on-4abdbdbac17f8)

There should definitely be a second part to this analysis. For instance, dapp churn, and how the migration between one and another looks. We have done onboarding across several dapps and have switched depending on the circumstances. Just as we change dapps during onboarding, the users themselves keep changing as well.

Regarding the InLeo case, it would also be interesting to check if the highest wave of churn happened right after their DHF-funded adoption campaign. Beyond the allegations made by some regarding the use of bots, it could be useful to know if massive onboarding inherently generates a high rate of churn. I believe we should aim for more massive onboarding but while maintaining a close, community-driven approach. It is a massive challenge.

I imagine the next analysis would shift toward community onboarding, rather than the dapps themselves. In the meantime, I am going to prepare our own data for Hive Run.

Night atmosphere in Ruteng City, Flores — specifically around Motang Rua, one of the busiest and most familiar areas in the heart of the city.

This video captures the simple but peaceful feeling of Ruteng at night:
the city lights,
cool mountain air,
quiet roads,
and the calm atmosphere that makes this small town feel special.

Ruteng may not be as crowded as big cities, but that is exactly where its beauty lives.

Located in the highlands of Flores, Ruteng is surrounded by green mountains and fresh air, creating a relaxing environment both day and night. Motang Rua itself is one of the central points of activity in the city, where local life, transportation, food spots, and everyday moments come together naturally.

For travelers visiting Flores, Ruteng is more than just a transit city.
It is a place to slow down, breathe, and experience the authentic atmosphere of Manggarai culture.

Sometimes the beauty of a place is not found in luxury…
but in the peaceful feeling it gives to people who experience it.

body.title: ​El otoño ha llegado y mi gatita Manchita ha reclamado su trono
body.body:
![1000283372.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alina97/23xeg3NiE4TANvQUu3TB87qgyNKwDZDbtFhAnfTCnN3GqU3fsMZRhNZPCfLkF9m8FZviy.jpg)


# ¡Hola, querida comunidad de Hive!

Espero que estén teniendo una excelente semana. Hoy paso por aquí para compartirles un poquito de mi día a día y, sobre todo, para derretirles el corazón con la reina de la casa: mi adorada gatita Manchita.

![1000282000.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alina97/23tkhySriCTE8ZJt5V6vZPPHaisDd23NJ5E4BPVtMZsw1wZ64NtXzXAEVK9W3yq3EYmPZ.jpg)

​Quienes tienen mascotas saben que ellas son el termómetro perfecto del hogar. Aquí, el otoño ya se empieza a sentir con fuerza y los días frescos nos invitan a buscar el calor del hogar. Pero si hay alguien que se toma muy en serio lo de \

, esa es Manchita. Últimamente ha estado sintiendo bastante frío, y su instinto felino la ha llevado a activar su superpoder favorito: encontrar el lugar más suave, cálido y cómodo de toda la casa. ¿Y cuál creen que es? Exacto, ¡mi cama!

![1000281997.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alina97/23u5vWB7udtCUY6qWbwMAKuL9NXwm7qG5VKD2Cbe9tSjpK5wrEyQLn1X5zzBPmX2Cf3KS.jpg)

​Buscando el calorcito hogareño
​En la primera imagen que capturé, la pueden verla en su máximo esplendor de relajación. Se acomodó justo encima de una de las mantas más abrigadas que tenemos. Me encanta cómo cruza sus patitas delanteras con tanta elegancia, como si supiera que la cama le pertenece por derecho propio. Con sus ojitos cerrados y esa tranquilidad que transmite, es imposible tener el corazón frío al verla. Es increíble cómo un ser tan pequeño puede adueñarse de un espacio tan grande y hacernos sentir tanta paz.

![1000281999.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alina97/23tbJmkahNDnvW2nuaprAJqzBB6qBYPSDNb37WYUDhRQQEWg248W7vVV83cUDBVMbpE2r.jpg)

​Insertar aquí el archivo 1000281997.jpg
​Mimos y consentimiento mutuo
​Los gatos tienen esa fama de ser independientes, pero cuando el frío aprieta, se vuelven los seres más mimosos del planeta. A Manchita no solo le gusta dormir entre cobijas, sino que también busca el calor humano constantemente. 

En las fotos logramos capturar uno de esos momentos mágicos donde se deja consentir por completo. Sostener su carita entre las manos y ver su expresión de absoluta confianza y felicidad es una de las recompensas más lindas de compartir la vida con un felino. En momentos así, el frío del exterior simplemente desaparece.

![1000281998.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alina97/23u5bKe23c4LtrMJAQbmaNzgfq2BzkcSEUij6oyU9q4qibDt4yvTXATamwaTe88AyTEzw.jpg)

​Para mí, estos pequeños instantes son los que hacen que el hogar se sienta verdaderamente como un refugio. El otoño tiene su encanto, pero tener una compañera peludita roncando a los pies de la cama (o justo en medio de ella) lo hace mil veces mejor.

​¿Y a ustedes? ¿Sus mascotas también se vuelven extra cariñosas y friolentas durante esta época del año? ¿Cuál es el lugar favorito de sus consentidos para dormir? ¡Me encantaría leer sus historias y consejos en los comentarios!

​¡Gracias por leer y por acompañarme a presumir a mi hermosa Manchita! Nos leemos en el próximo post. ¡Un abrazo!



# English


![1000273764.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alina97/23tkmzG4DhAF8NrRod1UWa7ZjRsgdGN8ppmJvR7tmxwaN83JcCuaXK2nSxBdPZkgKAp5w.jpg)


​Hello, dear Hive community! I hope you are all having an excellent week. Today I'm stopping by to share a little bit of my daily life and, above all, to melt your hearts with the queen of the house: my beloved kitty, Manchita.

​Those who have pets know that they are the perfect thermometer for the home. Here, autumn is already starting to be felt with strength, and the chilly days invite us to seek the warmth of home. But if there is anyone who takes the concept of \

very seriously, it's Manchita. Lately, she has been feeling quite cold, and her feline instinct has led her to activate her favorite superpower: finding the softest, warmest, and most comfortable spot in the entire house. And which one do you think it is? Exactly, my bed!

​Looking for Cozy Warmth
​In the first image I captured, you can see her in her ultimate state of relaxation. She settled right on top of one of the warmest blankets we have. I love how she crosses her front paws with such elegance, as if she knows the bed belongs to her by right. With her eyes closed and that tranquility she transmits, it's impossible to have a cold heart when looking at her. It's incredible how such a small being can take over such a large space and make us feel so much peace.
​

​Pampering and Mutual Affection
​Cats have a reputation for being independent, but when the cold weather sets in, they become the most affectionate beings on the planet. Manchita doesn't just like to sleep among the blankets; she also constantly seeks out human warmth. 

In the photo, we managed to capture one of those magical moments where she lets herself be completely pampered. Holding her little face between my hands and seeing her expression of absolute trust and happiness is one of the most beautiful rewards of sharing life with a feline. In moments like this, the cold outside simply disappears.

​
​For me, these small moments are what make a home truly feel like a refuge. Autumn has its charm, but having a furry companion purring at the foot of the bed (or right in the middle of it) makes it a thousand times better.
​What about you? Do your pets also get extra affectionate and sensitive to the cold during this time of the year?
 Where is your spoiled one's favorite place to sleep? 

I would love to read your stories and tips in the comments!
​Thank you for reading and for joining me in showing off my beautiful Manchita! See you in the next post. Hugs!

body.title: ‎Potential Means Nothing Without Execution ‎
body.body:
‎Hi Hive,
‎
‎One of the hardest truths I have come to accept is that nobody actually cares about your potential. The world only responds to results.

https://img.leopedia.io/DQmQrMe8YwuX819GURegdjMXEY17JNuQuGi979DfngD4CJs/geralt-lightbulb-3704027_1920.jpg 
‎
‎[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/lightbulb-idea-think-training-3704027/)
‎
‎People might admire your dreams for a moment. They might praise your ideas, your talent, or the vision you carry in your head. But admiration quickly fades when there is no action behind it. Potential without execution is just possibility left untouched.
‎
‎We all know people with brilliant ideas. People who constantly talk about the business they want to start, the book they want to write, the skills they want to learn, or the life they want to build. But the sad reality is that dreaming has become more easier than doing. Planning feels productive, but plans alone actually change nothing.
‎
‎Execution is what separates wishful thinking from real progress.
‎You can have the biggest vision in the room, but if you lack consistency, discipline, and the willingness to act even when you don’t feel motivated, your potential will surely remain invisible. 
‎
‎The world doesn’t reward intentions. But it rewards effort repeated over time.
‎I have came to realized that success is rarely about who is the most gifted. A lot of talented people stay stuck because they never move beyond ideas. Meanwhile, average people who show up daily, gradually improve, stay committed and often end up achieving far more.
‎
‎And that's what totally changed my mindset. I stopped being overly obsessed with perfection and started focusing more on action. Small steps, daily work, and consistency over excitement. Because execution builds confidence. Execution is what creates opportunities. And execution turns dreams into evidence.
‎
‎At the end of the day, nobody can clap for what you could have been. They only see what you built, what you finished, and what impact you really made.
‎So dream big, absolutely. Think boldly. Make ambitious plans. But never let your ideas live only in your head. But instead..
‎
‎Move.
‎Start before you feel ready.
‎Stay consistent when motivation disappears.
‎Because potential may open the door, but execution is what keeps it open.
‎
‎
‎![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYaWnApEziAtLL5Zwv3ZNbDjRfSfG6h5njgTrpyasnE6y/1775569275821.png)
‎
