body.title: Playa Puerto Abajo es un pequeño regalo en medio del caos[ESP-ENG]
body.body:
> Hola mi querida comunidad de @hivemargarita, espero que hoy estén todos bien y disfrutando de su maravilloso fin de semana. Quería compartirles de un día que viví está semana pasada, algo diferente a lo habitual jajaja yo me río porque de verdad nosotros los venezolanos hemos pasado por tanto que ya nada nos sorprende. Como todos sabemos, el tema de la gasolina en Venezuela sigue siendo complicado, pero en mi zona aún contamos con una estación subsidiada donde el costo es un poco más accesible. Aunque no es una experiencia agradable, esta vez al menos pude registrarme en un link que me asignó número y hora, lo cual hace todo un poquito más organizado y mucho menos agotador ya que generalmente para surtir combustible hay que hacer largas calas que te llevan hasta a dormir ahí. Pero como nada es perfecto, pues ese día la gandola llegó casi a las 2:00pm y yo tenía asignado el número 67 y la hora es 7:30am. Reorganizaron todo y hubo que poner gasolina por orden de llegada ya no por número y tocó hacer una cola en medio del sol, así que mientras esperaba mi turno y rodaba el carro, decidí mirar un rato a la orilla de Playa Puerto Abajo. Esa playita que yo llamo “la playa del pueblo”, donde siempre vemos a la gente del municipio los domingos compartiendo, cocinando, disfrutando, es pequeña, sencilla, de pescadores, pero tiene su encanto especial. Ese día estaba un poco sucia, pero el clima estaba perfecto y el mar tenía un azul tan bonito que te hace olvidar por un momento las preocupaciones. Escuchar las olas y ver ese horizonte infinito fue un regalo inesperado en medio de la espera. Por eso quise traerles estas foticos, para que también puedan disfrutar un poquito de ese paisaje tan nuestro. Gracias por pasar por mi post, por el apoyo y por ser parte de esta comunidad tan especial. Les envío saludos y muchas Bendiciones. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRsPDEA52MEU3VbkNsi5MHo3bGCbCyzhpWLdzwMJHVzXk/separadores_28.png)
**ENGLISH**
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRsPDEA52MEU3VbkNsi5MHo3bGCbCyzhpWLdzwMJHVzXk/separadores_28.png)
Hello, my dear @hivemargarita community. I hope you’re all doing well today and enjoying your wonderful weekend. I wanted to share with you an experience I had last week—something a little different from the usual, hahaha; I laugh because, honestly, we Venezuelans have been through so much that nothing surprises us anymore. As we all know, the gasoline situation in Venezuela remains complicated, but in my area we still have a subsidized gas station where the price is a bit more affordable. Although it’s not a pleasant experience, this time at least I was able to sign up on a link that assigned me a number and a time, which makes everything a little more organized and much less exhausting, since normally to fill up you have to stand in long lines that even make you sleep there. But since nothing is perfect, that day the truck arrived around 2:00 p.m., and I had been assigned number 67 with a time slot of 7:30 a.m. They reorganized everything, and we had to refuel on a first-come, first-served basis, no longer by number, so I had to wait in line under the sun. While I was waiting for my turn and driving around in circles, I decided to take a quick look at the shore of Puerto Abajo Beach. That little beach I call “the town beach,” where we always see the locals on Sundays socializing, cooking, and enjoying themselves, is small, simple, and a fishermen’s spot, but it has its own special charm. It was a bit cloudy that day, but the weather was perfect, and the sea was such a beautiful blue that it made you forget your worries for a moment. Listening to the waves and gazing at that endless horizon was an unexpected gift in the midst of the wait. That’s why I wanted to share these photos with you, so you too can enjoy a little bit of this landscape that’s so dear to us. Thank you for stopping by my post, for your support, and for being part of this very special community. Warm regards and many blessings. body.title: 🔥 ¡LA ARMADA CUBANA EN MLB! Crónica y Análisis de una Semana de Puro Fuego (17 al 23 de Mayo, 2026)
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWWXZHFs3hde8ZnU6xBmTjXR9tcUumzFAusYk9AE9gR65/img_20260418_174512_064.jpg)

¡Saludos, comunidad de **Ecency** y apasionados de las costuras! Entramos de lleno a la recta final de mayo en esta electrizante temporada 2026 de las Grandes Ligas, y la constante no cambia: el sabor, la potencia y el guaguancó de los peloteros cubanos siguen dictando sentencia en el mejor béisbol del mundo.

Esta semana que sopesamos (desde el domingo 17 hasta el sábado 23 de mayo) nos ha dejado postales de puro dominio y ajustes de cuentas con la bola. Saquen su café, pónganse cómodos y analicemos cómo rindieron nuestros embajadores en el Big Show.

---

## 🏆 El MVP de la Semana: Yandy Díaz (Tampa Bay Rays)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXn9G2twgePU4gZkTSL6P5wZoCRJQi4XA6TffGAhbuubm/img_20260510_085000_982.jpg)
Miren que el término \

se inventó para describir a este señor. Mientras otros buscan el cuadrangular de 450 pies de forma desesperada, **Yandy Díaz** se dedica a dar una clínica diaria de cómo masticar turnos al bate y destrozar el pitcheo rival con líneas salvajes.

* **Promedio al bate:** El de Remedios cerró la jornada del sábado exhibiendo un robusto **.311** de average global en la campaña.
* **Poder y Disciplina:** En la serie contra los Yankees demostró que su habilidad para embasarse es oro en polvo. No le regala nada a los lanzadores y sigue siendo el motor térmico en la parte alta del lineup de Tampa Bay. Su OPS roza la élite gracias a esa mirada de halcón en el plato. ¡Sencillamente impecable!

---

## 🚀 Reporte Ofensivo: El Élite y el Poder de Resistencia

### Yordan Álvarez (Houston Astros)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSxYr9vFJ84wZZcwKCi58YQKJkAWn7UMmjW8CPPyRhUvU/img_20260510_084957_618.jpg)
El \

ha tenido una semana de esas donde los mánagers contrarios prefieren darle la base por bolas antes de que les desfigure la pelota. Aunque el pitcheo de los Mellizos de Minnesota y los Cachorros de Chicago lo llevó con extremo cuidado (recetándole varios pasaportes, incluyendo un juego de dos boletos el 22 de mayo), Yordan se mantiene en la estratosfera:

* **Estadísticas globales acumuladas al 23 de mayo:** Suma **15 cuadrangulares** y **31 carreras impulsadas**, luciendo un imponente promedio de **.303** y un **OPS astronómico de 1.017**. Cuando conecta, el sonido del bate avisa que la bola va directo a las gradas.

### Adolis García (Philadelphia Phillies)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXsULQJRqzSqTayq9wGY4YPWA6kuFc5FYz6a73tPZqRJn/img_20260510_084948_494.jpg)
\

, ahora defendiendo la causa en la Ciudad del Amor Fraternal tras un invierno de movimientos, está viviendo una campaña de altibajos en su promedio (**.201** al corte del sábado), pero su peligro es latente. Esta semana remolcó carrera clave frente a Cleveland; sabemos que Adolis es un bateador de rachas y que, en cualquier parpadeo del lanzador, te voltea el marcador con su agresividad característica.

---

## 🎯 El Candado de la Loma: Pitcheo de Élite

No todo es madera y conexiones de largo metraje. Desde el montículo, el brazo de la isla sigue imponiendo respeto en los innings de máxima presión.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVPmAqX5shrzfn83xyW89SZb42GkTjkKtvg94wyGZsZvL/img_20260510_085004_980.jpg)
* **Raisel Iglesias:** Sigue intocable en el noveno inning, hilvanando rescates con una frialdad matemática. Su efectividad se mantiene en mínimos históricos esta temporada gracias a un cambio de velocidad que rompe el suelo.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWX965166npTzK9C9ziCyWeMK8uNNQsoyesaV8YkFwDCz/img_20260510_084951_231.jpg)
* **Aroldis Chapman:** \

continúa desafiando las leyes del tiempo en este 2026. Aunque el conteo de boletos a veces nos pone a sufrir, la velocidad de su recta sigue congelando a los bateadores en momentos de apremio en el bullpen.

---

## 💬 Conclusión y Debate en Ecency

La campaña de MLB 2026 avanza a un ritmo vertiginoso y la representación cubana no hace más que afianzarse en los lideratos individuales. Tenemos a un Yandy Díaz que es una máquina de batear hits y a un Yordan Álvarez que compite de tú a tú por el liderato de cuadrangulares de la liga.

Ahora quiero leerlos a ustedes abajo en la sección de comentarios: **¿Creen que Yandy Díaz logrará mantener ese average sobre .310 durante todo el verano? ¿Logrará Yordan Álvarez sobrepasar la barrera de los 45 jonrones este año con los Astros?**

¡Suelta tu análisis, vota y hagamos comunidad! Nos leemos en el próximo reporte premium. 👇

body.body:
Today we have for you guitar picks from 

Ringo Starr and the All-Star band! 

![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/94a5440b-7a31-4523-b89d-f5337730466f.jpg)

---

https://youtu.be/AufMa3dGhHI?si=vpN_8RqqF4yIJITs

---

Here's a look at the front and the back of these guitar picks 

![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/d6cca699-76db-4035-aaf9-9af40eef91ee.jpg)

---

![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/13b278c0-f0a9-4fc6-8c6e-5069248e1611.jpg)

---

Ringo Starr & His All-Starr Band is a legendary, rotating supergroup formed in 1989 that beautifully celebrates rock-and-roll camaraderie. Instead of a traditional solo act, the beloved Beatles drummer gathers a handpicked lineup of iconic musicians from various legendary bands—such as members of Toto, Journey, Santana, and Men at Work. The band's unique performance concept operates on a simple, crowd-pleasing rule: \

meaning Ringo shares the spotlight equally. Throughout their high-energy concerts, Ringo performs his classic Beatles and solo hits, interspersed with the band members taking turns leading the crowd through their own massive, chart-topping anthems. It is a brilliant, feel-good celebration of rock history that has kept audiences dancing for over three decades.

---
---

This collection is a remarkable physical record of rock history, featuring a diverse array of guitar picks gathered from some of the most legendary North American tours. Each piece represents a specific moment in time, coming directly from the hands of the most influential touring bands of the last 20 to 40 years. From the thrash metal precision of Megadeth to the grunge-era icons like Eddie Vedder, these picks are more than just gear—they are tangible artifacts from the high-energy arenas and stadiums that defined a generation of music.
The significance of these picks lies in their connection to the peak of live performance culture across the continent. Over the past four decades, touring reached a massive scale, and these picks were used by artists who headlined the most iconic festivals and venues in the world. Whether it's a specialty \

design or a classic tour-stamped plectrum, having items from bands that shaped the sound of the 80s, 90s, and 2000s makes this a curated chronicle of modern rock’s touring legac. I'm putting this guitar pic together. Alphabetical order over the next few weeks and months. --- ---
_This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). Check out the original version [here on actifit.io](https://actifit.io/@dylanhobalart/actifit-dylanhobalart-20260524t131730369z)_

Bidden by @deirdyweirdy to give you my two cents on how to recover, here is what I would try for myself if I presented with your conditions. 

If you can get to someplace that sells homeopathic remedies (most health foods stores do), try **Chelidonium** in the lowest potency they have, ideally 6c. Take it three times a day until you start to feel some relief in regards to pneumonia, then reduce to 1 or 2 times a day. 

For the apparent food poisoning, **Arsenicum** is my first thought to help with the vomiting, ideally 30c potency. Take it whenever you feel the nausea coming on, then every 10 to 15 minutes for an hour. If that doesn't help at all, move to **Ipecac** every 10 to 15 minutes for an hour, in 30c. A third choice would be Nux vomica, 200c, same administration. 

All of these remedies are commonly sold in health food stores. If you don't have one of those nearby, try Walgreens or some other large pharmacy, look for combination/formula remedies that seem to be for your conditions, and follow the directions on the package. 

Try sipping very hot water to see if that gives you any relief. Gently sniffing peppermint oil can help with nausea. 

For continued recovery for your lungs, get some Kali carbonicum 200c and take it twice a day for a couple weeks. this one might be more difficult to find. 

You can order all of these from [Boiron](https://www.boironusa.com/). It will be easiest to just call them to order, rather than trying to find all these on their website, and they might give you more guidance. But I hope you can find at least some of these nearby so you don't have to wait for your order to arrive.

body.title: Harvest Day in the Palm Oil Plantation
body.body:
Hello Hive friends and everyone in the ASEAN Hive community.
Today I want to share some moments from our activities in the palm oil plantation area. This was a busy and tiring day because we were loading and collecting fresh palm fruit bunches before sending them to the factory.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQM4jnNYJ7ZKQ5T7jjpp4inAT3N95SuDqu5waxpddUhMP/1779628381387.jpg)

The weather was quite hot, but the work still had to continue. Since morning, we prepared the truck and gathered the palm fruit that had already been harvested. The piles of fresh fruit bunches looked very satisfying because they showed the results of hard work from the plantation workers.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbu8sXoY2Atk6595y5V2Tu4n4UjvzW7P9esbp1aU1N2xa/1779628420152.jpg)

One of the hardest parts of this job is lifting the heavy palm fruit bunches into the truck. Each bunch is very heavy and full of sharp thorns, so we must work carefully. Even though the work is exhausting, we are already used to this daily activity because this is part of our livelihood.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmP6b9BsF5g83GpDdnB8fBs9MtRenTYdwgWvxW5GSrEET3/1779628464115.jpg)

I also took a few photos while working today. Behind me, you can see the beautiful scenery of palm trees surrounding the village area. Life in the countryside is simple, but there is a special feeling when working together with friends and neighbors.
The yellow truck in the photos was used to transport the harvest to the palm oil mill. After all the fruit was loaded, the truck would continue its journey to deliver the fresh palm fruit for processing.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRqe7oRxa7RtvTnd3pFhAzTeZMMykdxRT9613pJsp3Aed/1779628518302.jpg)

The yellow truck in the photos was used to transport the harvest to the palm oil mill. After all the fruit was loaded, the truck would continue its journey to deliver the fresh palm fruit for processing.
Working in the plantation teaches us many things about patience, responsibility, and teamwork. Every harvest day is not only about work but also about appreciating the effort behind every result we achieve.
Thank you for visiting my post.
I hope you enjoy seeing a small part of our daily life in the plantation.

Have a great day everyone 😊

body.title: Propagation of my Nepenthes (Monkey jars) carnivorous pitcherplants
body.body:
Two years ago I visited the garden center on my birthday with my kids. They wanted to buy me a plant since they know I really like plants. When we were there I spotted a unique and intriguing plant; a Nepenthes pitcher plant. That just had to be my birthday present.
Now, 2 years later, my plant is doing really well. I have multiplied it in several ways and all offspring is seemingly doing very ![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)well.

![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)

# Propagation
After the first year I noticed a small new plant started growing next to the original one. The mother plant itself already consisted of three strong growth stems, so the plant was growing a bit too big for its pot. 
So I separated two main stems from the third and 'migrated' the new shoot with the third stem into an individual pot. I suddenly had two pithcer plants and both plants are healthy and actively producing pitchers.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23w2sDB6dcx2CTQyU21wYNzivGsJXgkgYaEWxhwN9V2LiRGm9utBvZZnCjMsDm8CY2MXJ.png)
The second plant.

![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)

# Pitcher development
This is the coolest part of this plant. Every year they form quite large pitchers. 
One of the plants has already formed a large pitcher this year. As you can see on the photo, the lid is still closed. You can't really tell by the photo, but there is liquid inside. This liquid contains digestive enzymes that help break down insects that get trapped in the plant. The plant absorbs the nutrient and uses it to grow.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23wgS4qrLheWRCCAivQfyL89j4hEDJS6LU9EoNBb2N3bJuu3pQESBGHB8aRyLm7fb8y9J.png)

The other plant is a bit behind, but also forming pitchers now. They are a bit smaller, but they will get there eventually.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23wqthWPmTMZ3Hd8hFsCfyqXn3RXvtp26oKdMv3ocTq5y5GpWNE9gMsGQqgx2dNQ9xZd2.png)


At the starting stage of forming pitchers they look very dry. But they aren't dead; they still develop and they often do turn out to become real pitchers.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23tmQN2auFtJgD1BTYGgY2ZyGoFFdjwfRdgdoLg3DsNWBnBcnknxJfQERuMVyTwDsFKdq.png)

![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)

# Propagation attempts
One of the stems of 'the mother plant' had become a bit too long in my opinion, so I decided to cut it back.
I've placed the removed stem in placed in sphagnum moss to see if it would root. After a few weeks it still looks pretty healthy to me. I don't know if it is forming roots yet, but the fact that it still looks healthy and green is a good indicator I think. For now I'll leave it and wait.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23uQyCB2sMQzPYd3PfSQkghksaAvBsZ5rb4xW4C1ZS2baiqned4aag2pTvjxYjiTf6UyF.png)


Today I noticed a new side shoot has started to develop in the stem I cut back. This shows it is a really strong plant. 

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23ynWkPkEfo5jDhPcNBzk9RXpbVi6GBLoJ8sEPjymsmjqv6jLb1ZJYTRAnQmgAZqCezdK.png)

I also noticed another new Nepenthes plant had popped up next to the mother plant, just like it did last year. It shows how easily this species can produce new growth. I do have to give away some for adoption maybe since I might get a bit too much pitcher plants this way 😂 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23z7E4R4UBbY6dRTgwMt1SoUEeyevP8mUJ7S9rkm4w4bTPJL7FYjeGdRPkErvnA3DX9f7.png)


![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)

# Caring
I often get questions on Hive whenever I post about this plant, especially about how it is cared for (@florian-glechner).
Nepenthes are tropical plants. They prefer a constant temperature around 20 to 30°C and a high humidity. They don't like tap water, so I use rainwater instead.
I keep them indoors, placed in a bright window where they get plenty of light. I also regularly mist them with a plant sprayer to keep the humidity a bit high.
Under these conditions they have been growing steadily for two years and they look healthy and they have been producing new pitchers and shoots every year.

![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)

Thanks for reading. Feel free to share your own experiences with carnivorous plants or propagation on Hive.



![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23tbRPyFGzXzKq4VRcfmTQNvhRdFZuW4RStJLr9oXfgFtXwgvohVK1n7iUoW318ZN1yrp.png)


Before supporting an account, it can be useful to take a closer look at its activity and behavior.
I recently built the **[Hive Account Health Dashboard](https://friendlymoose5717.github.io/hive-dashboard/)** to make that easier.

The dashboard gives quick insight into several account statistics that may help when deciding whether or not to support an account.
Feel free to test it yourself and let me know what you think.
![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)

body.title: A stroll down The Alacran Alley (Eng/Esp)
body.body:
>


Today’s tour takes us to an iconic spot in the city known as Callejon The Alacran, where it feels as though time has stood still. Everything here still retains a distinctive colonial atmosphere. Although I’ve walked through here many times—and have even written about it—every time I pass by, I experience new and pleasant sensations.

<center>
![1000117045.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23vsLSub4jaCPhg5vj7uvWGUqmEW9hDbL59tbgkRn32eny2rrwGg5djdFr5AVNZmYb211.jpg)
</center>

I entered this area via Comercio Street and immediately noticed the decorations hanging overhead—small light bulbs and artificial butterflies that have been there since Cumana’s anniversary celebration. Meanwhile, fresh flowers stand out in the planters lining both sides of the sidewalks.


<center>
![1000117038.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/242Y9hKT659EzSJ2JhRu2SnDEsib2P7Gf9WaMsRZ2KEfE9QzHdVqVDFzSsBM6SQoBUFQr.jpg)
</center>


This alleyway serves as a passageway to the city’s historic district; from the cross street, you can see the Church of Santa Ines, whose pastel colors make it stand out against the vast expanse of blue. This very angle has been depicted in countless paintings and is the most frequently reproduced by local artists.


<center>
![1000117033.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23w2kgPvA7AX7usUBEyaHKCx6ysSkAHt2cse4ZsRHUcbPeLCdqu9piZMzck6BbEeNZ7g6.jpg)
</center>

As I mentioned, all the facades retain their original design, and although everything seems arranged like the set of a play, these homes are inhabited; you can see pets wandering about, and in this case, I could hear music. 


<center>
![1000117028.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23yd45HLYrTwvz7syWi2491g2dsskQA5LwbhQCpgRggxn8mpjm9znnrtiyPcgzc8rSFX8.jpg)
</center>

I love colorful flowers; here, the trinitaria stands out like a queen, beautifying everything around it. The red, fuchsia, and orange hues stand out against the green contrast of the leaves. Another very beautiful plant I noticed is called the \

which grows in hanging clusters and is distinguished by its deep purple color.
![1000117053.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23w2mFY318WUp9DGL4AmJuBxkuXP4KjsaeUWktoeQ6NBkw1n4aWwHQBR2L4L7u3a2n34B.jpg)
I enjoy passing through here; it transports me to another era, like a gentleman of yesteryear strolling through neat streets, in the midst of a colorful dream where the vicissitudes of modernity have not yet caught up with me. *** ***
## Versión en Español

> El recorrido de hoy nos lleva por un lugar emblemático de la ciudad, el cual se conoce como Callejón El Alacrán, donde parece que el tiempo se detuvo. Y es que todo lo que existe en este lugar todavía conserva un distintivo aire colonial. Aunque ya he transitado por aquí en varias ocasiones, incluso he escrito sobre ello, cada vez que pasó por acá percibo nuevas y gratas sensaciones.
![1000117045.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23vsLSub4jaCPhg5vj7uvWGUqmEW9hDbL59tbgkRn32eny2rrwGg5djdFr5AVNZmYb211.jpg)
Accedí a este lugar por la calle Comercio y de inmediato concentré la mirada en la ornamentación presente en la zona superior, pequeños bombillos y mariposas artificiales aún están alli desde la celebración del aniversario de Cumaná. Por otra parte, las flores naturales se destacan en las jardineras ubicadas a ambos lados de las aceras.
![1000117038.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/242Y9hKT659EzSJ2JhRu2SnDEsib2P7Gf9WaMsRZ2KEfE9QzHdVqVDFzSsBM6SQoBUFQr.jpg)
Este callejón es una vía para comunicarse con el Casco Histórico de la ciudad, desde la transversal se puede observar la iglesia Santa Inés, sus colores pasteles la hacen llamativa ante la inmensidad de lo azul. Justamente este ángulo ha sido reproducido en innumerables pinturas, siendo el más replicado entre los artistas locales.
![1000117033.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23w2kgPvA7AX7usUBEyaHKCx6ysSkAHt2cse4ZsRHUcbPeLCdqu9piZMzck6BbEeNZ7g6.jpg)
Como indiqué, todas las fachadas mantienen su diseño antiguo y aunque todo parezca dispuesto como escenografía de una obra de teatro, estas viviendas están habitadas, se pueden observar animales domésticos deambulando y, en este caso, pude escuchar música.
![1000117028.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23yd45HLYrTwvz7syWi2491g2dsskQA5LwbhQCpgRggxn8mpjm9znnrtiyPcgzc8rSFX8.jpg)
Las coloridas flores me encantan, acá la trinitaria se presenta como la reina, embelleciendo todo lo que está a su alrededor. Los colores rojo, fucsia y naranja sobresalen ante el contraste verde proveniente de las hojas. Otra planta muy hermosa que pude distinguir se llama Flor de cielo, la cual crece en racimos colgantes y se distinguen por su color morado intenso.
![1000117053.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23w2mFY318WUp9DGL4AmJuBxkuXP4KjsaeUWktoeQ6NBkw1n4aWwHQBR2L4L7u3a2n34B.jpg)
Disfruto pasar por acá, me traslada a otra época, como un caballero de antaño paseando por unas calles pulcras, en medio de un sueño colorido donde los avatares de la modernidad aún no me alcanzan.   *** *** ✓Photos from my personal gallery, edited with Fotocollage. ✓Text translated with DeepL.

body.body:
![IMG_20260524_200634.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc7jbrc1RyNALZHtmfQRx3qta4nSRrRjFDHZq244Ab1bF/IMG_20260524_200634.jpg)

### Pop Music Landscape
Pop music was highly popular in the 1990s, though the first half of the decade was dominated by grunge from the likes of Nirvana and Pearl Jam. Rock music was incredibly popular then, dance music was gaining traction, and hip-hop was rising on the music charts.
During the second half of the 1990s, the pop music scene shifted as radio and music channels began to feature more radio-friendly tracks. The Spice Girls became a global phenomenon and are often credited for this shift; their song \
became a global smash alongside their first two albums, Spice and Spiceworld. Hanson is also frequently mentioned for hitting the airwaves with \
and selling millions of copies of their mainstream debut, Middle of Nowhere. Aqua also dominated pop radio with their hit \

which was known for its cartoonish style and music video.
Boy bands such as the Backstreet Boys, Boyzone, and *NSYNC also made a huge contribution to the late-1990s pop scene.

### Sunday
I woke up early because I heard my dog barking. Probably, there's a cat bullying him. I even heard him cried a little, so I headed downstairs to stop the cat. Also, I had let my dog release the wastes from his body, and put him back to his place, and prepared our breakfast. We attended our weekend meeting in sign language too. 

### Feels Like Paradise 
It feels like paradise as we strolled around Mount Olis. The beauty, serenity, and the climate is perfect enough that makes this place worth visiting.

Hi there,

I got a 404 page for the sitemap 😁.

Can I check what happens with posts published through peakd.com:

> Fetched as a crawler with no JavaScript, some Hive frontends are client-side rendered - the initial HTML is a near-empty application shell with the article body absent until scripts execute - while Ecency server-renders the full article in the initial response. This isn't a criticism; client-side rendering is a legitimate architecture with its own benefits. But it has a concrete SEO consequence: when Google chooses among duplicate copies, it favors the version it can parse immediately. [(Source)](https://peakd.com/hive-139531/@ecency/how-ecency-is-approaching-seo)

Is the full article rendered in the initial response?

body.title: #Monomad Challenge // A Nighttime Stroll / Un Paseo Nocturno
body.body: > Nighttime has always been one of my favorite times of day, since when the sun goes down, temperatures drop, the pace of life changes, and energies flow differently. That’s how these walks become idyllic moments, where it feels as though we’re reconnecting with ourselves, always feeling nature, yet with the certainty that we’re walking through spaces shaped by human hands.

> La noche siempre ha sido uno de mis momentos favoritos, puesto que cuando cae el sol las temperaturas bajan, el ritmo de vida cambia y las energías fluyen de manera distinta. Es así como estos paseos se convierten en momentos idílicos, en donde pareciera que nos estamos reencontrando con nosotros mismos, siempre sintiendo la naturaleza, pero con la convicción de que estamos caminando por espacios domados por el hombre.
![1-IMG_20260423_172839 (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yorgar/23zGW45XNZ9hp9hAf3iLzVX6ftNEr2dS275aAnQr7rDAV6FbQBr3YahCA8TJkXNVn5RCh.jpg) ![1-IMG_20260423_172839 (2).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yorgar/Eo8SHb2fEC39DePCnj4NaH4om4o7iXJHGfgy4nfeHtpLKD5PMqh7mGBREvq8wmm7SaC.jpg) ![1-IMG_20260423_172839 (3).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yorgar/242Nj2nVJTDBS5ZnDsHhDdLg4jPvoztAToTQkVUCiSV1AMZAPpATbXszJvyHVGNVLLkfc.jpg)

> High in the mountains of Caracas, there is a place where we can literally touch the sky. Here, towering trees stand amidst a dense mist, shops buzz with the rhythm of tourism, and the city’s hustle and bustle seems to fade into the background. It is along these trails that I captured images that strike me as profound—where we can observe a perfect coexistence and, at the same time, discover fascinating stories.

> Sobre las montañas de Caracas existe un lugar en donde literalmente podemos tocar el cielo. Acá los grandes árboles se discurren entre una densa neblina, los locales comerciales vibran al ritmo del turismo y el bullicio de la ciudad parece quedar en el olvido. Es sobre estos senderos en donde capturé imágenes que me parecen profundas, en donde podemos observar una coexistencia perfecta y en donde al mismo tiempo descubrimos historias interesantes.
![IMG_20260423_171645.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yorgar/23zRtoNSdfYUXQFaLsUV7ZXoaJcsK2wBReN7cgc2eR8H4C8iXEKbNa2iC9jtBrRDoPRSA.jpg) ![IMG_20260423_172747.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yorgar/EogPD7JR5RC1gTXCVtdburSzrrzt9qs78qp9MVZmYakRetmsZmMAEAvgKZ1W1Z1CyFZ.jpg) ![IMG_20260423_172830.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yorgar/242Y7X6TKU7NMGjjAJx45ap8eT7PFgsi84qefWnjiFdtwPvCqmJW7fje1yYjWkEYtPEDT.jpg)

> For a moment, we might think we’re strolling through some part of the Old World, but thanks to nature’s whims, we find ourselves in the very heart of the Caribbean, a tropical land that dresses up every night to welcome the cold and the mist.

> Por un momento pudiéramos pensar que estamos paseando por algún lugar del viejo continente, pero gracias a las curiosidades de la naturaleza, nos encontramos en el pleno corazón del Caribe, una tierra tropical que se viste de gala cada noche para recibir al frío y la neblina.
![IMG_20260423_172958.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yorgar/EnYRsPnPQETGPXbybM7B15Qviz7NJRA7kZhbwMqnV8zpMA131DiMjRJ6KkxK2byrRLG.jpg) ![IMG_20260423_183332.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yorgar/EoprspiJZPm4tGoEnXKJRz51ZQcQUrZoK6C6PJJ8CzcbST317R4GDNoRW6LAbLPoj5e.jpg) ![IMG_20260423_183406.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yorgar/EppKgqGUxSwnwpQpyKKUEh9rrhQMhMraPxzBExtJAgMjavrzG2AnPfqMMGqyBnaC2bc.jpg)

body.title: Tracing the Roots of Melody: The Story of the World's Oldest Instrument
body.body:
​ဟိုင်း... အားလုံးပဲ မင်္ဂလာပါရှင်။ ဒီနေ့တော့ ထူးထူးခြားခြား လွန်ခဲ့တဲ့ နှစ်ပေါင်းသောင်းချီက ကမ္ဘာဦးခေတ်ဆီကို စိတ်ကူးနဲ့ ခရီးသွားကြည့်ရအောင်။ ကျွန်မတို့နေ့စဉ် နားဆင်နေတဲ့ ဂီတသံစဉ်တွေ၊ သီချင်းတွေက ဘယ်ကနေ စတင်မြစ်ဖျားခံခဲ့တာလဲဆိုတာကို စဉ်းစားဖူးကြလားရှင်။ လူတွေ စကားကောင်းကောင်း မပြောတတ်ခင်၊ စာအရေးအသားတွေ မရှိခင် ကျောက်ခေတ်ကတည်းက ကျွန်မတို့ရဲ့ ဘိုးဘေးတွေဟာ ဂီတကို ဖန်တီးခဲ့ကြတယ်ဆိုတာ တကယ်ကို အံ့ဩဖို့ကောင်းပါတယ်။ အဲဒီခေတ်ကတည်းက ရှိခဲ့တဲ့ ကမ္ဘာ့ရှေးအကျဆုံး တူရိယာအကြောင်းကို ဒီနေ့ ကျွန်မက  ရှင်းပြပေးချင်ပါတယ်ရှင်။


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeMqRz9eDmiyDsBS5qmnBaPeCMAmgoQFJXeuaRXc48Zcp/ai_generated.webp)


​Hey everyone! Today, let’s take a little trip back in time—tens of thousands of years ago, right into the Stone Age. Have you ever wondered where the music we listen to every single day actually comes from? Long before humans could properly speak or write, our ancestors were already creating music. It's truly mind-blowing, isn't it? Today, I want to sit down and share a fascinating story about the world's oldest musical instrument, just like sharing a cool story with a friend.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZAk2cTof4a3hm4yJ5rmPNMp7HEtDkuPoA6sG5tVeujWg/1778387232876.jpg)

​ကျွန်မတို့ နေ့စဉ်ဘဝမှာ စိတ်ညစ်တာပဲဖြစ်ဖြစ်၊ ပျော်တာပဲဖြစ်ဖြစ် ဂီတနဲ့ မကင်းကြဘူးမလား။ အခုလို နည်းပညာတွေ မရှိတဲ့ လွန်ခဲ့တဲ့ နှစ်ပေါင်း ၄၀,၀၀၀ ကျော်က ကမ္ဘာဦးလူသားတွေမှာလည်း ဒီလိုခံစားချက်မျိုး ရှိခဲ့ကြပုံရပါတယ်။ အဲ့ဒီခေတ်က လူတွေဟာ တိရစ္ဆာန်တွေရဲ့ အရိုးတွေကို အပေါက်လေးတွေဖောက်ပြီး \
အဖြစ် တီထွင်မှုတ်ခဲ့ကြတာပါ။ လက်ရှိအချိန်အထိ ကမ္ဘာမှာ သမိုင်းပညာရှင်တွေ ရှာဖွေတွေ့ရှိသမျှ ရှေးအကျဆုံး တူရိယာကတော့ ဒီ \

(Bone Flute) ပါပဲ။ စဉ်းစားကြည့်ရုံနဲ့တင် ရင်ခုန်ဖို့ကောင်းတယ်မဟုတ်လားရှင်။ သူတို့တွေဟာ အမဲလိုက်ရင်း၊ အစားအစာရှာရင်းနဲ့ပဲ တစ်ဖက်ကလည်း အနုပညာစိတ်ကူးတွေ ရှိခဲ့ကြတာပေါ့။

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfVLyThM3Fqa8wJw2mFubfxxh8MkuvrLTa1JfLyyLELRf/1778387201786.png)


​In our daily lives, whether we are sad or happy, music is always there for us, right? It turns out that early humans living over 40,000 years ago, without any modern technology, shared that exact same connection to sound. Back then, people took animal bones, carefully carved holes into them, and made the very first flutes. To this day, the oldest musical instrument ever discovered by archaeologists is this \

Just thinking about it gives me goosebumps! While they were busy hunting and gathering to survive, they still found the time and soul to create art.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmemzyxV8JM6D983U1ppWmghJ6nsNxgRhcxGSUdS5pz7YA/1774965657976.jpg)


​ဒီနေရာမှာ ကျွန်မ နည်းနည်း အသေးစိတ် ပြောပြချင်တာက ဂျာမနီနိုင်ငံတောင်ပိုင်းက ဂူတစ်ခုထဲမှာ တွေ့ခဲ့တဲ့ \

(Hohle Fels) လို့ခေါ်တဲ့ ပုလွေအကြောင်းပါ။ အဲ့ဒီပုလွေလေးကို လင်းတငှက်ရဲ့ တောင်ပံရိုးနဲ့ လုပ်ထားတာဖြစ်ပြီး လက်ချောင်းလေးတွေနဲ့ ပိတ်ဆို့ပြီး အသံပြောင်းလို့ရမယ့် အပေါက် ၅ ပေါက်တောင် ပါဝင်ပါတယ်ရှင်။ သုတေသနပညာရှင်တွေက ဒီပုလွေရဲ့ ပုံစံတူကို ပြန်လုပ်ပြီး မှုတ်ကြည့်တဲ့အခါမှာ အခုခေတ် ကျွန်မတို့ကြားနေရတဲ့ ပုလွေသံလိုပဲ သာယာစူးရှတဲ့ အသံမြင့်တွေ ထွက်လာတာကို တွေ့ရပါတယ်။ အဲ့ဒါကို ကြည့်ရင် ကမ္ဘာဦးလူသားတွေဟာ ရိုးရိုးလေး အသံမြည်အောင် လုပ်တာမဟုတ်ဘဲ တကယ့် သံစဉ် (Do-Re-Mi) အတိုင်း ထွက်အောင် စနစ်တကျ တွက်ချက်ပြီး လုပ်ခဲ့ကြတာဆိုတာ သေချာသလောက် ရှိနေပါတယ်။


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUSp3bkEN4MXKfSP1QAFnA53dYCKWJAN29DVgPXH2iJMA/img_0.2951814577976987.jpg)

​I’d love to share a few more details about this. In a cave in southern Germany, scientists found a specific instrument called the Hohle Fels flute. This delicate little thing was crafted from the wing bone of a vulture and featured five precisely carved finger holes. When researchers made a replica of it and tried playing it, they were amazed to find that it produced clear, high-pitched notes just like modern flutes! This proves that early humans didn't just make random noises; they actually calculated and designed a proper musical scale to express their feelings.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTF8bDj5hGPVfLceaFm4bnW1EwZVmLPH4QMsFWmvo7Wxx/img_0.20558356355500287.jpg)


​ဒါဆိုရင် ကျွန်မတို့ စဉ်းစားစရာရှိတာက \

ဆိုတာပါပဲ။ အဲ့ဒီခေတ်က အသက်ရှင်ရပ်တည်ဖို့တောင် ခက်ခဲတဲ့အချိန်မလား။ ကျွန်မ အမြင် ပြောရရင်တော့ ဂီတဆိုတာ လူသားတွေရဲ့ စည်းလုံးမှုကို ပြုလုပ်ပေးတဲ့ အရာတစ်ခုမို့လို့ပါ။ မျိုးနွယ်စုတွေ အတူတူ စုဝေးပြီး မီးပုံပွဲလုပ်တဲ့အခါ၊ ဒါမှမဟုတ် ရိုးရာနတ်ပူဇော်ပွဲတွေ လုပ်တဲ့အခါမှာ ဒီပုလွေသံတွေနဲ့အတူ ကခုန်သီဆိုပြီး အချင်းချင်း ပိုပြီး ရင်းနှီးလာအောင် လုပ်ခဲ့ကြတာ ဖြစ်နိုင်ပါတယ်။ ပြီးတော့ တောနက်ထဲမှာ အမဲလိုက်ရင်း အချင်းချင်း အဝေးကနေ အချက်ပြဖို့ ဆက်သွယ်ရေးကိရိယာအနေနဲ့လည်း သုံးခဲ့ကြမှာ သေချာပါတယ်။


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeRKzMxpdfWXuUQPqu3BLeNAtpVLTWE9BXm8XT2tUos6V/img_0.3710072561825513.jpg)

​This makes us wonder: \

Life back then was purely about survival, wasn't it? In my opinion, music was the ultimate tool for human connection. When clans gathered around the fire or performed rituals, dancing and singing along to these flutes probably brought them closer together as a community. Plus, it's highly likely that they used these sharp sounds as a communication tool to signal one another while hunting deep in the wild forests.


​အခုလို ရှေးဟောင်းသမိုင်းကြောင်းတွေကို ပြန်တွေးကြည့်တဲ့အခါ ကျွန်မတို့ လူသားတွေရဲ့ ရင်ထဲမှာ ဂီတ DNA ဟာ ကမ္ဘာဦးကတည်းက စီးဆင်းနေတာပဲလို့ ခံစားရပါတယ်။ ခေတ်တွေ ဘယ်လောက်ပဲ ပြောင်းသွားပါစေ၊ ကျောက်ခေတ်ကနေ အခု ဒီဂျစ်တယ်ခေတ်အထိ ဂီတကို ချစ်မြတ်နိုးတဲ့စိတ်ကတော့ ပြောင်းမသွားပါဘူး။ အခုဆိုရင် ကျွန်မတို့ဟာ ဂီတကို နားဆင်ရုံတင်မကဘဲ Web3 နည်းပညာတွေ၊ Blockchain တွေပေါ်မှာပါ ဂီတနဲ့ ပတ်သက်ပြီး ဖန်တီးမှုတွေ၊ ကစားမှုတွေ လုပ်လာနိုင်ကြပြီလေ။ အတိတ်က အရိုးပုလွေကနေ ဒီနေ့ခေတ် ဒီဂျစ်တယ်ဂီတအထိ ခရီးစဉ်က တကယ့်ကို အံ့မခန်းပါပဲ။

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZAk2cTof4a3hm4yJ5rmPNMp7HEtDkuPoA6sG5tVeujWg/1778387232876.jpg)


​Thinking about this history makes me realize that music is literally coded into our human DNA from the very beginning. No matter how many eras pass, from the ancient Stone Age to our current digital world, our love for melody remains unchanged. And today, we don't just listen to music; we can actually interact, create, and play with it on modern Web3 and blockchain platforms. The journey from a simple bone flute in a dark cave to digital music on our screens is nothing short of incredible.


​ဂီတအကြောင်း ပြောရင်းနဲ့ ကျွန်မတို့ Hive Blockchain ပေါ်က မိတ်ဆွေတွေကိုလည်း Risingstar Music ဂိမ်းလေးအကြောင်း သတိပေးချင်ပါသေးတယ်။ ကျွန်မတို့ ကမ္ဘာဦးဘိုးဘေးတွေက ပုလွေမှုတ်ပြီး ဂီတလမ်းကြောင်းကို စတင်ခဲ့သလိုမျိုး၊ ကျွန်မတို့လည်း ဒီဂိမ်းထဲမှာ Busker ဘဝကနေ စတင်ပြီး Rock Star တစ်ယောက်ဖြစ်အောင် ကြိုးစားရင်း ဂီတလောကကို ပုံဖော်နိုင်ပါတယ်။ ရှေးခေတ်က ဂီတဟာ လူတွေကို စည်းလုံးစေခဲ့သလိုပဲ၊ အခု Risingstar ကလည်း ကျွန်မတို့ ဂီတချစ်သူတွေကို Hive ပေါ်မှာ တကယ့်အသိုင်းအဝိုင်းတစ်ခုအနေနဲ့ စုစည်းပေးထားတာပါ။ ကဲ... သမိုင်းဦးက ပုလွေသမားလေးတွေလိုပဲ ကျွန်မတို့လည်း Risingstar ထဲမှာ ကိုယ့်ရဲ့ ဂီတအိပ်မက်တွေကို ဆက်ပြီး အသက်သွင်းလိုက်ကြရအောင်လားရှင်။

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfVLyThM3Fqa8wJw2mFubfxxh8MkuvrLTa1JfLyyLELRf/1778387201786.png)


​Speaking of music, I really want to give a shoutout to our Hive community about the Risingstar Music game! Just like our prehistoric ancestors started their musical journey with a humble flute, we get to start our own journey as a simple busker and work our way up to becoming a legendary Rock Star in this game. Music united people in the past, and today, Risingstar unites all of us music lovers as a powerful community right here on Hive. So, just like those ancient flute players, let's keep keeping our musical dreams alive and rocking inside Risingstar!


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYVmxjWbT38JLzNzpiKHmechqJxmjKQByT21UQb4cuWtG/1778387326388.gif)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNNdubDMKXRQkpKzevfMCRvZFp1QCt6uCro2Tn1Bgo3bP/1773495267843.jpg)

Full Metal Ox Day 1911
Sunday 24, May 2026
Abundance Year Episode 1976
Noxsoma Life Camp:  
Sol-2-Soul Sunday #86
Ascension 
Common Sense
It started with stubbornness, then all out rebellion.       

![1976.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUGb6zYjwK8fvCfwshJKdtTZd6x7XYbf6NphsqtSJyG5Z/1976.png)

Today's Episode:   https://odysee.com/@Noxsoma:2/1911_full_5-24-26_1976_sol86:f?r=47k2ScJsm9Uex9eETqgCCA8q1fukdST9  
Channels: go to noxsoma.substack.com and subscribe.
Filling the Gap 

Five weekends in May and this one is Memorial Day, and your boy wasn’t ready. What’s there to be ready for? A barbecue? Too many people. 

We are close enough to June that I can tell you about Radio Free Spirit. It’s just another part of our imaginary media empire. It has to be imaginary at this point because it would take all of my street studio time to set up, maintain and promote a proper podcast. In June we are going to post audio versions of some of our videos. Not AI voice-overs. My actual voice, recorded in the street studio. The topics are varied. If it was music it would be called, “Jazz.” These are night time grooves for our US listeners, dropping every other night at 10 PM, New York time. But they are not “sleep lectures.” They can get pretty in-you-Mind. It’s the Mind Cafe. 
If you are listening from Singapore, you can catch them just before lunch hour, at 11 AM. 
If you’re listening in Honolulu, tune in at 4 PM. 
In Sydney – shout-out to Sydney – catch it at 2 PM. They will stay up for, maybe a fortnight. I want to get out of the habit of posting media and just leaving it there.
We’ll see.     

There’s this one, (actually there’s more than one), podcaster I glanced at. The room is small. It looks stuffed. The host is some dude in some kind of costume. I guess he’s dressed up as a podcaster, or maybe they call them streamers now. There are six women, three on each side of the host. They all have these big mikes in front of them. They all look alike. Not like clones, but the type of women who would catch the average guy’s eye. All the women looked uncomfortable, like, “is there are hair out of place? “Am I sweating?” Is something slipping?” I never turned up the sound, so I don’t know. The host. His body language and costume told me this was something I didn’t want to, or need to watch. It’s probably a “relationship” podcast, or something. Either way. The takeaway for this observer was, “I’m not going to do my podcast like that.”

Did I tell you I started podcasting when it was called, “webcasting?” Officially as a guest in 1998, and then as a host in 1999. Then on video in Y2K. It’s something I mention from time to time. All I did was show up and host a show. Well, a little bit more than that but no tech stuff. I booked guests. I was freelancing at a weekly newspaper in those days, and working grave yard shift in the system. 

I’m imagining what my studio will look like. If I have my way, it will look like I wanted my dorm room to look in the 1970s. Maybe some psychedelic black light zodiac posters hanging up. Pisces & Ox symbolism strategically placed. Posters of Pam Grier from back in the day. You know the one I mean. 7th floor baby. 

I don’t imagine I’ll need that much room to podcast. No bright lights. Lava lamps. Christmas lights hanging. And maybe some old logos of 1970s icons. Maybe iconography from Philly. But back to the space. I may have some space left over to set up a small photo studio. Just head and shoulders shots, maybe some full length if I get ambitious. 

By the time I get this built and situated, this Trinity will have lived in 8 decades. I almost declared the 70s to be “my” best decade. It was probably the best decade of the 20th Century. And the worst. The music was great! Best ever. Across genres. That’s why the industry killed it. Because of the 70s. Star Wars came out in the 70s. That makes the 70s good for movies. I was still a TV addict in the 70s. 

Basically, if I had it to do at this moment, I would build a faux 70s cocoon and talk about today’s issues and stuff that interests this curious Mind. 

Right now though, I’m just filling the gap. I want to have 2 to 4 minutes for the audio. I’m not at am impasse with Cosmogony. We uncovered some amazing coding in the Annunaki story that I haven’t heard anywhere else. The info is thick and I haven’t had time to dig into it, edit it and make it comprehensible. Plus, unless you’re into history, mythology, space-alien philosophy, & numbers, (not necessarily math), you probably won’t be interested. 

Thank you for subscribing. This account posts four or five time a day. You should know that if you are subscribing by email. Articles, original videos, podcasts, and notes, (I don’t know if notes get sent via email.) Feel free to holler through chats or DM’s, or comments. I have not gone live on Substack. I have no plans to. However those plans could change is there is sufficient interest. 

Enjoy your days. Make them magical and not miserable.

body.title: Simple lunch, turkey burger and boiled potatoes/Almuerzo sencillo: hamburguesa de pavo y patatas cocidas.
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbTdt7zdBpeP6BzaPxZY5BuqBYeU58pdi6QiV9wuZ7N3t/1779620631224.jpg)

Good afternoon, blog friends, how are you? Today I still have a bit of a stomach ache, but better than yesterday and the day before. 

However, today I decided to eat something more solid, yet still healthy and simple: turkey burgers with boiled potatoes.

 Here's the recipe for this simple yet delicious dish.

 * 4 turkey burgers
 * 5 medium potatoes 
* 6 tablespoons oil 
* 1 vegetable bouillon cube
 * 3 tablespoons fine salt 

First, prepare the boiled potatoes. Bring a pot of water to a boil with three tablespoons of salt and the bouillon cube. Bring to a simmer and wait for it to boil. Meanwhile, peel the potatoes and cut them into medium-sized pieces, or as desired.

💖💖💖💖💖💖💖💖💖💖💖💖💖💖💖

Buenas tardes, amigos del blog, ¿cómo están? Hoy todavía tengo un poco de dolor de estómago, pero mejor que ayer y anteayer. 

Sin embargo, hoy decidí comer algo más sustancioso, pero a la vez sano y sencillo: hamburguesas de pavo con papas hervidas.

 Aquí les dejo la receta de este plato sencillo pero delicioso.

 * 4 hamburguesas de pavo
 * 5 papas medianas
 * 6 cucharadas de aceite
 * 1 pastilla de caldo de verduras
 * 3 cucharadas de sal fina

 Primero, prepara las papas hervidas. Pon a hervir una olla con agua, tres cucharadas de sal y la pastilla de caldo. Baja el fuego y espera a que hierva. Mientras tanto, pela las papas y córtalas en trozos medianos, o como prefieras.




![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXVB1cZzwC1NS4T6LhRuSxHzp4b8WkWKKzHoA3aRbquGo/1779620631494.jpg)

body.title: Against mosquitoes
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUDKyg23jroseitLyKMSx8bh7ScW2r1SUpVWoiVYXJ7gV/img_20260510_071639.jpg)

---
A few days ago, a neighbor spent the afternoon trimming bushes and even a tree near his building. He wasn’t alone—his wife was with him. She said they were doing it to see if the mosquitoes would calm down a little.  

Yes, in my neighborhood there are a lot of mosquitoes. At home we go crazy from all the itching. The solution has been to buy repellent candles, but they only work for a short time. I’ve long been aware that the problem of such infestation has two main causes: a deficient sewage system and the large leaks in the pipes and aqueducts.  

My neighbors know this unconsciously. For decades we’ve been bombarded with propaganda about how to avoid mosquito breeding grounds, as well as the biology of the little insect. We know everything about them. So how is it possible to believe that trimming a few plants will stop them from invading us?  

Mosquitoes track us because of the CO2 we exhale. There’s no way to escape them except with physical barriers or by working directly on their life cycle. If we eliminate the leaks and get the sewage system working, the mosquito population would probably decrease.  

Right now, for example, they just restored the water service after about two weeks. The streets are full of water and keep filling up because of so many leaks. I get the feeling we’re taking the easiest path, which isn’t even the right one.  

The worst part is that we’re killing the little flora we have in the neighborhood. We’re contributing a bit more to our own extinction. I need a few frogs as pets to see if they protect me from the mosquitoes. The problem is my wife is afraid of them.

body.title: Ніч, коли Київ знову не спав: страшна атака 24 травня, яка залишила шрами на всьому місті
body.body: >Знаєте, я вже не раз думав, що звик. До сирен, до вибухів, до того, як серце стискається щоразу, коли вночі починається цей жах. Але ніч з 23 на 24 травня 2026 року була особливою. Ворог кинув на столицю все, що міг — і ракети, і сотні дронів. Пошкодження зафіксували в кожному районі Києва. Це не просто атака, це спроба зламати нас, показати, що ніхто не в безпеці. А ми стоїмо. Як завжди.
>Я прокинувся від перших вибухів. Вікна дрижали, наче хотіли вилетіти. Дружина схопила дітей, ми бігли в коридор. А в голові тільки одна думка: \
. На жаль, не для всіх.

>Станом на ранок відомо про одного загиблого і 13 постраждалих. Сім людей у лікарні, шість отримали допомогу на місці. Цифри можуть ще зростати, бо рятувальники досі працюють. Але вже зараз зрозуміло — це була одна з наймасштабніших атак за останній час.

>Почнемо з Дарницького району. Там уламки БпЛА та ракет поцілили в гуртожиток. Уявіть: люди спали, а раптом стіни затремтіли, скло посипалося. Пошкоджено кілька нежитлових приміщень, СТО, автівки біля будинків. Люди вибігали в піжамах, хтось ніс на руках дітей. Рятувальники працювали під постійною загрозою нових ударів. Це не війна з армією — це війна з цивільними.

>Source
В Оболонському районі все було ще жорсткіше. Дрон влучив прямо в приватний одноповерховий будинок. Повністю зруйнував. Добре, що господарі встигли вибігти — чисте диво. А поруч, біля триповерхового будинку, загорілася відкрита територія. Потім пожежа перекинулася на 16-поверхівку. Друга будівля теж загорілася. Чорний дим стояв стовпом, його було видно з іншого берега Дніпра. Сусіди допомагали один одному — передавали воду, витягували літніх людей. Ось що робить нас сильними.

\n\n

>Source
Шевченківський район... Тут серце стискається особливо. Уламки ракети пошкодили два житлових будинки і офісний центр. Автівки на парковці просто згоріли, як сірники. А ще пожежі на територіях двох шкіл. Шкіл, друзі. Місця, де вчора бігали діти з ранцями. На щастя, вночі там нікого не було. Гасили і газову трубу між будинками — один неточний рух, і могло бути ще страшніше. Рятувальники працювали як боги.

Так зараз виглядає ТРЦ Квадрат в Шевченківському районі Києва.

>У Дніпровському районі уламки впали на дах багатоповерхівки. В іншому місці дрон влучив у приватний будинок — пожежа. Постраждали склад і гаражний кооператив. Люди втратили машини, інструменти, частину свого життя, яке накопичували роками.

>Святошинський — уламки на одноповерховий приватний будинок. Просто пробили дах. Подільський — падіння на нежитлову забудову. Голосіївський — дах 24-поверхівки. Деснянський — супермаркет і торговий центр. Солом’янський — влучання на рівні 23-го поверху 24-поверхового будинку. Руйнування конструкцій, пожежа. Печерський — пожежа в 20-поверхівці.

>

Приліт біля підземного переходу у Києві, де люди ховалися від атаки рф
>Зокрема, знищено ринок на Лук'янівці, пошкоджено вестибюль пошкоджено вестибюль станції метро Лук'янівська.
>Кожне влучання — це не просто цегла і скло. Це долі. Хтось втратив дім, хтось — спокій. Я розмовляв з другом з Солом’янського. Він каже: \

. Ось так. Випадковість.

А це влучання в музей Чорнобиля.
рф розгромила Нацмузей Чорнобильської трагедії, який відкрили лише місяць тому. Також був приліт по облуправлінню ДСНС.

>Але знаєте, що вражає найбільше? Як швидко кияни приходять в себе. Вже зранку люди несли волонтерам воду, їжу, ліки. Хтось розбирав завали разом з ДСНС. Хтось просто обіймав сусіда, який залишився без нічого. Ми не ламаємося. Ми стаємо твердішими.
>Ця атака — частина більшої картини. Росіяни запускали сотні дронів і балістику по всій Україні. Був удар \
по Білій Церкві. Вони хочуть терору, паніки. Але бачимо протилежне. Повітряні сили збили більшість, хоча не все. Наші захисники роблять неможливе.

>Я думаю про тих, хто загинув. Про поранених. Про дітей, які тепер бояться спати. І розумію: ненависть — це не емоція, це паливо. Ми маємо пам'ятати кожне ім'я, кожну зруйновану квартиру. Бо це не просто війна. Це боротьба за право жити нормально.

>Сьогодні Київ у диму і пилу. Але він живий. Ремонтники вже латають дахи, волонтери збирають допомогу, психологи працюють з людьми. Життя продовжується. Ми ховаємо загиблих, лікуємо поранених і йдемо далі.
>Хочу сказати кожному, хто читає: якщо ви в Києві — тримайтеся. Якщо в іншому місті — дякуйте нашим хлопцям на фронті. Вони дають нам шанс прокидатися щоранку. А ми маємо бути сильними тут, у тилу.
>Ця ніч залишить шрами. На будинках, на серцях. Але не на нашій волі. Київ вистоїть. Україна вистоїть. Бо ми — не просто люди. Ми — народ, який не вмів здаватися.
>Слава Україні. І вічна пам'ять тим, кого забрала ця підла війна.

body.title: DAILY LIFE STORY: Disposal of Expired and Damaged Items
body.body: /> * * * Working in the wholesale and retail industry means dealing with the disposal of expired and damaged items. It is part of the company's policy when it comes to inventory control. And recently, we needed to dispose of the items that needed to be cleared out from the warehouse. Some of them are expired, while the others have damage. First, we disposed of the drinks. There are Corona beers and a box of ice creams. We had to dispose of them first since they are easier to dispose of.

/> The next thing we prepared is the box of oil packed in a plastic bag. There are a lot of them, and the reason for disposal is that they have already expired. We checked the barcode and the total quantity since they need to be zeroed out in the system after disposal. It was really disappointing to see such products go to waste just because they are not monitored well in the warehouse. They have been stuck inside the cages until they expired, which could have been avoided if the personnel assigned to check this item had proper monitoring and checking.

/> Lastly, we needed to dispose of a lot of Coca-Cola, the ones in plastic bottles. You can see them piled up in the receiving area, and we need to dispose of them since they have already expired. The supplier failed to pick them up; we will conduct the disposal. In this case, the suppliers delivered these items on their near-expiry stage, so it resulted in this. We need to get them out of the warehouse and report for their disposal right away. The task was really tiring, but it was part of our monthly clearing and disposal activities.

/> So, that's it for today. Thank you so much for reading. See you on our next blog. body.title: Changes…       …Part 1               …Tired of Running
body.body:
**They always say time changes things, but you actually have to change them yourself* ― Andy Warhol*


![download.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQy4SBAa6tq6LdoTjVJLBTnFdLr7oXPzVeZ2LWKFDzZGF/download.jpg)
*Looking For Work*


“Want a drink, Hon?” She’s one of those country bargirls I figure is supporting a lazy boyfriend—and judging by the lines around her eyes, she’s close to forty. “Naw, I’m kinda between gigs.” She pushes back a stray wisp of blonde hair and I can see she looks pretty. “I didn’t ask you for a job application—it’s on the house—what’s your poison?” I smirk, “In that case, how about a C. C. Rider?” She slants me a baleful look. “I take it you mean *Canadian Club*—won’t take it any other way—and you got rich taste for a honky tonk country singer.”

I smile my charming smile and she slaps down a tumbler and pours two fingers of the good stuff I rarely get to drink. “And don’t go flashing those pearly whites—I’m just being kind cause Cal—well, Cal can be real mean, you know?” I nod and look repentant—that pose is my one-two punch—gets them every time, if they’re interested, that is. But she may be kind-hearted cause I see her splash a little extra in an old guy’s drink at the end of the bar. He looks up bleary-eyed and smiles, “Why thanks, LeAnn!” I’m not sure that’s her name or he figures she looks like LeAnn Rimes—but if that’s the case, he’s dead wrong—she’s prettier.

Cal finally waddles out from the office in the back—he’s got to be three hundred pounds and has a mean streak more ugly than the jagged scar down his cheek—I’ve seen those tracks and I know broken beer bottles do that. He sits down beside me wheezing and motions for LeAnn to drop him a drink. He’s sizing me up all the while. “Caught your set at *Hoots Hollow* the other night,” he deadpans. “Don’t say—how’d you like it?” “Music’s okay, but voice is kinda pitchy—know what I mean? You’re the type doesn’t hit the notes—sort of sing between the keys,” he starts to wheeze and laugh. “Ha ha, you kinda fall between the cracks in the piano keys.” His eyes are watering. “Is that a fact? Well, that’s my way—and I like it.”

He looks at me quizzically as Blondie drops his drink. “How’s that?” “You see, I sing it real. I sing between the cracks because that’s where the truth settles, like dirt that gets under your finger nails.” I watch Blondie’s eyes and see her repress a grin. “So, you’re just like all these old boys around here—not afraid of the soil?” “That’s me,” I smile. He tilts his head in my direction and Blondie drops two fingers of CC in my glass.

“Hell, is that what you’re drinking, boy? You’re going need to sing a lot of country blues to pay that bill.” “I’m available for the week.” He gets up and grabs his drink. “You’re hired. Tell LeAnn to advance you a coupla hundred and we’ll settle up on Saturday night.” LeAnn flashes me a thumbs-up. I think I’m going to like it here.

I get a deal on a motel room for the week—Cal’s got some arrangement with the owner. I spend the morning driving around *Bill’s Corners*—well, actually, the countryside. The town consists of one stoplight and a few hundred residents, but it’s a truck stop on a busy secondary road, and at night it’s hopping. After a while the towns all look the same—and the people too. That’s when I start pointing my F150 in the direction of The Big Smoke and Bonnie, and wend my way home. The way I live is not for everyone—watching towns fade into dust in a rearview mirror. Bonnie hates it, but she’s stayed faithful down through the years. We’ve been going on ten years now and she keeps waiting for me to grow up—but it’s not just the music—it’s the travelling and the road that’s got my soul. Besides, I don’t know how it would work—going home. I realized the other day all my memories are melodies—and photos with the GPS turned off.

I’m flying under the radar in more ways than one—leaving women my cell number on rolling papers and not answering when they call. The women are either wild or sweet like LeAnn, but I always go home. What I like best though is writing my songs and hanging out with other musicians. Most people think country singers are cut-throat—like they’d drive over you in an eighteen wheeler if you got in their way—but it’s not like that.

Sometimes we sit around till three or four in the morning jamming and playing our songs—and when I play something good they’ll get thoughtful and cry, or laugh along and be as proud as if it were their own. That’s the side of country I’ve seen. But lately, I’m getting tired of all the honkytonks and bars and women whose names I forget the moment I leave. Maybe It's time for a change, but what's it going to take to make me go home? I wonder if I even can.

To be continued…

body.title: What will be the future of BTC?
body.body:
![277465.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josediccus/23wWkGsKujoCAHE1LuizMu5Nuhjm8Rj2tHoFt9KDASN9PRBsdyzP47Zn7ZYUtT6io66E4.png)



<Hr>



BTC was 75k yesterday and today it's 77k, so basically still hovering around that 70k to 80k range which is ridiculously good, considering that we should be hitting even lower.


 Perhaps BTC is learning to be a stable asset rather than a volatile one, I won't put it past it.


 The interests of institutions and government means that at some point we weren't going to see those crazy dumps anymore, but them we also won't see those big and life changing pumps anymore, then it becomes more of a digital asset rather than traditional crypto and probably joining other forms of digital assets which means it's no longer going to be that **\

** that Satoshi actually design it to be.  


> It was inevitable. 


This is what happens when a digital asset gets so much acceptance and attention and the government can no longer overlook it, and since they can't kill it, they might as well try to control how it works.



 Reminds me of Spartacus, he became so popular that the Roman government couldn't ignore him anymore. I'm not saying BTC is likely to meet the same fate as well, my point is that, the trajectory of BTC was meant to change, perhaps at some point begins to identify as something other than crypto, but I was thinking, at least this shouldn't happen until 10 to 15 years time.


 > It's already looking like this


**The price manipulation we saw in 2025 was evident.**

 Trump and co manipulated the market so hard, mad a lot of money off it, and even created their own coin by riding the bull market's fame. Although the market is still likely to pump hard after the next halving which is stipulated for the April 2028 I think? 




 Yeah, somewhere around that time. In reality this might be a speculation, the rambling of a mad man, or just someone who is looking too deep into the meaning of all of these. 

However we look at it, I think the biggest bulk of dump happened in late 2025 amd early 2026, quite ironic that this particular period was once the peak of a green market. 


However it looked like we've seen the worse of the market and we would just continue to consolidate until 2028, but who knows?


 Anyway this isn't a speculation post, my point is that all these \

and the glaring predictability of the market *(the BTC Price market actually)*


### Conclusion 


 it just looks like BTC will most likely become a predictable asset in the future; no excessive pumps and dumps, just a crypto or digital asset that you can just save money in, especially if you hate banks or just hate fiat in general, not minding the occasion dumps you see, provided some better pumps were guaranteed.


 This means it's no longer going to be an asset that could change one's financial standing, except of course you're planning to hold for 20 to 30 years, and then your kids or kin gets to inherit it or something. 

This might leave alt projects completely dependent on themselves to push their projects, their business or something like that to the wider audience without completely having to wait for BTC to lead while they follow. 


**This might be good, but who knows, it might not.**


 No one can exactly speculate the future of crypto, but one thing is clear: it'll definitely not look like what we have today, it'll not mirror what we currently have and sadly this will no longer benefit the folks who are banking on the future of crypto to make it big.

body.title: Spraying with milk, improvised fence for chickens, tent and a ladder for hazelnuts
body.body:
Last year we had an invasion of stink bugs, they literally ate our tomatoes and there was nothing they didn't damage. Luckily this winter there was frost and a little bit of frost so there is no one this year. But this year the Colorado potato beetle is the one that attacked our potatoes and also lays eggs on tomatoes.
![20260522_171135.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AJmsPDgCZpLQo3u961tp9duapRSPSBbLVcMnD9FaG435Pkan8xN7gxo3Qi7kbkw.jpg)
Although we collected and removed it, it did not help. It is an extremely invasive species and if not treated quickly it can destroy the entire potato patch.
My wife and I try to produce our fruits and vegetables organically, so some poisons are out of the question. Only as a last resort. But until then, we have purchased homemade milk from a woman in our village. Since insects are not lactose intolerant and some insects do not like the smell of milk.
![20260524_125441.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AK9Pukav2rCNKXEHSrFYtSoThuGfUTYrw9mm6naeaEvtbdNPLEVQ92NypQonPJw.jpg)
Our recipe is simple: mix 2 deciliters of milk with 5 liters of water. Mix everything well in a spray bottle. Spray on a sunny day so that the milk sticks to the potato leaves.Nettle is also good against this pest, but we are currently in short supply of it.
![20260524_131416.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKU3y9pRnLzdycUSZBwNvybc9CC2BJ42rfWBiFo8kKaMbAJQNB8fLNaQK192Eb3.jpg)
In the part of the yard that is closer to the garden, we have a chamomile invasion. We have harvested some for tea, maybe we will do a little more. But I should definitely get a chamomile comb.

![20260524_121310.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AJJau5AnjHyMXpCwPknCiT5FahAseKU25bbej8ueuJ7QoSnF9cdBj8n3EN6gGsj.jpg)


Last year, a storm took away our fence, with which we divided two parts of the yard. In the part where the chamomile is, there were cockscombs. Last year, I made a smaller part of the yard intended for cockscombs. They don't have grass there either. In order not to build a fence again, we used real netting to just fence off the yard. So that the cockscombs don't go into this part of the yard where we have a greenhouse and a flower garden.
![20260524_124939.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKDgzCqo1AtrAYG5uzHF6t8h9wkeXUspnprTRwCvUPb2utVJRWbSQ3oqxeNCMeR.jpg)
Old tree stumps were used for improvisation.The little chickens will be released all day on the grass, the hens will be released for a few hours at a time, so that they don't destroy all the grass.
![20260524_131448.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKNJgQBR4iMWiWEp2L7eUMqa8KHEr7TTX4Bza4uJb8JgZmJLkdatUfYLn98dXYf.jpg)

My son has taken over the hazelnut tree. Last year I built him a treehouse, then he added a swing between the hazelnut and apricot trees.
This time he asked for a tent and a ladder.
We made the tent from a 3x4 m tarpaulin. And for the ladder, we used an old plastic ladder from a slide. So that he could climb and sit on the tree.

![20260524_125117.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AJkQ7oa4t1ndvuqcf9UEm4BkM63MN3TirAXYtcdL7WkCSw5nt1jwvsiHSBMg5TQ.jpg)

The cultivated form of hazelnut is a tree.
We shaped it like an umbrella. More precisely, a parasol because it really creates shade all around. Ideal for children to play under it.

![20260524_125107.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AJpiEaxtvjcyfuwEK3EDvbHJ4L2JftBjaNqTvN4HtDAJYKN9sPLh3kCeAPSgoom.jpg)

---
Thanks for reading.
Until next time.
Stay healthy.
Markone85.
---

body.title: My safe haven | Loh #290
body.body: > Everyone needs a safe haven. There are times when life gets overwhelming. We've all been there. In such moments, it feels like you're going to break down. Some feel like they are drowning is so much.

/> [Image Source](https://pixabay.com/photos/man-grass-lying-resting-relaxing-1867800/) Life is filled with so many stressors. We are all going about different things, hustling to make money and build a better life for ourselves. The stress can pile up to the point where we just need a safe haven from it all. A safe haven must not necessarily be a place. It can be a person, it can be a thing, or it can be an activity. In fact, it could be anything. As long as it gives you peace, as long as it's an escape from stressors, as long as it makes you feel safe, it's your safe haven. My safe haven is movies. I'm a huge fan of movies. I do have overwhelming days often. Days when I just want to disconnect, relax and recover. More importantly, days when I just want to escape problems or at least forget about them. Movies are that escape for me. Movies have a way of bringing me to another world for a moment. In that moment, I'm engrossed in what is happening in it. I'm fascinated. Scene after scene, episode after episode, I get engrossed. It makes me forget about everything else that may have kept me in an overwhelmed state. You'll be surprised by what a good, captivating movie can do to you. Most times, when I get home after a hectic day, I just watch a good movie to relax. Sometimes I binge watch, especially during the weekends when I just want to recover from the stress of the week. It could be sci-fi movie, a thriller, rom com or even action. As long as that move had an interesting plot, I'm delving into it. Why this is such a safe haven for me is because when you watch a good movie, your mind isn't focused on anything else. You're just focused on the movie. I would be busy trying to figure out what's happening in the movie. This takes my mind away from the problems I'm probably facing in real life. That kind of distraction gives you clarity of mind most of the time. With a clear mind, I'm be able to figure out how to go about whatever issues are bothering me.

body.title: Capítulo 6: El Libro de las Sombras Blancas
body.body:
>El Padre Thomas se sentó frente al viejo escritorio de caoba en la rectoría, lejos de los muros opresores de la casa del canal, pero aún bajo su influencia. Sus dedos, largos y amarillentos, acariciaron el lomo de un cuaderno de cuero ajado. En su interior no había oraciones, sino una crónica de ausencias.
Thomas no siempre había sido un hombre de fe inquebrantable; su devoción nació del terror puro el día que vio a la primera familia desvanecerse.

### Los Van den Berg: El silencio del banquete (1984) Thomas recordaba con una nitidez dolorosa a los Van den Berg. Eran cuatro: un matrimonio joven y dos niñas que siempre llevaban lazos azules en el pelo. La casa los recibió con una calidez engañosa. Él los visitó una tarde de diciembre. Al entrar, notó que el aire en el comedor estaba estancado, como si el tiempo se hubiera congelado. La familia estaba sentada a la mesa, frente a platos llenos de comida humeante, pero nadie se movía. * **La anomalía:** Las niñas no pestañeaban. Miraban fijamente un punto en la pared donde las sombras de las velas parecían bailar sin que las llamas se movieran. * **La desaparición:** Al día siguiente, Thomas regresó preocupado. La puerta estaba abierta de par en par. La comida seguía en los platos, aún caliente, desprendiendo vapor a pesar del frío glacial de Ámsterdam. Pero la familia se había esfumado. No había señales de lucha, solo cuatro sillas ligeramente apartadas y los lazos azules de las niñas flotando en el agua estancada del sótano. ### Los Meyer: El eco en las paredes (1994) Diez años después, llegaron los Miller, una pareja de historiadores que creían poder catalogar el mal. Thomas intentó advertirlos, pero lo trataron como a un viejo supersticioso. Thomas recordaba haber pasado por la acera de enfrente una noche de tormenta. A través de las ventanas del segundo piso, vio a los Miller corriendo de una habitación a otra, pero sus movimientos eran erráticos, como si estuvieran atrapados en un laberinto invisible. * **El horror:** Lo que Thomas vio esa noche lo persiguió por décadas: los Miller no estaban solos. Detrás de ellos, sus propias sombras se habían despegado de sus pies y los perseguían con movimientos fluidos y depredadores. * **El final:** Cuando la policía entró tres días después, encontraron la casa vacía. Lo único que quedaba de ellos eran grabaciones de audio. En la última cinta, solo se escuchaba el sonido de alguien rascando frenéticamente la madera... desde el interior de las paredes. ### La confesión del vigilante Thomas cerró el cuaderno. Sus ojos se empañaron al recordar cómo la casa parecía \

después de cada desaparición; la madera se volvía más brillante, el mármol más frío, y el silencio más profundo.  
—He sido el pastor de un rebaño que camina directo al matadero —susurró Thomas para sí mismo, mirando hacia la ventana.  
Él no era un salvador. Con los años, Thomas había comprendido su verdadero papel: él era el **notario de la casa**. La entidad que habitaba los cimientos exigía un testigo, alguien que recordara a los que ya no estaban para que el vacío que dejaban fuera más real.  
Ahora, mientras pensaba en Ana, una punzada de culpa le recorrió el pecho. Sabía que la casa ya había comenzado a digerir su presencia. La visita rutinaria que le había hecho no era para protegerla, sino para observar cuánto terreno había ganado la oscuridad en sus ojos.  
Thomas tomó la pluma y comenzó a escribir el nombre de Ana en la página siguiente, dejando el espacio para la fecha de su desaparición aún en blanco. Por primera vez en cuarenta años, su mano tembló.
