body.title: The Power of Shield and Void Armor in Splinterlands — How Grimbardun Fighter Destroyed My Strategy
body.body:
![MINDLESS THRALL.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23wMUMPfewJhwgBQdHvRPV7EhfsLkB5nE6QFiPMCTG5UALCccq9HE8NeffER6pLYZQnkR.png)


Todays battle was quite strange for me and maybe it is the first time that something like this happened that I had to face this kind of defeat. Mostly in Splinterlands I have a good experience of winning battles especially when the mana is high because it allows to select strong monsters and make a good combination.

But what happened today was completely different from my expectations. I think my opponent was quite a pro player and very expert in the selection of monsters.

To be honest I feel that this time my selection and positioning were not as strong as they should have been. Usually I win my high mana battles so I was quite confident that I would easily win this battle as well. But sometimes the game also teaches us that we should never underestimate any opponent.

Todays battle was of 56 mana which comes in the high mana category. In this battle I selected 7 monsters and my opponent also selected 7 monsters. When I made the team I felt that my combination was quite strong and maybe I would easily win the match. Because of which I also took this battle a little easy.

I selected the monsters according to my usual strategy. That means one good frontline tank then support monsters and backline attackers. I also kept the positioning best according to my understanding. But when the battle started, slowly I realized that the opponents strategy was quite strong.

The opponents first monster that was on the frontline kept fighting alone for a long time. His backline monsters kept giving him continuous support. Sometimes he was getting heal, sometimes extra defense, and sometimes strong attacks. 

![ChatGPT Image May 24, 2026, 01_44_48 PM.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23uFHTEXzBMF6b2qgk9LLhxjpcCY8LBStLYLyPmfsaNeTN6MQNpc6cUg4DdCnkwz4PvHG.png)

Due to which he survived in the battle for the long time.  This was quite unexpected for me. I rarely see such a defeat but this is also part of the game and this is where learning comes from.

In this battle the monster that impressed me the most was Grimbardun Fighter. This monster was a very strong part of the opponents team and was performing very well on the frontline. The abilities of this monster impressed me a lot.

The most important ability of Grimbardun Fighter is Shield which reduces the damage of melee and ranged attacks. In the same way it also has Void Armor which allows magic attacks to be absorbed by armor first. 

Its weakness is that its damage is not very high and if the opponent has very strong magic attackers then sometimes it can come under pressure quickly.

have you ever played this monster? tell about its any ability? Will be glad to see your answers in the comment section.

I hope you find this post useful and informative.. If you do, please remember to reblog it so that it reaches as many people as possible and that they can benefit the most from it. Also remember to upvote which will help me financially and grow my account.

During my vacation in Slovenia, I found beauty in the simplest things even in the shadows.

While walking around and enjoying the peaceful surroundings, I noticed how the sunlight perfectly created geometric shadows from these metal rails. The clean lines and sharp angles instantly caught my attention, making such an ordinary spot look artistic and unique.

Sometimes, we get so focused on famous tourist attractions that we forget to appreciate the little details around us. This moment reminded me that beauty can be found anywhere, especially when light and shadow work together perfectly.

I took this photo because the shadows looked calm, balanced, and somehow satisfying to look at. Moments like this are what make traveling more memorable for me — discovering unexpected beauty in everyday places.

Slovenia truly gave me not just beautiful destinations, but also simple moments worth capturing.

Thank you @melinda010100 for initiating this Shadow Contest

Thank you for reading everyone have a nice day!

body.title: Photo Trip | Czech Republic - Small Church of The Holy Trinity
body.body:
![COVER.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23u5tRhR2ovhjFy2pnoVmAhgkNXjxteWKMzCy6a12ADSjvbnAd4s2Sfcq3Vyz8iR1UTCT.jpg)

In today’s post, we’ll visit a small town in northern Czechia, right on the border with Poland. Since it’s Sunday, we’ll also take a quick look at the Church of the Holy Trinity in Žacléř.


> <sub>**[ PL ]**</sub>
> W dzisiejszym wpisie zawitamy do małego miasteczka w północnych Czechach tuż przy granicy z Polską. Przy okazji niedzieli częściowo odwiedzimy Kościół Trójcy Świętej w miejscowości Žacléř.


![RSphotos-25-08-15-RSP_2594.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23ynJ8gvTThmoUG3PoU4dPdVhjLbGb8jE69x9HSgpCFLFGHV6ZLncW8daCT78DRYNCaYd.jpg)

When you’re at Rýchorské Square in the southern part of town, it’s easy to spot the church and find your way there. Its tower stands out against the other buildings.

> Będąc na miejskim placu Rýchorské w południowej części miasta możemy łatwo odnaleźć kościół i drogę do niego. Jego wieża wyróżnia się na tle innych budynków.

![RSphotos-25-08-15-RSP_2592.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23xeX9C4v89EiqPBPtXdTD4wpkKA3Y9jgWrAo8CK2G8HtKxPYcfATzgrZ1rtWJwjhf1RL.jpg)


![RSphotos-25-08-15-RSP_2571.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23y8gxbbDMPaxvRJEkuCMziNKJ3w7bTa16k9SQH8iSL7gVzNtaZYWjpA1g5yGJckYCKkb.jpg)

There are trees growing in front of the church, so you'll need to be a little creative when taking photos. On the north and west sides, including the entrance, the church has been renovated and restored.

> Przed kościołem rosną drzewa, więc potrzebna jest odrobina kreatywności aby zrobić zdjęcia. Od strony północnej i zachodniej z wejściem, kościół jest wyremontowany i odnowiony.

![RSphotos-25-08-15-RSP_2563.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23uFKXpzcbd4SEKEhLSipapvqsUqxJUXHQZc6fLndAQ6gFDok8hY8g8qc6gaUBkVLKz5E.jpg)

The first church was built here in the 14th century; the current Baroque-style church was built in 1732.

> Pierwszy kościół powstał tutaj w XIV wieku, obecny w barokowym stylu powstał w 1732 roku.

![RSphotos-25-08-15-RSP_2564.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/2423yimU1iQpRjJrp51sNuXXARkkcWgUyhg4NM8MuzUPfD7ZZDiLXEi4gUdybZPjcpLKk.jpg)

We couldn't go inside because the gate was locked.

> Do środka nie mogliśmy wejść ze względu na zamknięte wejście z kraty.

![RSphotos-25-08-15-RSP_2565.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23tbRZ1Dqb8NyVJzN3K3P5ng8UvWHgnY4M9eR1hduEKMU77BMYoW3BC8y7YrgvuPs8XoS.jpg)

However, I was able to take a few shots of the interior through those bars.

> Natomiast przez te kraty mogłem wykonać kilka ujęć wnętrza.

![RSphotos-25-08-15-RSP_2566.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23wWpSPUFNVBDVCzXauQ2rbbRWFak1GitVAmxHakFp73P3VuZDGpjwR2FKHoiG7rcAT7g.jpg)

It’s a bit of a shame that we couldn’t get a closer look inside.

> Trochę szkoda, że nie można było zobaczyć wnętrza tego z bliska.

![RSphotos-25-08-15-RSP_2567.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/23uFHFEQr64LnLWSbvSK8r6jUVDmSnRvzM7aL15zby8NNKfyGGqrBRBG7n8tXCyaLtPbZ.jpg)

![RSphotos-25-08-15-RSP_2569.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rsphotos/242NUQsL5ZyB6yGDLuu8xKE6FhJtnQKszxbJhbUQR6dCijbzMPmfhbxE8KtGwjH3XHwPn.jpg)

A view from the south side, which was still under renovation. You can see what condition the church was in before. On the east side of the church is a cemetery, which I didn't go to see.

> Widok od strony południowej, która nadal była w remoncie. Można zobaczyć w jakim stanie był wcześniej kościół. Po stronie wschodniej kościoła jest cmentarz na który nie poszedłem obejrzeć.

body.title: Leo Messi - LOH Contest #290
body.body:
>Yeah ive always viewed fame as a double edged sword. Yes, it comes with wealth, influence and opportunities most people can only dream of, but that is just from the outside but from the inside it also comes with alot of pressure to always look perfect and people put you on this unrealistic pedastal and a complete loss of privacy. Honestly, I do not really envy people who are overly famous. Imagine living a life where every single thing you do becomes news. Your mistakes and your bad days, even the way you breathe, somehow becomes public discussion. That kind of life sounds exhausting to me.

Sometimes I see celebrities walking through crowds with cameras shoved aggressively into their faces, and I wonder how they stay sane. The media constantly wants a story and social media users dissect every action. One wrong statement, and suddenly the entire internet becomes a courtroom.

Anyways that is by the way and with regards to this weeks prompt my answer would be Lionel Messi. Messi for me is one celebrity, probably the only celebrity that i will geek out when i see, all the others i honestly wouldn’t even care but messi..... and its not because he is the richest or the flashiest celebrity in the world, but because i so much admire him, he made me fall in love with football. Messi’s life and career seem to carry a level of peace and humility that many famous people never get to experience and to be honest his personality also matches mine. Despite being one of the greatest footballers of all time, he has always appeared reserved and calm. He is not constantly in unnecessary controversies and he does not seem addicted to attention.

Growing up, watching Messi felt almost unreal at times. The way he moves with the ball, the composure, the simplicity in his style, it all feels effortless even though you know it took years of sacrifice and discipline. So yeah, if I had to choose someone to swap lives with, it would probably be Lionel Messi.

body.title: Chapter 2: The Neeba Special
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRpdMfUXSg85QrjSUsscN4RHkhNbwYh2KpneSo4RgW26C/img_7126.png)
By the time Elijah’s flight landed, the woman in the corner had already finished one coffee and allowed the second to go cold.

She did not look like someone waiting for news.

That was deliberate.

People waiting for news had a particular stillness. A held breath. A little too much attention in the hands. They checked doors too often, touched their phones too often, looked up whenever cutlery fell.

She did none of those things.

She sat beside the window of a small corner café in a country where no one knew her name, with a scarf around her hair, a chipped mug beside her hand, and rain threading silver lines down the glass.

The café was ordinary enough to be useful.

No velvet chairs.

No polished floors.

No waiter asking if everything was to her liking.

Just a counter, a chalkboard menu, six small tables, a pastry case, and a woman behind the till who shouted orders with the tired authority of someone who had seen every kind of customer and been impressed by none of them.

Perfect.

Ordinary places were the hardest to search because nobody believed anything important could happen there.

A small voice clicked in her ear.

“Ma’am, confirmation. His flight has landed.”

The woman did not move.

Not at first.

Then her fingers loosened around the paper napkin she had been folding into smaller and smaller squares.

“Status?”

“Cleared arrivals. No secondary inspection. No visible tail inside the terminal.”

She closed her eyes.

Only for a second.

Long enough for relief to pass through her without becoming visible.

“Good,” she said.

The voice paused.

“Do you want us to approach?”

“No.”

“He is asking questions.”

“He always asks questions.”

“He asked for about the Receipt!”

https://ecency.com/hive-161155/@wordsofwealth/the-receipt


The woman looked out at the rain.

Her reflection stared back from the glass. Older than she remembered. Calmer than she felt. Alive, which had become an increasingly inconvenient condition.

“No contact,” she said.

“Understood.”

The line went quiet.

For a moment, she let herself breathe.

Elijah was safe.

Not free.

Not yet.

But safe enough to keep moving.

That would have to be enough.

She reached for her bag.

Then the woman behind the counter called out:

“One Neeba Special!”

The room did not stop.

Rooms never stop when a life cracks open.

A chair scraped.

Milk hissed behind the counter.

Someone laughed near the door.

The woman in the corner stayed very still.

The name had not been spoken loudly. It had not needed to be. It entered the room softly and found her anyway.

The cashier glanced down at the order slip and called again.

“One Neeba Special?”

Only then did the woman look up.

There, on the counter, beside the coffee cups and paper bags and cheap silver teaspoons, sat a plate that had no business existing in that café.

Three smoked sausages.

Potatoes.

Peppers.

Dark sauce.

Arranged with absurd care, as though the sausages had gathered for a private meeting and the potatoes had been invited against their better judgement.

Her mouth went dry.

No.

Not here.

Not in this country.

Not when Elijah was half a world away.

The Neeba Special had never been on any menu.

It had not belonged to cafés, kitchens, or strangers with order slips.

It belonged to a boy who once found her crying behind an old community hall and decided, with the grave confidence of childhood, that sorrow could be negotiated with food.

He had arrived carrying a plastic plate and a meal so strange she had stopped crying out of pure suspicion.

“What is this?” she had asked.

“Dinner,” Elijah said.

“It looks like a warning.”

“It is balanced.”

“The sausages look like they know something.”

“They are protecting the potatoes.”

“That is not comforting.”

He had sat beside her anyway.

That was the thing about Elijah.

He never asked sadness to explain itself. He simply arrived beside it, placed food between them, and waited.

After that, whenever she disappeared into herself, he made it again.

Three sausages.

Potatoes.

Peppers.

Sauce.

Never elegant.

Never sensible.

Always his.

And always with a secret hidden somewhere inside it.

A raisin.

A sweetcorn kernel.

A piece of apple.

Once, a jelly sweet, which she had called an act of emotional… she could not finish the thought!

“You need one surprise,” he used to say, “or sadness starts thinking it owns the room.”

The woman in the café stood.

Not because she wanted to.

Because some names are not called.

They are pulled from you.

At the sugar station, a man in a grey coat lifted his head.

Small movement.

Too small for anyone else.

Enough for her.

Her hand tightened around the strap of her bag.

So that was it.

Not a gift.

A test.

Someone had sent the plate into the room to see who would answer to the name.

The voice in her ear returned.

“Ma’am?”

She did not respond.

“Do not approach the counter.”

The cashier called again, irritated now.

“One Neeba Special?”

The woman walked forward.

Every step felt too loud.

The café remained beautifully, cruelly normal. People stirred coffee. Tore pastries. Read messages. Held conversations that would never matter to anyone trying not to be seen.

She reached the counter.

The cashier pushed the plate toward her.

“There you go.”

The woman looked at her.

“Who ordered this?”

The cashier shrugged.

“Paid already.”

“By who?”

“No name. Just the order.”

The man in the grey coat turned slightly.

The woman could feel him now.

Not looking.

Waiting.

There is a difference.

She picked up the plate.

It was warm.

Of course it was warm.

That offended her most of all.

The voice in her ear sharpened.

“Leave it.”

She should have.

She knew that.

Leaving was clean.

Leaving was smart.

Leaving kept people alive.

But the plate sat in her hands like a memory that had crossed borders without permission.

And Elijah had always hidden the secret where she least wanted to look.

Her eyes moved over the potatoes.

Nothing.

The peppers.

Nothing.

The sauce.

Nothing.

Then the first sausage.

Her breath caught.

A laugh rose in her throat, small and broken and entirely inappropriate.

Because after all these years, after all the running and training and names she had worn like borrowed coats, some part of her was still the girl behind the community hall asking where he had hidden the surprise.

And some part of Elijah was still the boy grinning beside her, proud of the one thing he knew how to do.

Feed what hurt.

She heard his voice before she remembered the words.

The secret is in the…

“Sausage,” she whispered.

The man in the grey coat moved.

So did she.

body.title: Returning to my first love: Splinterlands
body.body:
I am in the airplane, ready to take off and I am browsing my communities feeds on mobile. And while I have joined quite a few big communities on the Hive blockchain, what I have observed in these bearish times is that Splinterlands is the most active one. And when I hear such music and I feel there is a party going on in Splinterlands I say to myself: you must go there! So here I am with a Splinterlands post in quite a while. And to tell you the truth, I am quite happy seeing this project alive and kicking even in crypto bearish times. I hope the party will never stop as this game and the community around it has brought us so much joy and an escape from every day's life problems. Escaping into such a wonderful fantasy realm is always positive and along with the fun getting out of it, I like also the crypto earnings angle. What can be better than having fun and earning? Not any or many things.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/behiver/23tvW8WM9iTdx4381c8owyXZUfRbCFPbzEXACHBHuTdtRiDy1U8qygwxxZm5dMPTmF4YL.png)

I am yet to rediscover Splinterlands and all the developments done to it since my last playing it, but I want in this post just to rant about getting back to it and the community around it. And all or most of us know that Splinterlands transcended the real of just a game into a real web3 crypto ecosystem. Having its foundation on the Hive blockchain distinguishes it from any other games and is what made us devoted players and supporters if it. The novelty of a different mindset when playing games and truly owning assets in it is still strong and will be a strong feature of it. Maybe this has helped with its longevity and still kicking ass in the blockchain space.

Nevertheless the team behind Splinterlands is amazing and without some bright brains from there, this project would long time ago have been vanished. I would actually have been proud to work in such a team based in my real life experiences a d the knowledge I have in software building domain. A development team close to its community which is also attentive to incoming feedback, is a great recipe for a long lasting project. And like I said, I hope this will not stop anytime soon.

https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/behiver/23tH1CQve2wBDLiEciMuJguRW7BAX6Vn1JVo5oQ1NqpvrMhtgCbFs1BteWrZCi9roRiSA.png

Splinterlands is already part of Hive blockchain DNA and history. This game and community stood with it even when the hardfork happened, so it is hard to overlook the core values that they have. A great symbiosis push both worlds forward, even without crossing helping hands. Ans this is not necessarily a bad thing as o e growth pulls the other, without interfering within anyone governance path. The independence of projects even from the ecosystem they are running on ensure their own destiny while maybe affecting each other in a positive way. I hope to see both Hive and Splinterlands grow stronger and get market recognition as well. And until that happens, I will just keep at it! 😉

body.title: A Gentle Reminder for Anyone Fighting Silent Battles.
body.body:
From what I've seen, heard, and experienced personally, there's something I've come to realize. And even though we often just brush it off, it doesn't change the reality of things. Now, the thing is that a lot of us are actually facing real life situations, fighting battles and going through a lot behind the cameras/behind our screens.


https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/betheloji12/Eq9XDB9g8ge1JNuuouhTdN6h8yauoGHAVyrFkU1w8xFKZ5bDo9zCMX3346rSKvCKzSP.jpg





I won't be sharing anybody's story for secrecy sake, but I was prompted to write this after the discussion I had with someone just few days ago. She discussed a lot of things with me and I can't help but share some of my realities and predicaments with her too.


That was when it hit me the most, that a lot of us are just here online laughing, chatting, posting, taking pictures, and trying to act like everything is fine, but deep down, a lot of us are actually not fine, we are tired, sick, and exhausted.



Life itself is not easy, and having to also level up into the adulthood stage is another weight on its own. Responsibilities begin to choke, expectations rise, a lot of things happening around, young ones expecting you to come through for them, parents expecting certain things from you, while you're also trying to figure out life yourself. Honestly, it is not easy, its something I can very well relate with, it is my reality at the moment as well. And if you're a Nigerian, it will even hit you more, talk of the insecurity in our land, the high cost of living, the pressure and all, even those who we know to be rich and doing well for themselves are getting affected, how much more WE.



This is not to say only Nigerians are facing things, no, not at all. All around the globe people are facing, battling and struggling with one thing or the other. Just that its different for everyone, and we can't even say one is bigger than the other. Some are dealing with heartbreak, some battling sicknesses, some mourning the loss of a loved one, some smiling outside and crying inside, some......a lot that I can't keep on mentioning.




And with all of that, what some just needs is a listening ear. Not an advice or money or anything, they just need someone who can listen to them and maybe give them some encouragement. Which was what I gave to the lady I mentioned earlier. Someone who would see them, who can relate with them, who will understand them and not judge them... someone who will give them a bit of a spark to keep going and not give up.


So, I thought it best to do so here as well. Just to remind y'all of something that's simple, but important and deep.

Please, don't give up on yourself.

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/betheloji12/EokbA3zJqvn89cac93iXCNT5GrYE4uhmeNFcr3nZSemBr26xmAbUkKk46uXYbe3VWLv.jpg


I know the road is hilly, slippery and full of stuffs that could make you want to stop going, but please don't stop. One things I always remind myself of is that, it won't rain forever. Yea, no matter how long it takes, the rain will stop and the sky will become clear. So, this season you're in as well will end, just keep your hopes alive. The fact that you're still here means your life has meaning, there's strength inside of you, and that you will definitely do exploit.




Whatever it is you're going through is just a part of your story. It is not the end. Just take things one at a time, don't rush, don't push yourself too hard, rest if you need to, cry if you must, but don't ever think of quitting. Wipe those tears, come out of that thought and go harder.


I'm rooting for you, and I don't just believe, but I'm sure lines will fall in pleasant places for you. It might not look like it now, but you just be patient and watch.


It's a new week. So, go again this week, keep your hopes alive and never give in to any negative thoughts.

The data does not lie. The blockchain does not blink.

*What are you protecting?*

Is it the platform? Or is it your position within it?
Is it the community? Or is it the clique that controls it?
Is it the truth? Or is it the comfort of a lie that has paid your bills?

To pretend ignorance in the face of overwhelming evidence is not innocence. It is complicity. It is the quiet nod that allows the machinery of suppression to keep turning. It is the averted gaze that lets the garden wither while you claim to be tending it.

You can keep lying. You can keep pretending. You can keep defending the indefensible.

body.title: Why Flores Should Be On Every Traveler’s Bucket List
body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmUM3fcMAegqQU3vpf2jUdGZipWfrVhokJfzxKBLm222ok/1000705795.jpg
Some places are beautiful.
Some places feel unforgettable.
But Flores, Indonesia… feels like an entirely different world.
Recently, I uploaded a short travel video to 3Speak showcasing several incredible destinations across Flores — and honestly, the more I explore this island, the more I realize how underrated it still is globally.
From untouched beaches and ancient traditional villages to volcanic landscapes and mountains above the clouds, Flores offers a rare kind of beauty that feels both wild and peaceful at the same time.
🎥 Watch the full travel video here:
https://3speak.tv/shorts?v=yordan96/780yl2np

Where Is Flores?
  https://img.leopedia.io/DQmSmN4Q26c6RamjtWVnt9KuMt9deofLfip7a9ZnZoptiHn/1000705807.jpg 


Flores is an island located in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia.
While Bali often gets most of the international attention, Flores quietly holds some of the most breathtaking natural scenery in Southeast Asia.
And unlike overcrowded tourist destinations, many parts of Flores still feel authentic, peaceful, and deeply connected to nature and local culture.

Padar Island — One Of The Most Beautiful Views In Indonesia
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmV5mAXVZwwDjHYmThRUB5Rk6ohhqrD3LNXaeo4dDH49BW/1000705781.jpg 

One of the first places featured in the video is Padar Island.
The moment you reach the top viewpoint, it honestly feels unreal.
Massive hills rise above turquoise waters, creating one of the most iconic landscapes in Indonesia.
The contrast between the dry golden hills and the bright blue ocean makes the entire place look almost cinematic.
For travelers who love hiking, photography, or drone footage, this place is absolutely paradise.

Wae Rebo — A Village Above The Clouds
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmSjanybCY57vReKq93EhsoSrWMrTWDtwXt7jSg99DAw6A/1000705797.jpg 

Another unforgettable destination is Wae Rebo.
This traditional village sits high in the mountains and is surrounded by forests and clouds.
What makes Wae Rebo special is not only the scenery, but also the culture.
The traditional cone-shaped houses, the peaceful atmosphere, and the connection between the local people and nature create an experience that feels deeply human and timeless.
It reminds us that modern life is not the only way to live.
Sometimes simplicity itself becomes luxury.

Kelimutu Lake — The Famous Three-Colored Crater Lakes
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmTyyPMWAeCMjzkyyuLuH1oU28DqpUPytHZWUTcps9vWiW/1000705803.jpg 

Flores is also home to Kelimutu Lake, one of Indonesia’s most unique natural wonders.
These volcanic crater lakes are famous because their colors can change over time due to natural chemical reactions.
Sometimes blue.
Sometimes green.
Sometimes dark brown or black.
Standing there during sunrise feels surreal.
The silence, the cold air, and the volcanic landscape create an atmosphere that feels almost spiritual.

Pink Beach — Nature Doing Something Rare
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmQCL272uUiq84CfdM2mxMAEc14wbCBEoUm6m2RkviqJBU/1000705805.jpg 

Yes… the sand is actually pink.
Pink Beach is one of the rarest beaches in the world, created by tiny red coral fragments mixing with white sand.
The water is crystal clear, making it perfect for:
snorkeling
swimming
drone photography
or simply relaxing quietly by the ocean.
Places like this remind people why traveling matters.
Not to escape life completely…
but to reconnect with wonder again.
Flores Is More Than Just A Destination
Personally, I think Flores offers something modern cities are slowly losing.
Peace.
Space to breathe.
Real human connection.
And a reminder that nature still has the power to humble us.
In today’s world where stress, noise, and endless digital distractions dominate daily life, places like Flores feel increasingly valuable emotionally — not only visually.
Why More Travelers Should Visit Flores
I genuinely believe Flores has massive tourism potential globally because it combines:
beaches
mountains
volcanoes
culture
traditional villages
marine beauty
and adventure tourism
all in one island.
And unlike some overcrowded destinations, Flores still feels raw and authentic.
For travelers searching for:
meaningful experiences
hidden gems
cinematic landscapes
or peaceful escapes
Flores deserves serious attention.
Final Thoughts
After creating this video, one thing became very clear to me:
Flores is not just a place people visit.
It is a place people remember.
And maybe that is what makes travel truly meaningful.
Not simply seeing beautiful places…
but feeling changed after experiencing them.
If you ever have the opportunity to visit Indonesia, I honestly think Flores should be near the top of your list.
Because some places still have the power to make the world feel magical again.

body.title: Some People Don’t Burn in Sunlight, They Burn in Time
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmT8JfLAafWgbAJCEsHBQbHCcc4jBuJjsajpKnGfYkVtLP/1779611394148.jpg)

Those who suddenly turned pale…
They once had colors too.
They used to laugh, make noise, and be the loudest people in gatherings. But life slowly started taking away their light, and one day people only noticed how much they had changed.
Honestly, I have also gone through a phase where I would look at myself in the mirror and feel surprised. Even after sleeping enough, the tiredness under my eyes never disappeared. People would ask, “Are you okay? You don’t look the same anymore.”
And I would just smile, because not every pain can be explained with words.
Some exhaustion is not physical,
it comes from responsibilities.
Some pain is not illness,
it is silent stress.
I once had a friend who was always smiling. He was the soul of every gathering. Then suddenly he stopped meeting people. Later I found out that family problems, work pressure, and disappointment from close people were slowly destroying him from inside. From the outside he still looked “fine,” but in reality he was breaking a little more every single day.
Life does not steal a person’s colors in one day.
It happens slowly.
Sometimes by taking away sleep,
sometimes by stealing peace,
and sometimes through the people from whom we expected the most.
We often judge people too quickly and say, “This person has changed. They are not the same anymore.”
But maybe life never allowed them to stay the same.
Maybe time changed them without their permission.
Now whenever I see a quiet person, I pay attention, because I know every silence hides a battle. Some people scream their pain out loud, and some slowly fade into pale colors… 💔

body.title: [ESP/ENG] El impacto sicólogico de los apagones eléctricos / The psychological impact of power outages
body.body:
**Una introducción necesaria **

Vivimos en una era donde la electricidad es mucho más que un lujo: es el sostén de nuestras rutinas, el trabajo, el estudio, la comunicación y el descanso. Sin embargo, desde hace varios meses, en mi país, enfrentamos a diario una realidad agotadora: los apagones eléctricos recurrentes. Mientras se habla de pérdidas económicas y daños a electrodomésticos, rara vez se menciona el devastador impacto psicológico que estas interrupciones generan en la salud mental de las personas. 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV979cBSwM8hdheyr9e4ckAGd5CZwN5qWFkQvJzKsiyEF/1779514694668.jpg)



A continuación, les dejo algunas de las consecuencias menos visibles, pero igualmente graves, de estos apagones eléctricos.

**Estrés crónico y vigilancia permanente**

Cuando los cortes de luz son impredecibles, el cerebro entra en un estado de vigilancia total. No saber si en los próximos minutos habrá un apagón, o si durará horas, activa el sistema de alerta constante. El cuerpo se mantiene tenso, esperando lo inesperado. Esta respuesta, útil ante peligros inminentes, se vuelve tóxica cuando se prolonga durante semanas o meses. El resultado es un estrés crónico que agota física y mentalmente: dolores de cabeza, fatiga extrema, irritabilidad y sensación de estar siempre al borde del colapso.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfKx5HcdaH5hudSeQFiY5mV7qp3ucpDJdLNQZSDTMxW7e/1779590628620.jpg)


**Alteraciones del sueño**

La falta de electricidad no solo apaga las luces, también altera uno de los pilares de la salud: el sueño. Sin ventiladores o aire acondicionado, sin ruido blanco de un aparato electrónico, o simplemente por la angustia de quedarnos sin conexión o  incomunicados, muchas personas desarrollan insomnio. Dormir se convierte en una lucha: cuesta conciliar el sueño, se interrumpe el descanso y es imposible mantener rutinas regulares. La privación del sueño, a su vez, potencia todos los demás problemas psicológicos.

**Cuando la mente se rinde**

Quizás uno de los efectos más profundos es la indefensión aprendida. Después de sufrir apagones repetidos sin poder hacer nada para evitarlos, las personas comienzan a sentir que no tienen control sobre su entorno. Se instala una sensación de desesperanza: para qué planificar, si igual todo se va a interrumpir. 

Esta pérdida de agencia personal puede derivar en apatía, falta de motivación e incluso depresión. Dejar de intentar soluciones porque nunca funcionan es una herida silenciosa en la autoestima y la resiliencia.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRjJNq5VsyKzsXPEKTQaMng8HqYySykrHn4iRkSXqfJCm/1779551244263.jpg)


**Vivir pensando en el próximo apagón **

Quienes sufren apagones constantes desarrollan una ansiedad anticipatoria difícil de sobrellevar. La mente se llena de preguntas: ¿se irá la luz justo cuando esté viendo un eento deportivo?, ¿se dañará la comida del refrigerador?, ¿qué haré si mi familiar necesita oxígeno y no hay energía?. Esta carga mental pesa como una mochila de piedras. El futuro se experimenta como una amenaza, y la persona queda atrapada en un bucle de preocupación que consume energía mental y emocional.

**Tensiones familiares y sociales**

La falta de electricidad no ocurre en el vacío. Afecta la convivencia. El aumento de la irritabilidad por el cansancio, la impotencia y el calor genera discusiones más frecuentes. En los hogares, pequeños roces se convierten en explosiones. Padres e hijos, parejas o hermanos terminan peleando por cosas triviales, cuando en realidad el enemigo común es la situación de apagones. Las tensiones sociales también se extienden al vecindario o al trabajo: baja la paciencia, aumentan los malentendidos y se erosiona la cohesión comunitaria.

**La mente que se nubla**

Por último, pero no menos grave, está el impacto en las funciones cognitivas. Quien vive con estrés crónico, sueño interrumpido y ansiedad constante experimenta problemas de concentración, memoria y toma de decisiones. Cuesta seguir una conversación, leer un libro o terminar una tarea sencilla. La productividad se desploma tanto en el estudio como en el trabajo. Y lo peor es que la persona a menudo se culpa a sí misma, sin entender que su cerebro está funcionando en modo supervivencia, no en modo rendimiento.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWxGKf92nhfF7wo1S3HGVfUwwbVfwDYvb7RqBqCA3U4nA/1779590508311.jpg)


**Un comentario final** 


Los apagones frecuentes no son solo una falla técnica o un inconveniente logístico. Son un factor de riesgo psicosocial que merece atención urgente. El gobierno y la empresa eléctrica deben reconocer que garantizar un suministro estable de electricidad es también una medida de salud pública. 

Mientras tanto, es vital que las personas afectadas busquen apoyo psicológico, construyan redes de contención vecinal y practiquen estrategias de manejo de la incertidumbre. Porque cuando la luz se va, no podemos permitir que también se apague la esperanza.

**ENGLISH** 





**An Introduction necessary **

We live in a world where electricity is much more than a luxury: it is the backbone of our routines, work, study, communication, and rest. However, for several months now, we have been facing an exhausting reality every day: recurring power outages. While economic losses and damage to household appliances are discussed, the devastating psychological impact these interruptions have on people's mental health is rarely mentioned.



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV979cBSwM8hdheyr9e4ckAGd5CZwN5qWFkQvJzKsiyEF/1779514694668.jpg)


Below, I outline some of the less visible but equally serious consequences of these power outages.

**Chronic Stress and Permanent Vigilance**

When power cuts are unpredictable, the brain enters a state of total vigilance. Not knowing whether an outage will happen in the next few minutes, or how long it will last, triggers a constant alert system. The body remains tense, waiting for the unexpected. This response, useful in the face of imminent danger, becomes toxic when it lasts for weeks or months. The result is chronic stress that exhausts you physically and mentally: headaches, extreme fatigue, irritability, and a feeling of being constantly on the verge of collapse.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfKx5HcdaH5hudSeQFiY5mV7qp3ucpDJdLNQZSDTMxW7e/1779590628620.jpg)


**Sleep Disruptions**

Lack of electricity not only turns off the lights, it also disrupts one of the pillars of health: sleep. Without fans or air conditioning, without the white noise of an electronic device, or simply due to the anxiety of being disconnected or out of touch, many people develop insomnia. Sleeping becomes a struggle: falling asleep is difficult, rest is interrupted, and maintaining regular routines becomes impossible. Sleep deprivation, in turn, amplifies all other psychological problems.

**When the Mind Gives Up**

Perhaps one of the most profound effects is learned helplessness. After suffering repeated power outages without being able to do anything to prevent them, people begin to feel they have no control over their environment. A sense of hopelessness sets in: why make plans, if everything is going to be interrupted anyway.

This loss of personal agency can lead to apathy, lack of motivation, and even depression. Giving up trying to find solutions because they never work is a silent wound to self-esteem and resilience.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRjJNq5VsyKzsXPEKTQaMng8HqYySykrHn4iRkSXqfJCm/1779551244263.jpg)


**Living in Fear of the Next Outage**

Those who suffer constant power outages develop a form of anticipatory anxiety that is hard to bear. The mind fills with questions: Will the power go out just as I'm watching a sports event? Will the food in the fridge spoil? What will I do if my relative needs oxygen and there's no electricity? This mental burden weighs like a backpack full of stones. The future is experienced as a threat, and the person becomes trapped in a loop of worry that consumes mental and emotional energy.

**Family and Social Tensions**

Lack of electricity does not happen in a vacuum. It affects daily coexistence. Increased irritability due to tiredness, helplessness, and heat leads to more frequent arguments. At home, small frictions turn into explosions. Parents and children, couples, or siblings end up fighting over trivial things, when the real enemy is the situation of power outages. Social tensions also spread to the neighborhood or workplace: patience wears thin, misunderstandings increase, and community cohesion erodes.

**The Fogged Mind**

Last but not least, there is the impact on cognitive functions. Those living with chronic stress, disrupted sleep, and constant anxiety experience problems with concentration, memory, and decision-making. It's hard to follow a conversation, read a book, or complete a simple task. Productivity plummets, both in studying and at work. And worst of all, the person often blames themselves, not understanding that their brain is functioning in survival mode, not performance mode.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWxGKf92nhfF7wo1S3HGVfUwwbVfwDYvb7RqBqCA3U4nA/1779590508311.jpg)


**A Final Comment**

Frequent power outages are not just a technical failure or a logistical inconvenience. They are a psychosocial risk factor that deserves urgent attention. The government and the electric company must recognize that guaranteeing a stable electricity supply is also a public health measure.

In the meantime, it is vital that affected individuals seek psychological support, build neighborhood support networks, and practice strategies for managing uncertainty. Because when the lights go out, we cannot allow hope to go out as well.

body.title: Card Expo in Graz - Pokémon, One Piece, and financial ruin
body.body:
Finally… the day came. 
What day, you ask? Card Expo day! And this year it was in Graz. Sometimes life is nice and the chaos happens basically two steps away from home. Ok, maybe more like 10 km away… *(and no, I still have no idea how many miles that is)* 😊 

At first I called it a party. After spending 6 hours there, I realized “party” is maybe not the right word. My feet were filing complaints against me for walking around that long. 😔


![IMG_9610.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcDuPUFeCJQsq7yhzEpHehiF9uxWqx4jK5mQqAKNmK191/IMG_9610.jpeg)



But let’s start from the beginning. 💪

For a while now, we’ve been collecting cards. You know… those shiny little pieces of cardboard that somehow destroy your wallet and make you happy at the same time. My husband actually started with Splinterlands, so digital cards. He saw “future investment.” I saw “fun game.” Big difference apparently…🤔 


![IMG_9817.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYyJtPc8mE7Quyebpn9X6xri8rC9HXbuNra2jV8FZj9JS/IMG_9817.jpeg)



I honestly never cared much about tracking prices, watching markets, buying low, selling high, and staring at graphs all day. That’s his thing. My job was simple…point at cards and say, *“I want this one.”* Way easier. Way more fun. ☺️

Then one day we were in a store, saw Pokémon packs, and thought, *“Why not?”* 
Well… that “why not” became a habit very fast. 

At first we didn’t even open the packs. We just threw them into a closet and forgot about them for years. But of course, my husband’s brain never rests. Eventually he started checking card prices online and almost had a heart attack when he saw how expensive some cards were. Suddenly opening a booster pack felt like buying a lottery ticket. Maybe there’s a card inside worth 20,000 euros. Probably not… but maybe…🤔🤔

And then Netflix released One Piece. 

My husband already knew the story because he watched the anime as a kid, but I didn’t know anything about it. After watching season one, I was completely hooked. And then his brain went into full detective mode again. He started researching the One Piece Card Game market and realized collectors are absolutely insane. The game exploded in popularity and now competes with giants like Pokémon and Magic. Honestly impressive. 

And somehow… he dragged me into it too. 

Because I discovered something very important…ordering cards is **FUN**. Waiting for them to arrive, opening the package, holding the card, admiring the artwork like it belongs in a museum… amazing. Have you SEEN how beautiful some of those cards are?! They shine!! My simple visual brain is very happy 😊 

And yes… I also started paying attention to prices because apparently cardboard can magically double in value overnight. Totally normal behavior. 😏

Anyway… this was supposed to be about the Card Expo before I started writing a whole love story about shiny cards 😊 






So, the card show was in Graz, at Seifenfabrik, which honestly was the perfect place for it. Huge building, cool atmosphere, and enough space for what felt like half of Europe showing up. 


![IMG_9614.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaeVR9rf5eLYK2JpUeE7Y2ScFDNszPMdDe4y3int3y14T/IMG_9614.jpeg)



We had never been to an event like this before. We weren’t selling anything, just there to buy cards and experience the madness. 

For people who don’t know, a card trading show is basically a giant event where people buy, sell, trade, and admire collectible cards. Sports cards, Pokémon, Magic, Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece, Disney, Marvel, Star Wars… basically paradise for someone like me because everything is in one place and I don’t need to spend 7 hours online searching different websites!😊 

The show started at 10 a.m., and we thought we were smart arriving at 9:30. 

Cute. 


![IMG_9598.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmV1HWoXJtUpq9pjQQpSf5TMeQwYWJ4wSKGob7ZZn7EgFe/IMG_9598.jpeg)



There was already no parking. Security was directing traffic. That should have been our first warning. 

**Then we saw the line.**



![IMG_9602.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSuUr9HCseriZYByxPU1cQ6WCGaGyrgCmTU4GujTv9kNs/IMG_9602.jpeg)


At least 100 people were already waiting before the doors even opened. I turned around after a few minutes and realized the line behind us was HUGE. People everywhere. All ages, different countries, different languages… I honestly couldn’t believe it. 


![IMG_9606.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNuXVtG3GiEm55mudu9iF4dnRPgzu9DpfBkchCZpkjhEt/IMG_9606.jpeg)



And when we finally got inside? 
Absolute chaos. 


![IMG_9619.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVwiMC7uTTs2xJLsLqfrpjWwiWhJnot1kmVzVXAoW3M8c/IMG_9619.jpeg)

![IMG_9617.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfYLSrpFiz7c1Lo8MkdBQMoXyrVKwE9t5AFiWRNweZCLB/IMG_9617.jpeg)


So many people. So many sellers. So many binders full of cards. It was almost impossible to even reach the tables because crowds were packed around them nonstop. Every time you finally got space to look through cards, you had to decide FAST. Because if you walked away thinking, *“Oh, I’ll come back later,”* congratulations…the card was already gone 10 minutes later. 


![IMG_9629.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTpvUZ5GX1ZDeUDVv27ZDnu5AoT2DchrB6QsXZjzwXzd4/IMG_9629.jpeg)


After two hours of walking in circles through crowds, I was dying from thirst. So naturally… beer 😊 


![IMG_9637.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRXWqu4SdNXYj3wXUFKLQwQUXfLxfKhQDyxrvEwyQnMqV/IMG_9637.jpeg)



We also made the beginner mistake of thinking the crowd would calm down later. 

Nope. 

It somehow became MORE crowded. 


![IMG_9639.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmerMvJNS2w2UfYZH2gunvvsbnRz6KyYXM3A7ruZLTybqi/IMG_9639.jpeg)


At one point my only mission was: do not lose my husband in this sea of humans. Luckily he had a giant red backpack, so finding him wasn’t too difficult. 

What shocked me the most were the prices. Some cards cost 15,000 euros… and people were actually buying them. Every time we came back to certain sellers, expensive cards had disappeared. Sold. 


![IMG_9626.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZemQ3qVAyA1cd35T9upL5fz3ZK16opbUN56qaQYSTb7d/IMG_9626.jpeg)

![IMG_9631.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXp7WN6y1YZaozokgCcgfA1dkm5GV69SVi9HERuezSH1A/IMG_9631.jpeg)

![IMG_9632.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeraAZdubY1WTunQj7AnY7K5QExoy1GGgJvH3jxyEnw1D/IMG_9632.jpeg)



Outside, my husband started talking to some collectors carrying giant cases full of cards. One guy casually had a collection worth over 200,000 euros. EXCUSE ME?! How do you walk around with that much value in a suitcase?! I would be terrified. Someone could just grab it and run. 


![IMG_9645.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTqXf2yVEqqmtcws1QMN3YGTUTLYzFdSyDhNE4ZaUDduj/IMG_9645.jpeg)



Ok… maybe not in my case. I’d survive about 30 seconds of running before collapsing dramatically 😊 

But still. Crazy. 

After 6 hours we were completely exhausted, our feet were dead, and somehow the crowd was STILL growing. 


![IMG_9643.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNXUdTffNkan2jeECrf1tteRyq1M3hjE2RxjsJWrDA7z4/IMG_9643.jpeg)

![IMG_9648.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPuyKmh8FKNLQsQP2VswgKHacCYYEvr6qdEBe7SeGFaFs/IMG_9648.jpeg)



So we finally decided we were done. We bought some cards, a few booster packs, and escaped with what was left of our energy. 

But honestly? 
It was an amazing experience. 


![IMG_9633.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmR7N87xWFbujmytQWRG5zsqnL4YUgbNPCGqMWkvjGQhzF/IMG_9633.jpeg)

![IMG_9635.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNnMfgGMLMDkow1DQGxznFKbtp587s3jZK8f5i9uszReZ/IMG_9635.jpeg)

![IMG_9641.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNgb4iKspNFy66Awxf5qvT3RxquKZg1489MSXxGgtmaL6/IMG_9641.jpeg)



I truly didn’t expect these events to be this huge and this popular. 

And we definitely learned something for next time: 

Buy the freaking VIP ticket. Arrive early. And maybe…*(just maybe)*…you’ll actually get a chance to look through cards peacefully without being pushed around by 500 excited collectors! 😏


![IMG_9650.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmY3Ec47s5Xia36Q9EMcpf251CooRytpWe69ayZd7AKGZF/IMG_9650.jpeg)



With love, @tinabrezpike ❤️

body.body: > https://img.leopedia.io/DQmX5i6UXtWXZy9KEg7etbwNFqeV3cwYpBNppDdrnwqGHHy/1000070262.png Hello friends, I hope you are doing well. Welcome to my new post. Currently, in this age of the internet, online fraud has increased the most in our world. In fact, ever since digital devices came into the hands of people, online scammers have awakened. In our country, we sometimes see on TV how people are being cheated. When they give everything to these cheaters through their own mistake or unknowingly, they lose a lot. In fact, it is very sad to see these people. They cannot keep their money well. They give many of their personal things to other people as a result of cheating. And in this way, people are being cheated day after day in our country. To avoid online fraud, we must take various steps. We must not share our personal information with anyone. We will always keep our social media protected. Many people call us and ask for passwords, we will never give them passwords. The most online fraud in our country is seen in the field of mobile banking. I have never been a victim of online fraud in my life. However, I have seen many people around me who have been victims of such a thing. In our country, fraud is most common in mobile banking and social media, especially bKash, Nagad, Rocket, etc. For this, there are many fraudsters who take thousands of rupees from ordinary people. In our country, the most illiterate people are the ones who fall prey to these online frauds. Without realizing it, they give their various OTPs and passwords to people. At this time, fraudsters show them various lures. Especially the lure of money is the most. As a result, these people give their mobile and personal information. In my opinion, it is necessary to inform the general public about these matters through propaganda. No one should share any password or OTP with anyone. Do not give their devices to other people. There are many people in our society who are victims of online fraud from their own relatives and neighbors at times. Tropic\\.title: Yay, Finally! Our First Water Spinach Harvest
Tropic\\.body: > Happy Sunday Hivers! ## One of the easiest plants to grow is water spinach. Unlike other vegetable plants that require intensive care and constant attention, this one grows well as long as it gets enough water and sunlight. ## ![IMG_4205.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/245cKt83GPqmrAcrFM46iTseFQQteknxqVxwdyjxj9rZ4ovrgwELQWrsM8Vfu8iQh8DSZ.jpeg) ## Water spinach is also very quick to harvest. Just about a month after planting, it already grows big enough to be harvested, so you can enjoy eating what you planted right away. Unlike other vegetables that take several months to mature, this one grows really fast and is very convenient to grow. ## ![IMG_4203.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/23vhuMJaAmyLhfwXaeVtXhREhFSXLPMvfPFuQe9kXrW3jLkrCPMtdkfBjJDbpGqqjkYUG.jpeg) ## Finally, we have harvested our water spinach. This is our very first harvest. It feels really different and fulfilling when you grow your own food, because aside from the joy of knowing it is chemical-free, you also don’t waste it since it is the result of your own hard work and effort in planting it. ## ![IMG_4200.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/23uQp4zk4mHS2MHRByE3DYxnPkwYXdMfrwKTHak5HLya9P3Yx2DAKEFrBJjZe8pU21cvK.jpeg) ## ![IMG_4252.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/23wC7UpPeVYdpaaRiJLmVN7y2RjkUe7RfEcBC3eBrG4mu3QJz9FXVomLd3Z3aSKyg23iz.jpeg) ## After harvesting our water spinach, we cooked it right away. It tastes much better when it is freshly cooked. Since we already had ground pork in the fridge, we simply cooked the water spinach adobo-style and added the pork. Of course, it helped us save on our meal since we didn’t need to buy water spinach. ## ![IMG_4206.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/EoptTfqPrEXgtnWLL1sZ5ku2gCHn3kNCQ3c4yZiuqBp5fCWDHc7AUiWxPjgaBMt5kJm.jpeg) ## Overall, this small experience made us appreciate gardening even more. It may look simple, but growing your own food really brings a different kind of happiness and satisfaction. We also learned that even a small space or a simple plant like water spinach can already give something useful for the family. It helps us save money, eat healthier, and enjoy fresh food straight from our garden. Hopefully, this is just the start, and we can grow more vegetables in the future. It feels good to know that with a little effort and patience, we can already harvest something from what we planted. ##

>

Thank you for reading and see you on my next blog. Cheers!

[03:11.04] Rip a hole into our friendship
[03:13.63] This is how it's been, how it always will be
[03:18.69] You think you're above me (you think you're above me)
[03:21.79] But now I'm here to envy
[03:23.99] Four words to choke upon.
[03:26.26] Look (look) at me now!
[03:28.60]

Tropic\\.title: Cuando el lente se convierte en poesía | [ES/EN]
Tropic\\.body:
> ¡Hola seres de luz! El día se torna prolijo en opciones culturales en mi ciudad. Dentro de las opciones que hay, quiero compartirles a ustedes una singular exposición de fotografía inaugurada este lunes reciente a la que pude asistir y que disfruté al máximo. *** |![176670.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23xyQzQz6JFM5Z1NCa15fehh4ifm11NqboXEWZnpb3HFtkMRY6zknGL7ZVwEuTgzYBugs.jpg)|![176671.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23wC9ddNwKN4XmzjqJEuhQrGucJ2ewhrsUgWYnw7tiYRGmfgxBn9beVY1mXgtA5dYPLAY.jpg)|![176672.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Eopsvg1rcjdRNk6xTR1d2PhutFHdn5RLV9sNhazMKtmXQhSfMAwUQ2SiRQrwuTPxCf6.jpg)| |-|-|-| *** ¿Por qué digo singular?, se preguntarán. Pues resulta que estas fotografías, cuyo autor es Julio Valdés Méliz, vienen acompañadas de poemas que otro gran artista nuestro nos regala de modo genuino. Hablo de José Antonio Fulgueiras Domínguez, quien nos ofrece sus poemas pirograbados en trozos de yagua, ese material que desprenden las palmas reales y que identifican a la raíz de la cultura campesina, autóctona de nuestros campos y zonas más intrincadas del país. ***
![176673.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EoiVkqLgFeZ6YFYaJG3ZQsF5x2oT1vcvUXfatDsrPLBTKNgcUViy8qCaJn2PLD8C478.jpg)
*** Además, la inauguración tuvo otro regalo al público asistente: la presencia de José Manuel Silverio y sus hijos amenizando el instante con la poética de las décimas al más puro ritmo de las tonadas campesinas a tono con lo expuesto. *** ![176674.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EpEJkaAmSLnHNgwyGARcCEuVHBuL4Rx5FYcKctDXgzj82b47QFiU8cfqS4SeAMAjarS.jpg)|![176675.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EpA2XRUXRZcwitTiJU3bHq2nE1KhDcLGJ7wUp9w2HhRFoKVnG7NJQrpDeQbJcGr4yV2.jpg)|![176676.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Ep3fDV31Ama6oobY1TQ2uWSCqFxn5ZhTfX2QkzE7TNYaz9F1XvXUxNr4wszu7E2aHKy.jpg)| |-|-|-| ***
![176677.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Ep1Xom9ZrF2qHCU95YQDtcfAxeujHRCtWkJArAKrAUY5c8egTAtEWX39mBM6qEbUQF5.jpg)
*** Los autores de la exposición, Julio y Fulgueiras (como mejor se le conoce en el ámbito cultural), comparten raíces campesinas y a ello quisieron rendir merecido y necesario homenaje. *** ![176678.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EonmTxzorhPCcPSJTkxPsd8heWZoT7uMiCkH7aRd1voBn4mT2u2ozYd7WwE62JgJxuv.jpg)|![176680.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Ep5nBF4n5HCK9xHc1pZe1Tbdp3kzuqmEtb3C4nyyJv1mgWBbxmmF1fABqRDgKSd5t7k.jpg)|![176682.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Eou9BGPUZTgMFUb6xYCDP6kc9edem6J4uHu6fMiV5tRLq9d5jtdkucerpm3mioVgCfs.jpg)| |-|-|-| *** Julio, el fotógrafo, ha desarrollado una mirada artística a través de la fotografía participando en diversas exposiciones colectivas anteriormente. ***
![176683.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EoCj3nCs1NcNq7fTUVvKamRvB2TfCq4XsLy7iBTVxKM927UcNQ2CYy1z93po6qxC2DX.jpg)
*** Por su parte, Fulgueiras, el poeta, ha publicado más de treinta libros de diferentes géneros literarios, obteniendo disímiles premios en su trayectoria como creador. *** |![176684.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EoeFr6CyfzUJ4Esdu2Sbijaee3WBW791mNNKUVAUr1ocrr8jFVwPMpC2yRF2jMC1Vw9.jpg)|![176685.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23xVH1NryRoSfYx3r2mrinTWDdZH7ZypqSKc6krEabjZmo5cuBvweNXeLNhoXJFPwyzUr.jpg)|![176687.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23ycysjaUpCjbiLGsBYwok245G4nWb4x4fVgZmMwMu6rizV4GiEkBAXE6G33B3JXHLo9d.jpg)| |-|-|-| ***
![176697.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23wC5CCVnuRWwXBXttveXUJ2LKc3jmDCoZzRhFaxKQxuYcHHkJamwcbMyysyZ9zk1VUEc.jpg)
*** Como pueden apreciar, la naturaleza y la vida campesina constituyen la inspiración común de estos artistas de la región central de Cuba. Acá sus obras (fotografías y poemas) dialogan para mantener vivas las tradiciones cubanas que, autores como Samuel Feijó y Onelio Jorge Cardozo, exploraron en su literatura costumbrista. La muestra presenta imágenes de palmas, ríos, árboles e instrumentos de labranza que envuelven y acompañan la existencia del campesino, capturando con atinada intención la esencia de su labor y su entorno. *** |![176686.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EoK7GTVTZ6fmY9PokaYnecBYY7A9bwXSqpASWDy5yMmbeAQkaBoPBsuUBm3TNg37WLg.jpg)|![176690.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Epxqny1FyHNb9Yw7ZVYUiVVDDTCrbmQJreg7hxNAVzuJDADphrEj7oDCxA8XSyLg4GB.jpg)|![176691.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EpxrmRTJfYuecruvWN1yps9yAK8yif86XqJ1tfPeRCsGdNBs4Wm5dejgvSWNzwwZHhw.jpg)| |-|-|-| ***
![176692.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23u6BGkfe9LjPx1F8iT7f3UV7HPWia7qQPxrdvaKEEhDmqnEgGDQj47sUMc4kMqbWs4Dm.jpg)
*** |![176693.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EpxqJgYmTUiuQr8Lqfe2ak7Ft6dScNUyZDckZsqNzTxYdkJhk7nBBicaXaErsqvxdrZ.jpg)|![176695.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Ep3duN5vNw3zLqEkVHuszV1Mg3EUb24qjYUnQR88Km9nJKm7hTaHKva39g2UnkgD22R.jpg)|![176696.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23xpAd6WoTwQmnosLWaj64cn5QcckCyViEBGpUNWLDJNZZpBQVYG79z4XejQmeiTwNH6p.jpg)|![176698.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EowJ73WTUNiiyuxYdr7bbifbQ4SotjGUyEnkNxRy2zv4nxgJP2h2UureaFcXWqWXAwe.jpg)|![176699.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23xKxVV3REsiC2LhGuiid5QB9f8nedVLoCGEVznnYbNX5exeQbqRe6wNM7WbV4GfD67Jh.jpg)| |-|-|-|-|-| *** El título de la exposición, Lente Rimado, refleja este diálogo entre imagen y palabra, donde el lente de la cámara y la métrica poética se entrelazan para ofrecer al espectador un recorrido por la memoria, la naturaleza y la identidad rural cubana. ***
![176700.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EppKhu3ngGxn5qhJAkn3zYZ9jN2HAadYq2vGTzx8wYSssCSwezMAJNDMUaFyDaXMwgb.jpg)
*** |![176701.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EopstbmLfztYfbgj71wbPzAahus1yhVvvrojGx9x7y8ZpMsqVdyixZSKQmZqGTgBKy2.jpg)|![176702.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Ep1XM1Gic6W9dVbuTUnBj2vxewGPeTrQovL7jqnLayjSn9AzjS8Wr5cuJUPvcgLkWGs.jpg)|![176703.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Eoptt9anRG58UwSUYAjQez2Me2wHcu8YHjDCS2Joa46p3ZWKJm86tpfwRrsPrxoKYCx.jpg)|![176704.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23w2oCrdodEFBza4mNCgHQpve9QNa9vFnW746WsC6SVdpdwCCgsWZGobUvXmyKMB25Jq1.jpg)|![176705.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23wWy7ETohheziiR49zrLnmxvfVmzfXDsdgjgW2W7wNdmmRL1N8s6ECN4ya1oCujREgGA.jpg)|![176706.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EpLfRaqt2D7uK4E7VRtDUZVw6ZrbgmRCLAb1jvyJWsRwi4onZVMavkdkiww5xhVbknh.jpg)| |-|-|-|-|-|-| ***
![176707.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EoK7DAkVDpKGMjfXTgJBF4hXfA1f3UD7pT8XEfpkaY7s6HacjNSRfJc6FXJUGxnVtZf.jpg)
*** A través de estas obras, los autores invitan a redescubrir y celebrar la riqueza cultural de Villa Clara, haciendo de cada fotografía y cada verso un homenaje al hombre y la tierra que los vio nacer. *** |![176708.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EoyPUMymAno6tynBUn6ifnsRoqL9kiYTgCr5r18JHqytEDsjxKX7MRbyd5TbisHXszJ.jpg)|![176709.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Ep7thyZpLbbxF2YBvNUYzaJvCmUguyAhfEwZBYMo984PeVfGvsBcsw8hLYyEJ1FuigC.jpg)|![176710.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23xVPAbm8pFGSZBcexs3kW4LxDMg5dHNMyHMHfMdbwxm2bhEg3kwzpttwfXJK68tcJGZJ.jpg)|![176711.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Ep1XvwRbW5tHNnx58StjsnsU1vPJyXy4wjyjBzNk5HkWu6bpA6ERSPuygaj8nyNZqVC.jpg)|![176712.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EpLfwkNEm7Vuhd8yz4krTQvzRsf9HiyqwQoePaKgNEVz45xVimrimEfzzKWus5iipHn.jpg)| |-|-|-|-|-| *** No creo preciso añadir mucho más a estas imágenes, solo queda que disfruten sus detalles y, como siempre les digo, ¡no olviden sonreír! Hasta una próxima exposición, reciba cada uno de ustedes ¡un abrazo de luz! ***
![176716.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EqL8pCR5QzPNVXxEh1PXa9URBqstVhUWwxhgt94KvXqaUzsXh4jrLmu5rTKkQLXGVck.jpg)

>¡Muchas gracias por tu visita!

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYSrXVnBp3RpvNFNKeMrvQFbCxVh2pB9zNwFcCeryGNdQ/in_english_blanco_y_negro.jpg)

![176669.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EogNo5EKqG2WbxJQNdRpU4SmHdG8SgHVXwPWGmoj2VuPSwMyvEqiafZArec5eXdZjY6.jpg)
***

>

Hello, beings of light! 

The day is brimming with cultural options in my city. Among the many choices available, I want to share with you a unique photography exhibition that opened this past Monday, which I was able to attend and thoroughly enjoyed.

***

|![176670.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23xyQzQz6JFM5Z1NCa15fehh4ifm11NqboXEWZnpb3HFtkMRY6zknGL7ZVwEuTgzYBugs.jpg)|![176671.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23wC9ddNwKN4XmzjqJEuhQrGucJ2ewhrsUgWYnw7tiYRGmfgxBn9beVY1mXgtA5dYPLAY.jpg)|![176672.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Eopsvg1rcjdRNk6xTR1d2PhutFHdn5RLV9sNhazMKtmXQhSfMAwUQ2SiRQrwuTPxCf6.jpg)|  
|-|-|-|

***
Why do I say \

you might ask? Well, it turns out that these photographs, taken by Julio Valdés Méliz, are accompanied by poems that another great artist of ours has given us in a truly unique way. I'm referring to José Antonio Fulgueiras Domínguez, who offers us his poems pyrographically engraved on pieces of yagua, the bark of royal palms that represents the roots of the peasant culture native to our countryside and the most remote areas of the country. ***
![176673.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EoiVkqLgFeZ6YFYaJG3ZQsF5x2oT1vcvUXfatDsrPLBTKNgcUViy8qCaJn2PLD8C478.jpg)
*** In addition, the inauguration had another gift for the attending public: the presence of José Manuel Silverio and his sons enlivening the moment with the poetic décimas to the purest rhythm of peasant tunes in keeping with what was presented. *** ![176674.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EpEJkaAmSLnHNgwyGARcCEuVHBuL4Rx5FYcKctDXgzj82b47QFiU8cfqS4SeAMAjarS.jpg)|![176675.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EpA2XRUXRZcwitTiJU3bHq2nE1KhDcLGJ7wUp9w2HhRFoKVnG7NJQrpDeQbJcGr4yV2.jpg)|![176676.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Ep3fDV31Ama6oobY1TQ2uWSCqFxn5ZhTfX2QkzE7TNYaz9F1XvXUxNr4wszu7E2aHKy.jpg)| |-|-|-| ***
![176677.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Ep1Xom9ZrF2qHCU95YQDtcfAxeujHRCtWkJArAKrAUY5c8egTAtEWX39mBM6qEbUQF5.jpg)
*** The authors of the exhibition, Julio and Fulgueiras (as he is better known in the cultural sphere), share peasant roots and wanted to pay a deserved and necessary tribute to them. *** ![176678.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EonmTxzorhPCcPSJTkxPsd8heWZoT7uMiCkH7aRd1voBn4mT2u2ozYd7WwE62JgJxuv.jpg)|![176680.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Ep5nBF4n5HCK9xHc1pZe1Tbdp3kzuqmEtb3C4nyyJv1mgWBbxmmF1fABqRDgKSd5t7k.jpg)|![176682.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Eou9BGPUZTgMFUb6xYCDP6kc9edem6J4uHu6fMiV5tRLq9d5jtdkucerpm3mioVgCfs.jpg)| |-|-|-| *** Julio, the photographer, has developed an artistic eye through photography, having previously participated in several group exhibitions. ***
![176683.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EoCj3nCs1NcNq7fTUVvKamRvB2TfCq4XsLy7iBTVxKM927UcNQ2CYy1z93po6qxC2DX.jpg)
*** Fulgueiras, the poet, has published more than thirty books in various literary genres, receiving numerous awards throughout his career as a writer. *** |![176684.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EoeFr6CyfzUJ4Esdu2Sbijaee3WBW791mNNKUVAUr1ocrr8jFVwPMpC2yRF2jMC1Vw9.jpg)|![176685.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23xVH1NryRoSfYx3r2mrinTWDdZH7ZypqSKc6krEabjZmo5cuBvweNXeLNhoXJFPwyzUr.jpg)|![176687.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23ycysjaUpCjbiLGsBYwok245G4nWb4x4fVgZmMwMu6rizV4GiEkBAXE6G33B3JXHLo9d.jpg)| |-|-|-| ***
![176697.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23wC5CCVnuRWwXBXttveXUJ2LKc3jmDCoZzRhFaxKQxuYcHHkJamwcbMyysyZ9zk1VUEc.jpg)
*** As you can see, nature and rural life are the common inspiration for these artists from central Cuba. Here, their works (photographs and poems) engage in dialogue to keep alive the Cuban traditions that authors like Samuel Feijó and Onelio Jorge Cardozo explored in their costumbrista literature. The exhibition presents images of palm trees, rivers, trees, and farming implements that envelop and accompany the lives of farmers, capturing with keen insight the essence of their work and their environment. *** |![176686.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EoK7GTVTZ6fmY9PokaYnecBYY7A9bwXSqpASWDy5yMmbeAQkaBoPBsuUBm3TNg37WLg.jpg)|![176690.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/Epxqny1FyHNb9Yw7ZVYUiVVDDTCrbmQJreg7hxNAVzuJDADphrEj7oDCxA8XSyLg4GB.jpg)|![176691.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/EpxrmRTJfYuecruvWN1yps9yAK8yif86XqJ1tfPeRCsGdNBs4Wm5dejgvSWNzwwZHhw.jpg)| |-|-|-| ***
![176692.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/roswelborges/23u6BGkfe9LjPx1F8iT7f3UV7HPWia7qQPxrdvaKEEhDmqnEgGDQj47sUMc4kMqbWs4Dm.jpg)

Tropic\\.title: $HIVE, $BTC & ETH/BTC Technical Analysis - 24.05.2026
Tropic\\.body: I'm a bit early with my analysis post today, but it doesn't matter as the market is not doing much today, I mean there's not much momentum. However, I'd be cautious as there's a possibility for something to happen regarding the Iran situation. If an announcement is made by the US or the other party, it can move the market. Anyway, let's get started. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23t8CSPFAy7NbjF1hH5t7WpfQCxvM5GM61B8JmFeoZF7YyufpZTM6hnxgjPyeTB6cHTnD.png) The ***monthly*** chart looks a bit better compared to last week, but only compared to last week as price is trading at $0.061 at the time of writing, compared to $0.0597 last week. However, if you look at the monthly candle, you see a candle so many token holders don't want to see. We had a big move to the upside, then price literally came back to monthly open as there was no buying pressure to keep price at that level. As a trader, we trade the markets both ways, so every move is an opportunity, like was this one too, to make some money. Anyway, we still have a week till the candle close, we'll see after the candle close, but as long as we get a bullish candle (white one), I'm ok with that. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23t8CSPFC3qrkMFazf3hKYB6QuX5uyWajTjCcz3AoBeWDmiv1ueH9Zi5PArBpJq9AVnRn.png) The ***weekly*** chart look different, although it says the same thing, just in a different way. You can see the big spike we had three weeks ago, after which came the bearish candle and this week we have a bullish candle, which closes in about 17 hours. Unfortunately the big upside wick tell you that selling pressure was again dominating as it push price back to $0.061. The two levels I'd watch in case you want to trade or swap are swing low at $0.0553 and the current swing high at $0.0988, which seems miles away from where we are now. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23sxpRyy9SCb8FwQbcwnHBZeSXTHRKkESbpwDbYTtxSnUaXpABnYKqsDkfDwJ1XeKc1qW.png) On the ***daily*** time frame we had a bullish move yesterday, price swept liquidity till $0.0688 and then sold off. Today we have no momentum as price has printed a doji so far, which means indecision. Price needs to close above $0.0643, to set the bullish order block, then continue to the upside, but if there's more weakness, we could see $0.0569 revisited. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23tcNzkBDJe5iSXc1cRxk4tfFUeYnW9kMMqCeSQshXKhKqwFD9fY7aZNuwLSNsyShmxaq.png) This is not how I trade, but this support/resistance level marked with grey makes a lot of sense. Just look at how many times price has touched it. So if we take it into consideration, this level has to hold, otherwise it becomes resistance again. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23tcP5TrvzSfsbcSZgUhSpUQ9Ev2iN42VoMzSsULduwdj1NpeVXSVSMm2f1tU1p4a3Pzx.png) On a more granular scale, the ***h4*** time frame shows $HIVE trading above the bullish gap created yesterday, which has not been retested yet. This gap has to defend price, if we want bullish continuation. If the gap is lost, we could go back to $0.0578 and potentially $0.0569. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23t8D1dSedmPZtd4jjfezjcKj2wUG54Lh4nffa4fdF83Ct78FWAuXPGN92TK83tqjeE1z.png) This week ***$BTC*** lost the bullish gap, which could not hold price and swept $74,900, as I mentioned the possibility of it in my last week's analysis. We got a bounce there, but there's no enough bullish momentum yet, the order block has not been set yet. Let's see if we continue to the upside or we go lower. I'd be careful here. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23twA7Rpz51tS6dZGQ9RvLsRUgrak2a4N2zz1zooxZ8hB1Ny4GM8KnYkMe8LyS439AXaT.png) ***ETH/BTC *** has not done much lately. price is still retesting the top bullish gap. We either get a bounce here, which would be ideal, or we retest the second gap. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23t86HDp3HeKSq1wf2CgJmzaXEt69L6XguUjxfvZnSuxbgNgNPZnACcVLb7a3uuuNBdDD.png) [source](https://www.forexfactory.com/calendar) Next week we only have one red folder day, but geo-political events can move the market, so stay safe. *Remember, technical analysis is not about forecasting price, but about reacting to what price does.* As always, this is a game of probabilities, not certainties. Also please note, this is not financial advice, it's my view and understanding of the market. All charts posted here are screenshots from Tradinview. Tropic\\.title: They Don't Hack Our Phone First
Tropic\\.body:
A couple of years ago, around 2019, a message came exactly from my friend's number. And that was exactly what made it convincing. Not a strange number or link or email. His WhatsApp number, his profile picture, and his style of messaging. He told me that he needs my help because he is stranded and he is in need of four thousand naira. My spirit shifted a bit because he has never asked me for such, so I nearly sent the money. Because at that moment I didn't want to doubt my friend of many years, which made it look like doubting him felt more uncomfortable than losing the money he asked for. And to me, I feel that is where these scammers are smarter than some people. They will never target our phone first. Their target is basically our emotions. They study our level of trust in our relationship, and that is what they target to enter us. In a place like here, where someone can call me “brotherly” or “my blood,” it can activate a loyalty reflex almost automatically, and that is exactly a specific weakness they can easily feed on because they can easily find it. And from what I feel, the most dangerous scam is not the usual fake bank alert we see today or the lottery message we receive on our phone. It is the compromised account of the person I actually care about, someone whose style of chatting and replying the scammer has mastered before reaching out. Because, assuming it is from a strange number, our guard will increase. That is exactly the gap they step into. ![247187.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenproject/23t7936oD8NgLHXasogFZDPGx8DYtuDd6PE53QkAYbMGeR7WE9tHbejgzPD49nLwgyZ7j.png) And what I have been doing lately is that I call after seeing such a message. I won't reply. I just pick up my phone and call that person directly to confirm the message and hear if it's their voice to know what is going on. Most people will never do this because they don't want to sound or look too forward by accusing their friends. And that hesitation to call is precisely what gets exploited. Urgency is the weapon they usually use. And the moment we fall for that, we start rushing. We are falling gradually into their hands, and before we know it, they win while we lose. Tropic\\.title: Pollo a la parrilla, ensalada y mandioca-----Baked chicken, salad, and cassava
Tropic\\.body:
Buenos dias a todos, asi que para hoy domingo, lo mejor es preparar pollo a la parrilla y como siempre amigos, los primero es encender el fuego o sea el carbon, el cual una ves que se haga brasas, es ahi cuando agregamos la parrilla y sobre la misma la carne, como pueden ver la misma se trata de pata y muslo de pollo bien condimentada.una ves cocinado todo amigos, lo corto todo en porciones, al pollo, lo siguiente es preparar la ensalada, la cual contiene, arveja, papa, zanahoria cortada en trozos pequeños, pepino, tomate, huevo y mayonesa a gusto.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/prm4031/EogPpQ8RRCzm8Z1EzgiZLnMDw6omcvY2XWMcewPoQ3SmViLK5sn5HuWbtNiTycNZtgt.png)

Asi que para cocinar la mandioca o yuca, agregamos una olla con agua, cuando la misma hierve le agregamos dicha yuca, la cual una ves blanda, le quitamos el agua y listo para degustarla.

MUCHAS GRACIAS POR LEERME Y SEGUIRME.

TRADUCIDO AL INGLES

Good morning everyone, so for this Sunday, the best thing is to prepare grilled chicken and as always friends, the first thing is to light the fire, that is, the charcoal, which once it turns into embers, is when we add the grill and on it the meat. As you can see, it consists of well-seasoned chicken legs and thighs. Once everything is cooked, friends, I cut everything into portions, the chicken. Next, we prepare the salad, which contains peas, potatoes, carrots cut into small pieces, cucumber, tomato, egg, and mayonnaise to taste.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/prm4031/EogPpQ8RRCzm8Z1EzgiZLnMDw6omcvY2XWMcewPoQ3SmViLK5sn5HuWbtNiT

So, to cook the cassava or yuca, we add a pot of water, when it boils we add the yuca, which once soft, we remove the water and it's ready to taste.

Thank you very much for reading and following me.
