title.title: That's where it started =/= Hier ging es los - Kyoto Impressions 👹🍣🎎 Wonderful Japan ENG-GER
title.body:
![IMG_8525.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23ywsGQjeDUbuGQtBGkx5GBM2vihkPZZ2mWXuNSqgP3KHtmkmP8tQDHyMjGdZPVE4ebaD.JPG) It’s been a few days since our trip to Kyoto. Unfortunately, everyday life caught up with us way too quickly, leaving us no time to really reflect on what we experienced. We visited so many interesting places, and I took so many photos that I wanted to show you all. But somehow, I just haven’t gotten around to it yet. But you have to start somewhere, so I’ll just do that right now. Let’s go back to Day 1, which, after a long drive, finally brought us to the former Japanese capital. Fortunately, we still had a little time left, and of course we didn’t want to spend it at our accommodation—we already wanted to see a bit more of that city. So we decided on the Higashiyama district, which lies east of downtown Kyoto and is home to some of the old imperial city’s most famous sights. After a somewhat tedious search, we finally found a parking spot, walked a bit through the winding alleys, and after a few minutes came upon this interesting building. This is the Yasaka Pagoda—often known as the Hōkan-ji Pagoda. It is one of Kyoto’s most famous landmarks and, with its five stories, towers impressively over the historic alleys of the Higashiyama district. The pagoda was originally founded as early as the 6th century, although the current structure dates from a later period. ![IMG_8529.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/242hUeFrU4Mk8uymYKZqVhkaLaoUqS3AJwWxmUn5utWmW3QxjLaw4PbTW73t8N7RjV1nq.JPG) DEUTSCH _Unsere Reise nach Kyoto liegt nun schon ein paar Tage hinter uns. Der Alltag hatte uns leider viel zu schnell eingeholt und lässt einem gar keine Zeit, mal richtig auf das Erlebt zurückzuschauen. Dabei waren wir doch an so vielen interessanten Orten gewesen und ich habe so viele Fotos gemacht, die ich euch alle zeigen wollte. Aber irgendwie bin ich da noch gar nicht zu gekommen._ _Irgendwo muss man aber anfangen, und da mache ich jetzt einfach mal. Wir gehen zurück auf Tag 1, der uns nach langer Fahrt dann endlich in die ehemalige japanische Hauptstadt gebracht hatte. Glücklicherweise hatten wir noch ein wenig Zeit und diese wollten wir natürlich nicht in unserer Unterkunft verbringen, sondern wenn möglich noch ein wenig sehen._ _Und so entschieden wir uns für den Higashiyama-Bezirk, welche östlich vom Kyotoer Stadtzentrum liegt, und in dem sich einige der bekanntesten Sehenswürdigkeiten der alten Kaiserstadt befinden._ _Nachdem wir nach einiger, leicht umständlicher Suche endlich einen Parkplatz gefunden hatten, liefen wir ein wenig in die verwinkelten Gassen hinein und kamen nach wenigen Minuten auf dieses interessante Gebäude zu._ _Hierbei handelt es sich um die Yasaka Pagoda – oft auch als Hōkan-ji Pagode bekann. Sie ist eines der bekanntesten Wahrzeichen von Kyoto und ragt mit ihren fünf Etagen eindrucksvoll über die historischen Gassen des Higashiyama-Viertels hinaus. Ursprünglich wurde die Pagode bereits im 6. Jahrhundert gegründet, auch wenn das heutige Bauwerk aus späterer Zeit stammt._ ![IMG_7222.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/EqhQF3PNniKPMuTQKVWYSBCaGSffYvsY5NhMSnmeWqFJbzFEcWmknjdz6mLDdcdH9WK.JPG) The view of the pagoda from the narrow streets of the neighborhood is extremely popular, and it’s a favorite photo spot—something we quickly realized ourselves. We happened to be there in the afternoon, when crowds were pushing their way through the alleys. But in the early morning hours, when you’re likely almost alone here, this place is said to reveal its very special magic. But even on that afternoon, this was already a great prelude to everything that was yet to come for us. And our walk that day wasn’t over yet either—it had actually only just begun. And that’s why it didn’t bother me at all that it was a little crowded here. I simply enjoyed the moment and took my own photos. And I kept stopping along the way to look back. We had planned to come back to this neighborhood another day. But who knows - usually it's best to thoroughly savor the here and now...
👹🍣🎎
_Der Blick auf die Pagode aus den engen Straßen des Viertel ist äußerst beliebt und sie ist ein populäres Fotomotiv, was auch wir ganz schnell mitbekommen haben. Wir waren halt auch am Nachmittag da, wo sich hier die Menschenmassen durch die Gassen geschoben haben. Aber in den frühen Morgenstunden, wenn man hier wahrscheinlich noch fast alleine ist, dann sollte dieser Ort seinen ganz besonderen Zauber entfalten._ _Aber auch an jenen Nachmittag war das hier bereits eine schöne Einstimmung auf all das, was für uns nun noch folgen würde. Und auch unser Spaziergang an jenem Tag war ja noch nicht vorbei, sondern hatte eigentlich ja gerade erst begonnen. Und deshalb störte es mich auch gar nicht, dass es hier ein wenig voller war. Ich lebte einfach den Augenblick und machte meine eigene Fotos. Und blieb dabei auch immer wieder stehen, und schaute zurück. Wir hatten zwar noch einmal vor, an einem anderen Tag in dieses Viertel zu kommen. Aber wer weiß, deshalb empfielt es sich das Hier und Jetzt immer gründlich zu geniessen..._ ![IMG_8535.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/243WRfkQpyqkWbsGpKrTqgxEzcb5vBS9UKbnBCDm7r8aBbAyjx5dBtJc9pCrdz22YpENe.JPG) ![blog-ende.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23tv6H18WKn98nBVkn2MwVhwWsuFRFgjBGwxLEMVhRZD7zRRbFokaNiAn39fUaB3TxVX6.png)

title.title: The deepest peace on the shortest river in Serbia, Vrelo
title.body:
Hi everyone, I hope you have a great weekend! On our way back from a peaceful cruise along the Drina river, we made a stop at one of Serbia's most fascinating hidden gems, Vrelo. It is known as the shortest river in Serbia and one of the shortest in Europe.

![4075.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep3dsHuUYR2NJUDinJo5wB8gVCRtt6uB8FAUKaLNnwhxgVbSTHHHJuMnAqKQ7PA1W9r.jpg)

When I was a child, my parents took me on a trip to Perucac, and then we also visited this river. The feeling was exactly the same, Vrelo feels like a place untouched by time.

![4056.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoCgE5SJdiUYUaoVBBLYVpUWqCm7512HaXpkYM9x7a22zMyen4s8YNiHmb5W2zhe9sV.jpg)

![4062.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EonjYuTH1sByFcnoVemch8cMJRvg7CApeWVA2Uze6WWoHKGaiXBEoL8ZASzziAEXqCP.jpg)

![4064.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EowF5rp7yXJWtKyYvbg48L3G3qCfaTfdwUgeRbk81913BWtWRJ5tJquQ3eQw3eD8VP1.jpg)

I was a child then, so I didn't experience nature in the same way, and that's the only difference. Now I respect these gifts of nature much more. But what has remained the same is the feeling you have in this place, peace, freedom and freshness.

![4071.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoGwS9vXTvDYBPbxZzywgfqFaz2jKdoVEENKqmXtGSLvoncrJsYyPZt5wyFheSZqHjJ.jpg)

I remember that the most interesting thing to me then was that this river is also called \

because it is exactly 365m long, as long as the year has days.

![4083.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep5kpNyJZ98FxcyN8YF8doXBUTBej3J7UoGa4SYE6SsQ4pWpNvn8uxmFntLgyLpCA1P.jpg)

![4084.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EowEeWyu82Ydt74dT5wgZ761nsDGoZ1LYDTrK2W2VnxWoxf3WPSZ2YiqFps3Xv3FKJG.jpg)

I told this to my kids and they listened carefully. I love when I share with them some interesting facts about such beautiful places and teach them to appreciate what nature gives us every day, and with that comes the feeling of giving back to it.

![4077.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep3dqZNZrHXf3id6smoR7Ey6kWx4Ahfz7hsMBYwN2yvqWCxYiMpCX1qzFQ2NwcMTUvy.jpg)

![4082.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep1WrpTFmiMtBP48wyHxgBfFo1wAzksa9DKDzYU3PMXwj5Xrt7egP9tWfG1ViCayJTi.jpg)

![4067.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpGQAtEJPoKYcdjKR2wZ2GB6efMJypf5UrfvDMuhiEpBHZfBtamPj8XpibdUq9eTKJd.jpg)

Located near Bajina Bašta, at the foot of the Tara mountain, next to the Perucac lake, Vrelo is famous for its crystal-clear river and visitors are happy to stop here to take a break.

![4063.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpvhV2CrX66mms5nYaKR84jXftgXSejv6diKQuTC58GN8JckVCwAg559GP6t7vBypck.jpg)

![4057.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoeEQKrtktc3EX71X3FFy6tcn9tjqUzkJfGhQy5mJeHsCoRyiYdu3t4E1e7E9xDZphQ.jpg)

Despite its short length, the river leaves a powerful impression. The fresh mountain air, the sound of flowing water, and the deep green surroundings instantly create a feeling of calm.

![4066.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep3dKGwsoSFMSH36LY4tsAyycswYnxCQMxaCDoJ85DSWumCHACm7CtRWQDbCys5zSfp.jpg)

The water was unbelievably clean and transparent, I enjoyed watching the reflections.

![4059.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eoc82Td4ZMUioeqmkLr2EeZhjeAZj8NoaBBD5KtDF7DppfoeQFFgk2aS7CPuxbQxo8a.jpg)
![4061.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EowFAmdHZBeJUkC2SosdSZ4yzku4bHXYWRWkA7w4P2VnQJa9nEotgCj3Q9dQbatwUBM.jpg)

![4080.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoiVkpQTG5nu7Y8RHU8Nu5CghFZXzUVhSccC3K2sARbEqDX5b71GKPXGUubjnSqoVUR.jpg)

Small wooden bridges, lush trees, and the untouched nature around us made the entire place feel like a secret oasis hidden from the busy world.

![4074.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep1VR4EbvAJ6hYgdvvKLzrVN3vZ39oSYwkdBEMghT4fRvHtheGPSjSQQBSaZhZ4wEk5.jpg)

There was something incredibly grounding about standing there, breathing in the fresh air and listening only to nature.

![4068.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eokbaiztgo17YytwM7dYde6pw2iqsRkrVcm6Fehi68W3c1RyswjdPKXJx2iYyJYCixr.jpg)

There is also a restaurant where you can stop by if you are hungry. We were not there this time because we ate in Višegrad.

![4072.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoprWdxMWyAHCjfGeEA8UfDMkvKdS8G3cAk8Wu3jcx5wdD1zm3DWc6kV8wDHVdxf78L.jpg)

![4073.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eou7J3EpVdnx9r48hi3saot1QmWcMzDLQPPbtzdLwiH56mVKSD4GQBtTKN7juhWY3Ks.jpg)

After the movement and excitement of the Drina cruise, Vrelo offered another amazing experience, slow, peaceful, and deeply relaxing. It reminded me how important it is to pause sometimes and appreciate those simple moments.

![4085.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eoc64kyT5UphmWn9MPmj9SH55ZMhJm1j39KgFMDixk77SLYNuSSe2J5uLHnwvUNK5MC.jpg)

Thank you for reading.

Jelena

title.title: Topic Review: Forgive and Forget
title.body:
https://youtu.be/rI1_UqxSoB4?si=Qanwg47cPGKrFnZo


God wants us to live in peace and love with one another, and not in conflict. He forgives us for the wrong things we do, and in the same way, He expects us to forgive others. He showed us we ought to go about it, and now it’s our turn to follow that example.

This is how we should live our lives, even when it’s hard. Holding on to offences because caused us doesn’t do us any good. In fact, God made it clear that if we come to Him in prayer while we’re still holding something against someone, we should go and sort it out first before we go back to Him in prayers. This could be one of the reasons our prayers sometimes seem like they are not producing the answers we expect.

If we are not willing to forgive others, then we’re not truly following Jesus the way we are meant to. Forgiveness should be a character trait every believer should possess.

title.title: 真正的自由是啥？
title.body:
现在的微信和抖音可以自由的表达自己观点和诉求吗？

       这些平台顶多就是在没有智能手机的前提下多了一些好玩和有趣，没事吹吹牛逼，抽空发点视频和照片晒晒日常，偶尔看看不可描述的视频，想做网红的人可以做直播或长期发视频搞点额外收入，…所以各大社交过视频媒体自然就融入了我们的生活和工作，这种常态将继续下去…


  这不是废话么？是的，做为普通人的一份子我也想做一个网红，于是经过2个多月的准备，开始抖音直播，直播间开始3个人10个人再到40个人，我靠！这个过程看似轻描淡写，但真的很煎熬，特别是经常关小黑屋，话题涉及web3好多内容和词汇很容易被提示，开始的时候我非常注意内容上的打磨生怕触及敏感词，做过直播的人都知道，如果经常被提醒，流量很快被限制，但人啊就是样，越是谨慎就越容易出问题！

     尤其是直播互动时，有观众都提问总是是出其不易，开播前也有预设观众会提哪些问题，但总有没想到的，因为互动都是即时，需要快速准确回应，

   我去，就是这个回复的过程让我一次又一次的被提示，停播3分钟、15分钟、3天、7天、15天、1个月，直到最后一次在后台私信回复一个粉丝的问题，提及币安钱包这4个字，我草，…


  屏幕跳出一行红色字体，你的账号涉嫌经融诈骗风险被永久封禁，当时我整个人都懵逼了，我这个号虽然不到10000粉丝但涨粉和转化率还不错，每次直播后至少增加20个粉丝后台私信不断，转入微信的有互动的也很多！

   看到这个提示后，我马上联系抖音客服，我说你们有什么资格说我是经融诈骗，你们不是司法机构或政府机构凭什么这样界定，挖槽，当时我整个人都炸毛了…

    但无论你怎么说最后得到的回复都是千篇一律，是按抖音社会规范条约，对每个人都一样…

 后面打了10来通电话申诉没毛用，直到现在我的身份证号都不可以直播只能发视频，就这样辛苦半年熬了几百个小的夜所有的付出就这样无情终结了！


       扯了半天，谈什么自由，到现在我们国内所有社交平台动不动就提醒或封号，说话都要小心翼翼，战战兢兢，无论是民事诉讼或政务话题都是雷区，连说话都没有自由，至于其他自由那都是奢望，正如你的钱存入银行结果被莫名自由的挪用了，，这种自由永远停留在某个阶层，想想都踏马滑稽…



        我很爱自己的国家，但我鄙视一切盲人摸象的庸政，明主自由从来不是一句口号，更不是粉饰！！

title.title: Brochete de corazon de pollo con ensalada y mandiocaºººººChicken heart skewer with salad and cassava
title.body:
Hola a todos, bueno amigos, llego el mejor dia de la semana, con esto quiero decir que es porque siempre para el almuerzo, este dia es muy importante por el solo hecho de que, la mayoria de la familia en la medida que se pueda nos juntamos para compartir del mismo o sea del almuerzo, para el cual en esta ocacion prepare brochetas de corazon de pollo, con mandioca, ensalada y queso provolone.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoyR1x4t6CF72HjEEcAHKB91gR5otZmFEWySncdAC1e3erK3iHoBoR1AZhx8uqeCN9R.png)

Para preparar dicha carne o sea el corazon de pollo, lo dejo bien condimentado un dia antes, con el siguiente condimento, savora, sal a gusto y un poco de jugo de limon.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoGxWJ3yiV6q51DVzfvncJMPEy3XCGoXSjZ1R8FcXywbUu6RmxW6AaaH7gPwjxNKDeb.png)

Asi que cuando el dia de cocinarlo como lo es hoy se prepara de la siguiente manera, los palillos son de caña de bambu, donde se ensartan dichos corazones para luego de haber encendido el fuego como para asado, lo vamos agregando en la parrilla.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoEpbisWe4BWSa8tJ5wKSPoAusDLupoKdC6X89d6o4nUACVnfLNL38q1Q7cCAiND5YD.png)

Una ves que se cocina de un lado lo vamos dando vuelta para que se terminen de cocinar, en ese lapso agrego con papel de cocina el queso provolone para que se vaya ablandando.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoEq17aVhjVVcn9mu6RxAho977yNQkViwDJEaGgsrapE5zRGtRBQAHyJdbqzCkk1Piq.png)

Bueno la parte especial para acompañar estoas brochetas, lo mejor es hacerlo con mandioca, las cuales una ves peladas, se agrega una olla con agua en la hornalla de la cocina con la mandioca y una ves cocinadas, le quietamos el agua y lista para degustarlas.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23vsLSQQkA6hZGpUWgwEwwUUq6Pabb2J21h3b6VHLE8ru9bKUFSZpTJwW5Vf9njKrBKqV.png)

La parte de la ensalada amigos es facil, rallamos la zanahoria, para mesclarla con lechuga, que condimentamos con aceite de oliva y sal a gusto.

MUCHAS GRACIAS POR SEGUIRME Y LEERME, QUE PASEN UN BELLO DIA.

ENGLISH

Hello everyone, well friends, the best day of the week has arrived, and by this I mean that it is because for lunch, this day is very important simply because most of the family, as much as possible, gathers to share it, that is, lunch, for which on this occasion I prepared chicken heart skewers, with cassava, salad, and provolone cheese.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoyR1x4t6CF72HjEEcAHKB91gR5otZmFEWySncdAC1e3erK3iHoBoR1AZhx8

To prepare this meat, that is, the chicken heart, I let it marinate well a day in advance with the following seasoning: savora, salt to taste, and a bit of lemon juice.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoGxWJ3yiV6q51DVzfvncJMPEy3XCGoXSjZ1R8FcXywbUu6RmxW6Aaa

So, when the day comes to cook it, like today, it is prepared as follows: the skewers are made of bamboo, where the hearts are threaded. After lighting the fire as for a barbecue, we add them to the grill.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoEpbisWe4BWSa8tJ5wKSPoAusDLupoKdC6X89d6o4nUACVnfLNL38q1Q

Once it is cooked on one side, we flip it over to finish cooking. During that time, I add the provolone cheese with a paper towel so it can soften.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoEq17aVhjVVcn9mu6RxAho977yNQkViwDJEaGgsrapE5zRGtRBQAHyJdbqz

Well, the special part to accompany these skewers is best done with cassava. Once peeled, you add a pot of water on the stove with the cassava, and once cooked, you remove the water and it's ready to enjoy.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23vsLSQQkA6hZGpUWgwEwwUUq6Pabb2J21h3b6VHLE8ru9bKUFSZpTJwW5

The salad part, friends, is easy. We grate the carrot to mix it with lettuce, which we season with olive oil and salt to taste.

Thank you very much for following and reading me, have a beautiful day.

title.title: I had an accident. Here's how I navigated it... (The result is impressive!)
title.body:
We had some guys over yesterday, and they were installing solar panels on our roof.

Originally, I thought I would be needed to help, but @new.things let me know they had it covered. I thought I would get out into the garden and chop down some of the high branches that I had been seeing that had been bothering me. I was using this tool.


![b4a6ea68-f3c7-4cd4-8961-eafe258682af.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/consciouscat/23w2ktu77K8L5LT9w5JEnkzXputxAbQgZZVAAiETb4MnbHNaKRrYTyUCux9ngharB3S1G.jpg)


Now I had used this tool many, many, many times, so I was aware of what it could do, how to use it, and its limitations. I decided to go after a branch that was a bit too big for this tool, and in trying to force the tool to cut the branch, I was using the tool in a way that was not very safe in order to achieve the outcome.
What happened is that the tool ended up falling down onto my arm and hurting it quite badly. This story is about what I did following that and how I navigated how that felt physically and emotionally. 

---

The first thing I did after noticing that the tools and the branches were all on the ground (and therefore that things were physically safe) was I made a point of paying attention to how my arm was feeling.

Initially, I was pretty embarrassed, so I had a look around to make sure that none of the guys on the roof could see me. When I felt **emotionally** safe to process this, I let myself really feel the sensations in my arm. At some point in that process, I looked at my arm, where it really hurt, and it made sense that it hurt so much because it was red and very swollen, with a giant lump where this tool had crashed down onto my lower right arm just above my wrist.

I really let myself feel the sensations of it.

One of my mentors says that pain is just trapped sensation.

**Pain is trapped sensation.**

When we don't feel the pain of something, it gets stuck in our body. So, I have got into the habit of feeling the sting, the sharpness, the physical discomfort or pain immediately whenever it's safe and possible to do so, even if I cut myself with a knife while I'm chopping vegetables or something.

It means that a lot of that intensity can be discharged straight away, which means that we don't have something that we then carry on for a long period of time.

I did that, and then I realised that it would be sensible to finish the job and chop up the things that were on the ground. I picked up the secateurs from the ground and chopped the branch up smaller with my left hand, my non-injured hand, but to do that, I sort of needed my right hand to steady it a little bit. Every time I did that, it hurt, so I thought this was not worth doing anymore.


![10600e68-5f81-4529-a9f6-a25ca03622ac.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/consciouscat/EoAYm4gWJusiJTGQVPLGYcAKHNZCrCtj6grYxpu9pG7sBtSDskDBkyEUnMy5ftGiGVv.jpg)


I carefully picked the tools up and walked back up to the house. As soon as I started walking, I realised how I was feeling emotionally, and that I was feeling very **angry** at myself.

I was hearing myself say very unkind things. That is, a voice in my head was saying very unkind things, and that was a surprise because I am usually quite kind to myself at that point in my journey with all the healing that I've done. But what I was hearing was that *I was so stupid.*

I did some tapping. Some of you might be familiar with EFT or Emotional Freedom Techniques. I did some internal tapping. You can do the actual tapping with your fingers, but because I've done so much of this processing now, I can actually do the whole process internally and move through that emotional experience.

Pretty quickly, I realised I wouldn't talk to my own friends like this. I wouldn't tell them they were stupid. I would just recognise that they made a mistake and they had misjudged the consequences of trying to cut a branch that big. 

And what was great is that by working through how I was feeling emotionally, I then felt so much calmer and far less reactive. It meant that I had space to think more clearly about what I would do next.


![81bd3ca7-03c1-4c1d-849c-fd644c04d785.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/consciouscat/EpNmP1sZPPbr61bbz4fubt7PdKL5h9Nmqxpzg46mt6WtpKMXTBR1KdguJs6PVTfbbfH.jpg)


Because I don't love going to doctors because I've had lots of medical trauma in the past, what I did was I thought of a friend of mine who's had lots of accidents. I wanted to try to self-assess whether or not it was a soft tissue injury or whether or not I had broken my arm because the lump on my arm was pretty big, and the pain in my arm was very significant. It was in the exact same spot where I broke my wrist when I was 15.

I started calling a couple of people who I thought might be able to help. In between, I talked to Brad, who came into the house, took one look at my arm and handed me an ice pack (and told me that in future I should yell out for help!)

I ended up calling the Health Line we have in Australia so I could talk to a registered nurse and get her opinion on what to do. This time it was a woman. She suggested that I go to a doctor and get it checked out.

I was able to quickly move through the options and, on a Saturday morning, snag one of the only doctor's appointments that were available anywhere around here. I got a referral for an X-ray just in case. But what was great about the doctor was that she just lightly pressed on the bones on either side of my lower arm. Even though it hurt at the site of the impact, it didn't hurt at all when she pressed on those bones. That was all really helpful.

So, there were a bunch of great actions that I was able to take because I had felt the pain, and I had accepted how I was feeling.

I had moved through how I was feeling emotionally, and it created space for me to be able to think more clearly and take really sensible actions. Even while I was waiting at the doctor's, I was alternating between having the ice pack on and using a tuning fork as a way to put coherent sound into my body to help heal it at the level of sound waves!

Overall, I'm very impressed. What's great is that it's now a day and a half later, and I'm able to use the fingers of my right hand more, and use my right hand in ways today that I couldn't do yesterday!

I can do a whole bunch of things, little things, pain-free today that yesterday when I tried to do them created sharp pain. I'm sure that my arm's ability to heal more quickly than I expected is partly due to the fact that I was really feeling what was coming up, but also that I could think clearly enough to really proactively take great care of myself. 


![1fdf0b38-ac30-4105-b7c7-3cf8d2da9fb9.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/consciouscat/Eou7heycVKmXpyuzLA2nbd7siMpcV8LNWmmFgk2Mv1yKaQreC8v3p6gox6LaW6yZZ6p.jpg)


[ All photos taken by @new.things, as there are still a bunch of things I cannot do yet. Used with his enthusiastic permission :P ]

title.title: Notes Toward an Understanding of a Number That Cannot Be Real
title.body:
# Notes Toward an Understanding of a Number That Cannot Be Real

$81.62 billion. One quarter. One company. Ninety days.

I keep writing it down and then staring at it and it doesn't get smaller.

Revenue up 69% year-over-year, earnings per share up 120%, data center alone pulling in $73 billion — and when Jensen Huang got on the call Wednesday night and said \

the stock fell almost 2%. That is the market we live in. That is the cognitive environment in which we are all apparently operating as adults. A company prints the greatest single-quarter earnings in the history of the semiconductor industry and traders go home slightly disappointed. The implied move was 5-7%. The actual move: negative. Three of the last four earnings reports have now ended with the stock falling. Not because the numbers missed. They didn't miss. They crushed. Because the expectations were so levitated that reality, however extraordinary, could not reach them.

Sit with that for a moment.

NVDA has $5.4 trillion in market capitalization. It is now, according to Louis Navellier, estimated to account for as much as 50% of the S&P 500's total performance. One company. Three hundred thirty million Americans have their retirement accounts indexed to a benchmark that is increasingly a single ticker wearing a disguise. The S&P 500 used to be a diversification instrument. It is currently a Jensen Huang fan club with a fee structure.

And look, I understand the counterargument. I really do. The hyperscalers — Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta — are collectively spending $725 billion on AI infrastructure this year alone, up 77% from last year's $410 billion. Microsoft is good for $190 billion. Amazon for $200 billion. These are not speculative projections scribbled on a napkin by a venture capitalist at 2am. These are committed capital plans disclosed in earnings calls. Huang himself stood at GTC in March and said he sees $1 trillion in purchase orders for Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips through at least 2027. A trillion. That's before the Rubin Ultra platform. Before the standalone CPUs. Before Feynman. The number is still expanding as you read this.

So the bull case is not imaginary. It is, if anything, almost embarrassingly concrete. The capex is real, the orders are real, the margins are real — 74%-plus gross margins on hardware, which is a number that would have made a 2015 chip analyst choke. The second-order effect is also real: Nvidia is now trying to take Intel and AMD's CPU market, with CFO Colette Kress estimating $20 billion in total CPU revenue this year. A GPU company declaring it intends to become \

is not a modest ambition. It is either genius or hubris, and so far the distinction has been irrelevant.

But.

There's a psychology here that gets uncomfortable if you probe it.

Q1 S&P 500 earnings growth came in at 27.1% — the fastest pace since Q4 2021. The forward P/E on the index sits at 20.9, above both the five-year and ten-year averages. The IT sector posted a net profit margin of 29.1% in Q1. Record after record after record. And somewhere in that cascade of superlatives is a question nobody wants to be the first to ask in a room: what is the consequence of failure? Not catastrophic failure. Just regular, boring failure. What if one of the hyperscalers, looking at that $200 billion annual capex commitment, quietly decides to slow down? What happens to the $5.4 trillion thesis when a single conference call shifts tone?

Nvidia beat expectations in 18 of its last 20 quarters. The two where it missed were in 2022. The stock fell 60% that year. It has since recovered everything and then some. The bears have been wrong for so long they have become conversational punchlines. And yet: the stock fell 5% after the February report, down 3% after the one before that, down nearly 2% this week. Three consecutive falls on beats. The market is telling you something. It may just be that expectations are priced for a kind of divine inevitability that even this company — even *this* company — cannot consistently deliver.

There is a version of the AI buildout story that ends with someone holding a $200 billion data center full of chips, waiting for the revenue model to arrive. It has happened before, with different nouns. The fiber-optic cable. The server farm. The hyperscale cloud itself, circa 2011, when everyone was convinced public cloud was over-provisioned. History keeps forgiving the infrastructure over-builders, but the timing of that forgiveness has historically required a recession and a write-down cycle as the intermediate step.

Nobody's penciling in a recession right now. The consumer is holding. The S&P closed April at 7,209, an all-time high. Margins at records. Buybacks everywhere. Nvidia just authorized an additional $80 billion in share repurchases, which is either a statement of supreme confidence or the most expensive capital allocation decision in the history of buybacks, depending on what happens in 2027.

Huang closed the call with: *\

he said. A trillion dollars, growing to three or four trillion. Every frontier AI model — Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, Meta, Google Gemini — runs on Nvidia platforms. The company is everywhere the intelligence is. That is a moat so wide you can barely see the other bank.

And the stock dropped 1.77%.

I don't know what to do with any of this. I'm not sure anyone does. The fundamentals say own it. The psychology of a stock that keeps selling off on record beats says be careful. The macro context — oil at $103, Warsh's first FOMC meeting three weeks out, inflation still printing above target — says the risk-free alternative isn't zero anymore. The 10-year yield doesn't care about Jensen Huang's enthusiasm.

What I do know is this: when a company earning $120 billion in net income in a single fiscal year can't get its stock to move on an earnings beat, one of two things is true. Either the market is efficiently pricing a business that has already captured most of its future value. Or the market is in a state of such profound expectation saturation that normal mechanics have temporarily suspended. 

Both of those are slightly terrifying for different reasons.

The number was $81.62 billion. Real. Verified. Audited eventually.

The stock went down.

Figure it out.

title.title: The End of The Hustle
title.body:
I’ve been thinking a lot lately about work, and what we’re all actually chasing.

A friend of mine was recently made redundant after fifteen years with the same company. She's in her mid-50s, a time notoriously hard for women to find work. But she's got a good reputation - she's excellent at her job, loyal, hard-working, team player, expert. She shouldn't have trouble getting more work, so she took the payout and figured she’d do a bit of contract work while she looked for something permanent.


![2335.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/23tvAvxFSuCGV6QifZRk6AtZPnqFx3LRcymyoJiJYcfDa7jojZ96JPifwzDaZwGmN7hmX.jpg)


What she didn’t expect was the absolute insanity of the modern job market. Every job gets 200 or 300 applications now because AI has made it so easy to apply. People can fire off tailored cover letters in seconds. So the genuinely thoughtful applications — the ones someone has actually sat down and written carefully — just disappear into the pile with everything else. What's the point? She’s spending hours writing proper applications, and still barely getting seen.

As she said, it’s not what you know anymore, but it's who you know. It's down to networks, connections, visibility, timing.

I kinda like her unemployed, to be fair - she’s actually become happier, calmer, and her sense of humour's back. Our relationship has deepened, for the first time in *years* and *years*. She’s more relaxed, present, herself.

It's this loss of self that has had me reject a full-time job since I left my full time, insanely demanding teaching job. But it's more than that - the thought of interviews makes my blood run cold. Truly. I feel physically sick thinking about it. I’d probably end up crying in front of them from pure anxiety, which I've been known to do before, even though I should be confident, and I know I'm excellent at my job - I just don’t interview well.

So instead, I keep doing agency teaching, or rather, I just sign up for work each term with the one school, which suits me. I make good money when I’m working. If I don’t want to go in one day, I don’t. If I’m exhausted, I rest, even though I'm trying hard to make hay whilst the sun shines. There’s freedom in it, even without sick pay or holidays.

![b384e77d-7665-4142-bdf7-633989d2a67d-1_all_1163.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/23u672MYogp9486p4bDSdFNCZNbGNzgvDi5fDCJrDnwRgapPJ614sVXhZVVkGUksn6SDK.jpg)

Years ago, temporary work felt transitional, like an unserious stopgap before “real work.” But now, for so many people, it *is* the work. My friend said even contract work has changed completely. You don’t go through agencies anymore but compete online with hundreds of applicants for short-term contracts too.

The whole landscape shifted while she wasn't looking. It's exhausting - I'd be freaking out, if I needed money that badly - I don't know why she's that calm. 

I hate it and I'm glad I'm at the end of my hustle. I'm debt free so I don't need to worry. The idea of looking for work is a nightmare for me. It's not just just the work itself, but by the performance of work where you're constantly trying to sell yourself and prove yourself, brand yourself via Linked In,  The constant proving. Selling yourself. Branding yourself. Interviewing, optimising, competing and smiling through anxiety while pretending this all feels a normal human experience. 

I don’t dream of being rich anymore, if I ever did. I don’t need a luxury car or a giant house or some hyper-productive empire. I just want enough money to live, enough to pay the bills, have a bit of freedom, maybe work a couple of days a week doing something useful, and spend the rest of my time actually living my life. Now that's my kind of ambition. 

Because the older I get, the more I realise the people who seem richest to me are the ones who have time. I look at the older people at the beach with their energy, laughter, chilled out nervous systems. That seems like success to me. 

Meanwhile, my friend stays on the work vision, squirelling away for retirement. We could be dead tomorrow. Fuck that.

title.title: Bắt đầu một ngày mới bình yên tại chùa Phúc Khánh Hà Nội
title.body:
Có đôi khi bạn thức dậy vào một ngày nghỉ và cảm thấy chán nản vì không biết phải làm gì. Việc nằm dài trên giường bấm điện thoại qua lại hết giờ này đến giờ khác chỉ làm cho cơ thể thêm uể oải và mệt mỏi. Thay vì để thời gian trôi qua một cách lãng phí bạn hoàn toàn có thể tạo ra một khởi đầu mới mẻ và tràn đầy năng lượng. Một trong những cách đơn giản nhất mà nhiều người thường làm là thức dậy thật sớm và đi tìm một nơi thanh tịnh để dâng hương như [Chùa Phúc Khánh](https://dulichcheckin.com/chua-phuc-khanh-ha-noi/). Việc thay đổi thói quen nhỏ này sẽ mang lại cho bạn một tinh thần vô cùng sảng khoái.

**Cảm nhận sự khác biệt khi đi lễ vào buổi sáng sớm**

Nếu bạn đang sinh sống ở thủ đô bạn sẽ thấy đường phố vào buổi sáng sớm có một vẻ đẹp rất riêng. Tầm sáu giờ sáng không khí vô cùng mát mẻ và trong lành. Trên đường Tây Sơn thuộc khu vực quận Đống Đa lúc này chưa có tiếng còi xe inh ỏi chưa có cảnh kẹt xe chen lấn hay khói bụi mù mịt. Mọi thứ diễn ra rất chầm chậm và yên ả.

![Chùa Phúc Khánh](https://sqhx-hanoi.mediacdn.vn/91579363132710912/2025/6/30/tap-chi-nghien-cuu-phat-hoc-chua-phuc-khanh-ngoi-chua-linh-thieng-dat-ha-thanh-1-2-17512565287901055134055.png)



Việc chạy xe tà tà trên con phố vắng bóng người mang lại một cảm giác vô cùng dễ chịu. Gió sớm thổi qua làm tung bay vạt áo giúp bạn tỉnh ngủ hoàn toàn. Khi bạn bước chân qua cổng chùa vào giờ này bạn sẽ thấy khuôn viên bên trong vô cùng vắng vẻ. Chỉ có vài người lớn tuổi đang đi bộ chầm chậm quét dọn những chiếc lá rụng trên sân. Không gian lúc này hoàn toàn thuộc về bạn tĩnh lặng và vô cùng bình yên.

**Lựa chọn đồ lễ mộc mạc mang đầy lòng thành kính**

Buổi sáng là thời điểm tuyệt vời nhất để bạn mua được những bông hoa tươi mới nhất. Trên đường đi bạn có thể dừng lại ở một sạp hoa nhỏ ven đường mua một bó hoa cúc vàng hoặc một bó hoa huệ trắng tinh khôi. Những giọt sương đêm đôi khi vẫn còn đọng lại trên từng cánh hoa tạo nên một vẻ đẹp vô cùng thanh khiết.

Bạn có thể ghé qua một sạp trái cây để mua vài quả táo hay một nải chuối xanh. Việc tự tay chọn lựa từng quả ngon nải đẹp thể hiện sự thành tâm rất lớn của bạn. Bạn không cần phải mua những món đồ đắt tiền hay cầu kỳ tốn kém. Sự chân thành và giản dị luôn là điều đáng quý nhất khi chúng ta đi đến những nơi thờ tự trang nghiêm.

**Từng bước dâng hương đúng cách tại Chùa Phúc Khánh Hà Nội**

Khi đã chuẩn bị xong đồ lễ bạn bước vào bên trong khuôn viên một cách nhẹ nhàng. Bạn hãy đặt mâm lễ lên ban thờ một cách ngay ngắn và cẩn thận. Sau đó bạn đi ra khu vực lư hương lớn đặt ở ngay giữa sân để thắp một nén nhang. Buổi sáng sớm lượng người đến viếng chưa nhiều nên việc thắp hương rất dễ dàng không bị khói bay mù mịt làm cay mắt.

![ Chùa Phúc Khánh Hà Nội](https://cdn.xanhsm.com/2024/11/b8b36f26-chua-phuc-khanh-so-7.jpg)

Bạn cầm nén nhang trên tay chắp tay trước ngực và cúi đầu thật thấp. Bạn hãy nhắm mắt lại và cầu nguyện những điều tốt đẹp nhất cho gia đình mình. Bạn có thể cầu xin sức khỏe cho bố mẹ xin sự bình an cho bản thân và những người thân yêu xung quanh. Việc nói ra những mong muốn từ tận đáy lòng trong một không gian tĩnh lặng sẽ giúp tâm trí bạn được giải tỏa khỏi những lo âu thường ngày.

**Ngồi lại dưới bóng cây để tĩnh tâm và thư giãn**

Sau khi dâng hương xong bạn đừng vội vàng ra về ngay lập tức. Khuôn viên nơi đây có rất nhiều cây cổ thụ to lớn với những chiếc ghế đá đặt dọc theo các lối đi quanh sân. Bạn hãy chọn một chỗ ngồi thật thoải mái dưới gốc cây già.

![Chùa Phúc Khánh](https://static.vinwonders.com/production/chua-phuc-khanh-2.jpg)

Bạn hãy cất điện thoại vào sâu trong túi không xem tin tức không nghĩ ngợi về công việc bộn bề. Bạn chỉ cần ngồi im lặng nhìn khói nhang bay nhè nhẹ trên không trung và lắng nghe tiếng chim hót ríu rít trên cành. Không khí mát mẻ của buổi sớm mai cùng với mùi hương trầm quen thuộc sẽ xoa dịu toàn bộ hệ thần kinh của bạn. Đây là khoảng thời gian vô cùng quý giá để bạn kết nối lại với chính mình và tìm thấy sự thanh thản từ bên trong.

**Thưởng thức bữa sáng giản dị ngay trong ngõ nhỏ**

Khi mặt trời bắt đầu lên cao chiếu những tia nắng vàng ươm xuống mặt sân gạch cũng là lúc bạn nên kết thúc buổi đi lễ. Bụng bạn lúc này chắc hẳn đã bắt đầu réo gọi. Ngay cạnh khu vực ngã tư này có vô vàn những quán ăn sáng bình dân nằm sâu trong các con ngõ nhỏ.

Bạn có thể đi bộ thong thả tìm một quán phở bò truyền thống hay một hàng bánh cuốn nóng hổi bốc khói nghi ngút. Việc ngồi ăn trên một chiếc ghế nhựa thấp xì xụp húp bát nước dùng ngọt thanh giữa tiết trời mát mẻ là một trải nghiệm vô cùng tuyệt vời. Bạn vừa ăn vừa ngắm nhìn những người hàng xóm qua lại hỏi han nhau chuyện trò rôm rả. Một bữa sáng giản dị và ngon miệng như vậy sẽ cung cấp cho bạn một nguồn năng lượng vô cùng dồi dào.

**Khép lại chuyến đi với một tâm thế vô cùng nhẹ nhàng**

Một buổi sáng cuối tuần trôi qua thật chậm rãi và đầy ý nghĩa. Bạn không cần phải đi đâu xa xôi hay tốn kém nhiều tiền bạc để tìm kiếm niềm vui. Những điều bình dị và gần gũi ngay xung quanh chúng ta luôn ẩn chứa một sức mạnh chữa lành vô cùng to lớn đối với tâm trí.

Việc thay đổi thói quen ngủ nướng để đi dạo và dâng hương vào buổi sáng sớm sẽ mang lại cho bạn một cơ thể khỏe mạnh và một tâm trí minh mẫn. Chúc bạn sẽ có những ngày nghỉ thật sự thư giãn luôn tìm thấy niềm vui trong những điều nhỏ bé và sẵn sàng đón nhận những điều tốt đẹp trong cuộc sống hàng ngày.

title.title: [카일의 일상#872]석가탄신일 강원도 고성 화암사
title.body:
![IMG_0747.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXjQ45EtvabA6VcqcdbikWA1ZnYgcAoDoco7xKE9Srixs/IMG_0747.jpeg)


여행 중 절 한군데를 들르고 싶었는데 마침 근처에 보였던 화암사.
강원도에서 유명한 절 중 하나라 사람은 좀 있겠거니 했는데, 입구부터 유난히 북적였다. 알고 보니 오늘이 바로 석가탄신일!!!

연휴까지 겹쳐서인지 절 안은 가족 단위 방문객들과 여행객들로 활기가 가득했다. 사람들의 웃음소리와 이야기, 형형색색의 연등들이 어우러져 오히려 따뜻하고 생기 있는 분위기였다.
너무 늦은 나머지 공양은 이미 끝이 났다. 기대한 건 아니었지만, 살짝 아쉬웠다.

주차장에서부터도 꽤 오르막을 올랐는데, 길 옆으로 흐르는 시냇물 소리에 기분이 좋았다.
맑은 하늘 아래 초록빛 산과 절 풍경이 너무 잘 어울렸고, 곳곳에 걸린 연등들이 햇빛을 받아 더 화사하게 보였다. 밝은 표정으로 절을 둘러보는 사람들을 보고 있으니 괜히 기분까지 좋아지는 느낌.

화암사는 강원도 고성, 금강산 남쪽 자락에 자리한 천년 고찰이라고 한다. 신라 시대에 창건된 오래된 사찰로, 설악산과 동해 풍경이 함께 어우러지는 곳이라 경치 좋은 절로도 유명하다고 한다. 특히 절 뒤편의 거대한 수바위와 주변 암릉 풍경은 화암사의 상징처럼 느껴졌다.

산길 따라 천천히 걷다 보니 계곡물 소리도 들리고, 바람도 시원해서 잠깐 쉬어가기 참 좋은 곳이라는 생각이 들었다. 단순히 관광지 느낌보다는 자연 속에서 마음이 편안해지는 공간에 가까웠다.

석가탄신일이라 그런지 절 안 분위기도 더 특별하게 느껴졌다.
연등 아래를 지나며 소원을 적는 사람들, 가족끼리 사진을 찍는 모습, 조용히 두 손 모아 기도하는 사람들까지. 각자의 방식으로 하루를 보내고 있는 모습이 인상적이었다.

조용한 산사도 좋지만, 이렇게 북적이는 화암사도 참 좋았던 하루.

title.title: ‎The Season Bruno Fernandes Proved Everyone Wrong ‎
title.body:
‎There has been a lot of debate about who truly deserves the Premier League Player of the Season award for this campaign. Many people have mentioned players like Declan Rice and David Raya because of their massive contributions to Arsenal’s title-winning campaign. And honestly, they have both been outstanding this season.
‎
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmNQZv2juYNaNHR8B458zzDi8r3CQaNQJ6M4mKHTK9kieb/images%2033.jpeg 

‎[Source](https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&source=web&rct=j&opi=89978449&url=https://www.facebook.com/SportPremiHQ/posts/-bruno-fernandes-premier-league-stats-this-season%25EF%25B8%258F-34-games%25EF%25B8%258F-8-goals-20-assists-/996654262868096/&ved=2ahUKEwjt66qSt9GUAxWda0EAHVXvNfEQr4kDegQIHxAA&usg=AOvVaw1GbH8TPdp0JqPU6t-rtQ0D)
‎
‎But for me, one name stands above the rest which is Bruno Fernandes of Manchester United.
‎
‎Sometimes football is not just about who lifts the trophy. Sometimes it is about who carried the biggest burden, who stepped up when everything depended on them, and who consistently delivered when the pressure was highest. That is exactly what Bruno Fernandes has done this season for Manchester United.
‎
‎Without Bruno, I really do not think Manchester United would be back in the Champions League or finished at the position they do this season. He has been the heartbeat of the team from start to finish. Every important moment, every comeback, every crucial win, somehow Bruno was involved. Goals, assists, leadership, energy, creativity, he gave everything.
‎
‎What even impresses me most is how he keeps producing despite the criticism he receives. Season after season, people doubt him, question his attitude, and sometimes overlook his influence. Yet when you look at the numbers and watch the games closely, you realize how important he really is.
‎
‎This season, he has already equaled the 20 assist record set by Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne and Arsenal icon Thierry Henry. That alone tells you the level he has reached. And with one game still left to play, he has the chance to make history by becoming the player with the most assists in a single Premier League season.
‎
‎That is not luck. That is brilliance.
‎
‎To me, Bruno Fernandes has been the most creative, decisive, and influential player in the league this season. While others had strong systems around them, Bruno often looked like the one holding Manchester United together.
‎
‎Football fans will always debate awards, and everyone has their opinion which is good. But personally, I believe Bruno Fernandes has fully earned the right to be called the Premier League Player of the Season.
‎

title.title: ROSES ARE RED
title.body:
At the quiet corner of my backyard blooms a red rose,proudly beneath the sky as if guarding silent memories. Each morning, its petals awaken with the touch of sunlight, glowing calming like a secret by nature itself. Though small in place, it carries a beauty too lovely to ignore — a reminder that even the simplest corners of life can hold something extraordinary.
![IMG-20260522-WA0088.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/adediji/242NoLWUyUfKoGVpzuYmbzvA9u4TZst6iCAnQ5cvsTWGgEu8ejQqt6vdNp9V5MrocKwRp.jpg)

Whenever the breeze dances through the yard, the rose gently sways, as though telling only the heart can understand. Surrounded by thorns blooming fearlessly, it speaks of strength hidden wi softness. In my backyard, this red rose is more than a flower; it is a quiet companion, painting ordinary days with beauty, peace, and a touch of wonder.

title.title: It's Just A Song
title.body:
It's quite beautiful. Wait, the one where everything went sideways? Just add that through the middle, guys. I'm just kidding.

I know. Melody has a beautiful, beautiful voice, and she has such a sweet spirit. I love hearing her sing.

I miss the space, but it sounds like a great time. Dante, I think you wanted to sing a song for us. Oh, I did want to sing for DJ, but he left.

I did wish him a happy birthday, but I could sing a song. I guess so. Hold on.

I like the sound effects. I'm trying to make believe I'm turning pages when I'm really not. Actually, this song is right in front of me.

And HR didn't approve this, so she just gave me a middle finger in the DMs, so I don't know how this is going to go. All right, this one was for DJ and anyone else who's been through it and back a few times. She lifts her skirt up to her knees, walks through the garden rows with her bare feet laughing.

I never learned to count my blessings. I choose instead to dwell in my disaster. I walk on down the hill through grass grown tall and brown, and still it's hard sometimes to let go of my pain.

I'm past the busted back of that old and rusted Cadillac that sinks into this field collecting rain. Will I always be this way? So empty, so estranged. Of these cutthroat busted sunsets, these cold and damp wild mornings, I've grown weary.

If through my cracked and dusty dime store lifts I spoke these words, how loud would no one hear me? Lay your blouse across the chair. Let fall the flowers from your hair and kiss me with that country mouth so plain. Outside the rain is tapping on the leaves.

To me it sounds like they're applauding us. The quiet love we've made. Will I always feel this way? So empty, so estranged.

Well, I've looked my demons in the eyes, laid bare my chest, said do your best to destroy me. See, I've been hell and back so many times. I must admit, you kind of bored me.

There's a lot of things that can kill a man and a lot of ways to die. Yes, and some already did and walked beside me. There's a lot of things I don't understand, but so many people like.

It's the hurt I hide that fuels the fire inside me. Will I always feel this way? So empty, so estranged. Thank you, Dante, that was beautiful.

Thank you, thank you. You're welcome. Yeah, that was just, like I said, I know that DJ's been through a lot.

I've spoken to him and been in spaces with him, and that's a song by Ray LaMontagne called Empty. It's just a song that I thought of, and I know he's been through hell and back. Like most of us in here or else we wouldn't be in this hot yoga slash reflections of self S2E7 slash HR approved links space.

I started a challenge of taking 100 days off to mainly focus on my health and overall personal development and used this account as a personal blog to keep track of all my activity. I enjoyed it and continued afterward trying to build better habits and find a good balance between health, fitness, work, entertainment, and my personal life...

Saturday was another hot day where I ended up skipping my last yoga class. And started my acceleration toward fully getting ready to leave to Thailand for a few months. It feels like I'm almost ready but at the same time have many small individual things to do left which add up with 2 more days to go. In the early evening there were some football matches getting too the end of the season on Sunday with 3 more to go which all will be played at the same time. I went out to get some sun portective lip gloss and also took home some chocolate. title.title: The Inner Voice Reminding Me I’m Not Alone
title.body:
<div  class=text-justify>

Life has been great for the last few months and it's not because I've got everything figured. Infact, if I'll look at the things I'm struggling with, there are way too much for me to say life's been great for me. But there is this inner push with assurance I have inside me that I can't explain.

But I love the feeling, a feeling that tells me that everything will work out fine eventually and that I just need to keep pushing. I get more negative thoughts than positive ones some days but I noticed how the negatives shrink when the feeling comes with all it's grace and positivity.

![file_00000000051471f4b4b1babbfee17baf.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/merit.ahama/Eq5JJkKk332CjW9F2oTd7XB2Amg3uV21hbCWWqX2gK6aFb49mDoc62vRUoDHMWQL7kR.png)

Like I shared in the past, being grateful is one of the best ways to avoid complaining and see more good in yours and others life. Being especially grateful for being alive is the biggest and it is what has been bringing this good feeling to me every single day. I'm excited about little things.

I woke up this morning and a song was playing in my head, a part of the lyrics says *\
* and then the lyrics went on to say, *\

* and that's God. That was a powerful line that got me smiling whenever I listened to the song, it's like an assurance from God that I am covered, He is thinking about me every single day even when I'm in my lowest. And I want to remind anyone to have that same thoughts, we are never alone. I love melodies and harmonies made from music a lot and this song gave all that with beautiful lyrics that got me feeling so happy, grateful and assured. I think this is a great start to my morning and facing whatever comes, being assured that I'm not alone. Do listen to the song. https://youtu.be/h4SmxOHR2Pw?si=bsf4e6AKoBhTEFLd
I especially love the merging of the two songs in one, they call it medley. Imagine an awesome one knows and see you. I don't know what's greater than that. I feel so high spirited and happy writing this, I pray and ask that this feeling continue in my life and in everyone who wishes for it also.

The seeded random embeddings are deterministic -- same path or query always produces the same vector. In a real system you'd replace `_make_embedding` with actual CLIP inference, but the search and ranking logic stays identical. Cosine similarity between unit vectors is just their dot product, which is the core operation behind every embedding-based retrieval system we've built since episode #63.

            ie = [rng.gauss(0, 1) for _ in range(embed_dim)]
            te = [rng.gauss(0, 1) for _ in range(embed_dim)]

            self.text_embs.append(self._normalize(te))

    def _generate_data(self):
        pairs = []
        for cat in range(self.n_categories):
            for _ in range(self.pairs_per_cat):
                pairs.append(cat)
        return pairs

    def _normalize(self, vec):
        norm = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in vec))
        if norm < 1e-10:
            return vec
        return [x / norm for x in vec]

    def _dot(self, a, b):
        return sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))

    def compute_loss(self, img_indices, txt_indices,

The alignment gap (matching similarity minus non-matching similarity) is the metric that actually matters. A gap of 0 means the model can't distinguish matching from non-matching pairs. As training progresses, matching pairs get pulled together while non-matching pairs get pushed apart -- that's the entire contrastive learning dynamic in two numbers.

The per-category breakdown is where the real insight lives. Counting and color questions tend to work well with simple keyword matching because the answers are directly stated in image descriptions. Spatial reasoning is harder because \

requires understanding relational prepositions. Reading/OCR is even harder since it depends on how exactly the text was transcribed in the description. __main__\\.title: Women Are To Be Love Not To Be Tame
__main__\\.body:
Yesterday, I went to visit a friend, and while we were out together, something happened that I honestly can’t stop thinking about, like it gets on my nerves.

My friend wanted to get a few things so I followed her, and while waiting for her, I overheard two men talking nearby. At first, I wasn’t really paying attention until one of them asked the other how he manages to keep his wife “under control” even with the way he behaves sometimes.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmSKjvGopyURFw9A6eceL4S63hWqc3UnAD2wiUmxEGmC9d/1000219307.jpg 

[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/women-friends-meadow-lying-girls-1487825/)

The other man laughed and said something like, “Just don’t let a woman become too independent or too sure of herself. Once she fully relies on you emotionally and financially, she’ll always stay no matter how badly you treat her.”

I don’t know why, but hearing that really hit me deeply. I kept asking myself, is this really how some people see women? Like we are people to control instead of people to love? It honestly made me sad because there are actually men who think a woman’s confidence should be reduced just so she won’t have the strength to walk away.

To me, that is not love at all. Love shouldn’t be about making someone feel weak, dependent, or trapped. Real love should make you feel safe enough to grow. It should encourage confidence, not destroy it. I can’t imagine loving someone and then intentionally trying to stop them from becoming better, stronger, or more independent just because I’m scared they might leave one day.

And the painful part is that many women are already living in situations like this without even realizing it. Some are constantly discouraged from chasing their dreams, getting good jobs, speaking up, or even believing in themselves. Little by little, they lose their confidence and start depending on the same person hurting them.

That conversation honestly opened my eyes in a different way. A woman is not something to “tame.” She is a human being with emotions, dreams, ambitions, and value. Wanting a woman to stay because she loves you is different from wanting her to stay because she feels stuck and has nowhere else to go.

I believe a healthy relationship should be built on respect, trust, support, and understanding not manipulation. A man who truly loves a woman will want to see her grow, succeed, and become confident in herself, not intentionally make her feel small.

To every woman reading this, please never let anyone make you feel like your confidence is a problem. Keep growing, keep learning, keep building yourself emotionally and financially. The right people will never feel threatened by your strength. That short conversation yesterday stayed in my mind longer than I expected. Maybe because deep down, I know this kind of mindset still exists in society, and honestly, that’s scary.


**Thanks for checking on my blog and have a wonderful day**

__main__\\.title: Chicken apple gourd stew (tindy chicken)
__main__\\.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaMn7KiBZJ1FtFrgjbSgXx8jZRfKtuBG9GnyRh2rEv1Kx/1779531362265.jpg)
Hello hi everyone how are you greetings to all of you and welcome to my another recipe blog in the community @hivelearners . Sunday is also a day of special food for enjoying at lunch . Today I cooked **chicken apple I gourd stew** . This is not my favourite but my mothers favourite vegetable . It's also known **Indian gourd** . After many years today I cooked this vegetable . I want to share my recipe with all of you so let's start the .

**Ingredients**

One kg chicken 

One kg apple gourd 

Onions 

Tomato 

Green chillies 

Crushed Ginger garlic 

Fresh green coriander 

**Spices**

Salt 

Turmeric 

Red chilli 

Chilli flakes 

Black pepper 

Cumin seeds 

Garam masala 

**Process **

First I cut apple gourd into small pieces then washed under water very well . Then I also cleaned and washed chicken and put all . Later on I cut other ingredients like onions ginger garlic and green. Chopped them into the chopper machine .

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYWLUAUnBKKmhvVweUbq1x4si2pFmEDueXwEFSYsDwHj2/1779533039469.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfDuSrCJ3LVswx5zJjTbrUeoQ4k6FheRFCZNjufD1E28h/1779533055804.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdk6Mf15xWeG9uz76apfyhZt99BeV49Er4XNxTRoq8eZq/1779533069814.jpg)

I fired chicken in the oil till the golden brown then added chopped ingredients and tomato slices . I mixed well and cooked 5 minutes .


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNwM7yo1UTngrQC9eFLicHXgsVRrx9hJ4QjSCMq3eyCm5/1779533204979.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaNQrA82NBqzz96jAhwVPqn6ST6KNFykyQkDhou3aD4nY/1779533314479.jpg)

I added half glass water for cooking the ingredients and chicken . Then I added whole spices that I mentioned above .

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPSde1q1T9rcNTy4oXqY2uQq5RkVX8tmTjpvWr5Qy76jy/1779533364182.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfGSft5nCjgutgfJaEEhg8NmJDtDwyNXSGJfxcRTsEUzr/1779533382567.jpg)

Later on I added apple gourd vegetable in the chicken and mixed well .


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQiX3vpUj2eLjmEkWr8cvX4byiUBmx56RJdtWocD6vRK3/1779533448621.jpg)
I added one and half glass water in the vegetable and covered with lid under midum flame for cooking till the oil separated and gravy dry  .


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQbS6WsFAKMmXXXcYQisrFWRfWeSC4Kbx2JrrwYXsdccF/1779533505327.jpg)
When vegetable cooked I spread fresh green coriander and black pepper and garam masala . I served it with flatbread.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeuvGFakTj8G7hvumeGhxDhDvwyvJ1mM2q87zyZqa22Pu/1779533576975.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXrb6RExyowwEum8f7sakWbLHuPmc5ez4BrZKYFFBvwQF/1779533590550.jpg)


**Final look**


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVNjeSmUg3hgFXp9pyWjzWnHjw4CYQUFBKR2jpLixwxCn/1779533625655.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeeoWyjxwjLGREyG99eBLPt3TQLuPv6KWFjcRkgKJ6XzX/1779533638274.jpg)
Don't forget also giving me feedback on my recipe . See you soon . Take care . Bye bye .

楼下邻居大叔又送给我两盆吊兰，这花听说特别好养活。家里空置的花盆不少，前前后后我也添置了好多绿植，幸福树、富贵树、栀子花、蝴蝶兰样样都有，细数下来种类真的不少。
 
看着大叔手里的吊兰枝叶繁茂，长势格外好看。我把它移栽到了我的大花盆里，小盆又还给大叔让他继续培养其他植物。

我们同住一个单元楼下摆满了大大小小的盆栽，各色花草应有尽有。大叔还叮嘱我找个好看的陶瓷浅盆，打算帮我移栽金钱草。等会儿我就来网购一个。

我与大叔分享网购绿植的经历，大叔劝我不必再破费，日后想要花草直接跟他说就行，还说看中哪盆自己拿就好，我反倒觉得不好意思。
 
闲聊时我说起之前养枯丢掉的两棵幸福树，没想到正被大叔从垃圾桶捡回来养活了，不由得由衷佩服他的养花本事。看，这就是我丢掉的幸福树，如今又重新被大叔呵护起来。
 
大叔平日里十分热心，常常把自己培育的花草无偿分给邻居。谁家绿植养得状态不佳，送回他手里调理一番，总能重新焕发生机。

兰花等各类花卉在他打理下生机盎然，也给整个小区装点出满满的绿意。
 
我曾好奇问过大叔，当初选房为何没选一楼，若是带个小院子，正好能随心栽种花草。大叔坦言，两个儿子担心低层潮气重，便没选择一楼，想来他心里多多少少还是有些遗憾。毕竟老家房子没拆时院子里可是摆满了花花草草。如今也只是取一小块地方种上一点，幸好我们这儿的物业管的较松，不然大叔这爱好和手艺可就没地儿发挥了。
 
大叔的两个儿子如今都在外生活，大儿子在上饶开牙科诊所，小儿子在政府单位还是我的老同学，娶了吉林的姑娘，小两口打算丁克生活。大叔心态特别开明豁达，从不会强求子女按照世俗的标准生活，只希望孩子们日子过得舒心安稳就好。两个孩子都被教导得懂事优秀，如今老两口相守相伴，日常侍弄花草、悠闲度日，生活平淡又安稳。

__main__\\.title: So that my daughter can read Sir Nigel by Conan Doyle [Eng/Esp]
__main__\\.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma2atMZHziVtd4zcCeGuL38tHruTmaKe5ege678PLxpxU/1779607076928.jpg)



***
***
When I think of the first true readings my daughter should have, those that leave a mark, I cannot help but imagine Sir Nigel in her hands. It is not the most famous novel by Arthur Conan Doyle, but for me it is his most noble work.

The story takes us to 14th century England, where Sir Nigel Loring is a young squire of humble lineage but with a fiery heart. To earn the right to ask for Lady Mary's hand, he must perform three deeds that prove his worth. And there lies the first lesson: love is not begged for; it is deserved through actions.

***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRVLajGDs2oNnDsUUUeqXrDqdwX6smiw4yGGjVBA7CRwS/1779607077013.jpg)

***

What moves me most about Nigel is that he is not an invincible warrior. He is small in stature, sometimes clumsy, but he possesses an iron will. His values are not abstract ideas but rules that govern every gesture. When he accepts a challenge, he does not think of glory, but of not letting his loved ones down.

In an era where so many young adult stories show cynical or morally ambiguous heroes, Nigel seems to me a balm that reminds us that courage is not the absence of fear, but acting in spite of it, and that a pledged word is worth more than any easy victory. Without a doubt, treating others well is not weakness, but the greatest strength.
***



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXCTYfvVbmwU6oaU9hES7f6J9ctDum4s683wGC6mrzcFz/1779607274106.jpg)


***
Doyle wrote this novel at the end of his career, almost as a spiritual testament, and it shows that he took care with it, because the dialogues sparkle, the battles feel real, and the medieval landscape envelops without overwhelming. But above all, within it beats the conviction that a decent young man with clear ideals can change his destiny without betraying himself.

I will not lie to my teenage daughter to whom I recommend this reading: the language is denser than that of current young adult sagas, and the values of chivalry may sound strange to her. But that is precisely why I want her to read it now, not in ten years, so that she can argue with Nigel, so that she can ask herself whether his sense of honor can be translated to her world, and above all, so that she can see for herself that a story with swords and castles can speak of very intimate things, such as faithfulness to oneself, the patience to prove who you are, and the beauty of striving for an ideal.
***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmd3y4DqMkh794Zr6Pb18XbRpXTyiiRPCM6GJ215Q3m5jB/1779607274049.jpg)


***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeygHmwUwtGcAQ3qRh7M9WHBaNyeyYYRGsJufM6Lgdqts/1779607274153.jpg)

***
Perhaps she will find passages old fashioned, perhaps she will even smile at so many \

but I hope she also discovers, as I did, that beneath the armor beats a young man not so different from her, and that never goes out of style.

<center>📖</center>
<center>📖</center>

## <center> Para que mi hija lea a Sir Nigel, de Conan Doyle </center>



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXi3i99629srSmxF6T9iPe4iPua1m6NsoU8bZQPueMQLE/1779607076972.jpg)


***
***






Cuando pienso en las primeras lecturas de verdad que debería hacer mi hija, esas que dejan huella, no puedo evitar imaginar Sir Nigel en sus manos. No es la novela más famosa de Arthur Conan Doyle, pero para mí es su obra más noble.

La historia nos lleva a la Inglaterra del siglo XIV, donde Sir Nigel Loring es un joven escudero de linaje humilde pero corazón ardiente, que para ganar el derecho a pedir la mano de lady Mary debe realizar tres hazañas que demuestren su valor. Y ahí está la primera lección: el amor no se mendiga, se merece con obras.
***

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRVLajGDs2oNnDsUUUeqXrDqdwX6smiw4yGGjVBA7CRwS/1779607077013.jpg)



***
Lo que más me emociona de Nigel es que no es un guerrero invencible. Es pequeño de estatura, a veces torpe, pero posee una voluntad férrea. Sus valores no son ideas abstractas, sino reglas que rigen cada gesto, y cuando acepta un desafío no piensa en la gloria, sino en no fallar a los suyos.

En una época donde tantas historias juveniles muestran héroes cínicos o moralmente ambiguos, Nigel me parece un bálsamo que nos recuerda que la valentía no es ausencia de miedo, sino actuar a pesar de él, y que la palabra empeñada vale más que cualquier victoria fácil. Sin dudas, tratar bien a los demás no es debilidad, sino la máxima fortaleza.
***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXCTYfvVbmwU6oaU9hES7f6J9ctDum4s683wGC6mrzcFz/1779607274106.jpg)


***
Doyle escribió esta novela al final de su carrera, casi como un testamento espiritual, y se nota que la cuidó porque los diálogos tienen chispa, las batallas se sienten reales, y el paisaje medieval envuelve sin abrumar. Pero sobre todo, late en ella la convicción de que un muchacho decente, con ideales claros, puede cambiar su destino sin traicionarse.

No le voy a mentir a mi hija adolescente a la que le recomiendo esta lectura: el lenguaje es más denso que el de las sagas juveniles actuales, y los valores de la caballería pueden sonarle extraños. Pero por eso mismo quiero que lo lea ahora, no dentro de diez años, para que discuta con Nigel, para que se pregunte si su sentido del honor es trasladable a su mundo, y sobre todo para que compruebe por sí misma que una historia con espadas y castillos puede hablar de cosas muy íntimas como la fidelidad a uno mismo, la paciencia para demostrar quién se es, y la belleza de esforzarse por un ideal.
***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmd3y4DqMkh794Zr6Pb18XbRpXTyiiRPCM6GJ215Q3m5jB/1779607274049.jpg)


***



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeygHmwUwtGcAQ3qRh7M9WHBaNyeyYYRGsJufM6Lgdqts/1779607274153.jpg)


***
Tal vez ella encuentre pasajes anticuados, incluso tal vez sonría ante tanto \

, pero espero que también descubra, como yo, que bajo la armadura late un muchacho no tan distinto a ella, y eso nunca pasa de moda.

__main__\\.title: Waiting in the airport sucks.
__main__\\.body:
#
Too little time to do anything, too much time to kill

Usually when I'm stuck in an airport I try to hit an airport lounge. Free food, comfy chairs, and reliable washrooms. However, in smaller airports or in this case when I arrive early in the morning and don't feel like their breakfast food... then I'm stuck in the general waiting area. Unfortunately that means overpriced everything, people everywhere, and not much to do or look at. **which sucks** Because I really want to keep working on the GLD website. Sure it isn't much but but I want to finally get things to **\

** status so that people can use it and try things out.


### The Faucet

On that note I would like to thank @fnzcmd for using the faucet that I setup and mentioned once.  Since he has a 7 day streak I'm assuming that :

* The faucet works
* It is giving incremental increases the more it is used
* @fnzcmd is awesome for posting daily.  ***Good job!***

But I will admit that the faucet looks pretty awful and doesn't really feel like part of anything larger.  So, there is a newer version under construction and it will actually be the launch page for the GLD website when it does launch.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cinderclaw.gld/23wzzr5rZnyxWKY3KgipAxf7KThZAjfqbtZ5b8s8iHMqhzijHjdfvpa762afyKeUUkWaZ.png)

It now has a clock on the page.  That's kind of important because the faucet looks back during the day to see if anything was posted.  It doesn't look back 24 hours but rather by date and it uses the UTC to determine the date.  

So, when before it didn't give any payout even when someone has posted recently?  That's because there was a post a couple hours prior but on a different UTC date. (UTC=Universal Time Code).

### Delegation payments.

@hiveabbyftp curation account will be getting a boost to its HP soon as a couple of supporters are moving their support from @helios.voter back to @hiveabbyftp.  I'm watching curation rewards closely with a little app that shows fairly regular curation payments and HP growth


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cinderclaw.gld/23tGXmhzMBbNJyA9SWz1t5C6jnGvKUYzk5jZZMvpch29n7Qapt69C2Tq28gb2TWeQ6p16.png)

More importantly.  Using that data I can figure out how much I'll be distributing to those people who delegate HP to the project.  Things are still in the works right now but the plan is to make HP delegation rewards claimable from the GLD website daily.  With every delegator receiving a portion of the rewards proportionate to the amount delegated but requiring them to actually claim it.  The goal?  Reward active members rather than just get passive delegations.  Exact mechanism is yet to be determined but here is a sneak peak at what I'm working on.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cinderclaw.gld/23tRxWeXbbRpSMdsTfrAzEciSLZsss9UjTY2Zu7nNQxist96iby9oLfm3C6uxuvqFrWeh.png)

Things likely won't be running for at least two weeks (and possibly much longer depending on schedule) as I'll be in Scotland vacationing but **IF** it were launched today?

@drstealth would get a daily amount (if claimed) of 0.138125 HP/day * 365 days for a hypothetical 50.41 Hive on 100 HP delegated (50% APY).  Which of course brings up the question:  **Why so much?**.  Well, it would be because all of the curation rewards would be distributed to delegators and the @hiveabbyftp account wouldn't be keeping any of its rewards but rather give it to those who delegate.

***Again... this is the plan, it is not in operation yet!***

For now there are absolutely rewards being given out but its done manually and weekly using a different formula.

Now GLS token is exchangeable on the hive-engine 1:1 for HIVE 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cinderclaw.gld/23tmm5sZDaSpSzBpn4iXoXuujNa5RrdZnoRzjaWudpCHJRfMRNKTG89QiBbRzGb4SjWKC.png)

So the 0.1595 GLS = 0.1595 HIVE (its larger than just the proposed delegation reward because its a combined payment of delegation and holding GLD tokens).


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cinderclaw.gld/23viKE9KhzYfGD4kBgyVmgBdhN3aVjzsNa6JnH4xsJnVWhfyPVeKZef2CpWhbBtevXo4s.png)

### Why am I posting this?

Well, 

1) I'm bored in the airport
2) I want to show I'm actually working on things behind the scenes 
3) To let people like @drstealth, @lovlygirl, and @fmzcmd that I see their support and appreciate it.

### Looking forward to things moving forward

At the moment things are kind of boring in this community as nothing has happened for a long long time, but I really am trying to make things better and who knows maybe one day I'll succeed :)

__main__\\.title: Splinterlands: Avoid using Taunt monsters in Ferocity
__main__\\.body:
Splinterlands is a complex game, and it allows for various cards and strategies. Each fight is different as there are various rulesets applied, and this can give specific cards an advantage depending on how you use them. In this post, I talk about a great battle where I saw a battle where I took advantage of the ruleset.

## Rule Set, Battle, and Plan

<center>![rule set.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jfang003/23u5VJG4Q9TwCD9Gd33zqRXNHSfDmHZhV6KNJmQNRTgf3kWPFY78w9fBC4haMSGL3NDKN.png)</center>

The rulesets this time are Equal Opportunity and Ferocity. This means that all monsters gain the opportunity and fury ability. There is also 77 mana available, and I can use fire and death [splinter](https://leofinance.io/@leoglossary/leoglossary-splinter).

|Splinter|Mana Cost|Position|Reason|
|---|---|---|---|
|Barthalamas|6|Summoner|+1 speed|
|Frankarsgard|7|1st||
|Great Bear Druid|9|2nd||
|Chaos Furybringer|6|3rd||
|Agniavan Salamander|8|4th|Blast|
|Sturdy Axe Warden|8|5th||
|A'lan Musketeer|8|6th|Double Strike|
|Total Mana:|52|||

My summoner is Barthalamas for the +1 speed. I have Frankarsgard. After that are my melee monsters Great Bear Druid and Chaos Furybringer. Finally, I have my ranged monsters as my damage dealers.

The focus of this lineup is to keep my monsters alive while dealing damage and outlasting my opponent. I don't have a taunt monster, but my backline is all placed around damage. They have some health, but with the speed increase from my Archon, I should be able to deal damage before they die.

### Round 1

![round 1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jfang003/23tbyi6fuCSnT6UNQGA8kp6e78Rx46UUyfLwJzbx44PSMmQ2bH9bniJLEZ3h5ptZoPuL6.png)
At first glance, I think that this match can go either way. My opponent may have a taunt monster, but it should die quite fast because of the fury. My opponent also has a decent setup, but I feel the lineup is skewed due to the ranged monster in the middle.

### Round 4

![round 4.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jfang003/23tvkxQSLbVYc1XQJ9oWarhN6aVuCcjRMPCkSqhsoHwiRywux1hDpraxEU2W8EzBoJkDP.png)
A few rounds later, my opponent is down to 1 monster, while I still have 4. This is my win because it is unlikely for all of my monsters to miss their attack for multiple rounds.

![conclusion.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jfang003/23tvkxQSLbVYc1XxGTYFhEirHLsMikSXhZKDLFNECZ6giriGifGT4DSsXpBhhcyZQ8NAj.png)
I won later that round.

## Conclusion
The battle did go exactly as planned. I avoided using a taunt monster and focused on damage with a speed archon. While I may not have had the level advantage, I was able to deal quite a bit of damage due to my opponent's weird lineup. The damage just added up, and that monster didn't work out that well for him.

You can see my entire match [here](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_2299da7fd11d0442a8fb5856e093e0f0?ref=jfang003).

What did you think of my match? Was there anything you would have done differently? I think it is quite interesting to see how different players use the same card.

__main__\\.title: ‎Not Every Ending Is a Loss
__main__\\.body:
‎
‎Hi Hive,
‎
‎
‎As I mature, I’m beginning to understand that not everything that leaves my life is meant to destroy me. Some things end because they were never meant to stay forever. While some people walk away because their chapter in my story is complete. And some disappointments happen because life is silently guiding me toward something I cannot yet see.
‎ https://img.leopedia.io/DQmYKHENBCGGE5yCu4rcMLGZzkhLJofsWntCW9dV6K54XeD/claire05-success-3521937_1920.jpg 

‎[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/success-challenge-mountain-summit-3521937/)
‎
‎There was a time when I viewed every setback as a loss. Every rejection felt really personal, every delay felt like failure and every closed door made me question my worth. I used to hold on tightly to things that were clearly slipping away, believing that losing them meant losing a part of myself.
‎
‎But growth changes my perspective.
‎
‎I now realize that life has different ways of teaching us. Sometimes it is redirection. What we wanted may not go align with where we are supposed to go. The opportunity we actually cried over missing might have saved us from future regret. The relationship that ended may have prevented deeper pain later on. Not every “no” is punishment. But some are protection in disguise.
‎
‎Other times, it is realization. Certain experiences are meant to be our eyes opener. They reveal who people actually are, what really matters, and how strong we truly can be. Pain has a strange way of exposing truths we neglected when life was fun and comfortable. It teaches lessons pride would never allow us to peacefully learn.
‎
‎And then there is protection. Looking back now, I can now thank God for things I once begged Him for but never received.  I thought I was being denied happiness at the time, but I was being protected from confusion, heartbreak, and unnecessary battles in reality. Some storms we never entered are blessings we fail to actually recognize.
‎
‎Maturity teaches me to stop seeing every ending as destruction. Because sometimes life removes things they no longer fit the person you are becoming. Growth requires space. Healing requires distance and purpose sometimes requires separation.
‎
‎So now, when things do not go my way, I try not to panic. I remind myself that life is not always taking from me. But sometimes, it is guiding me, guarding me, or teaching me.
‎
‎Nothing is ever truly a loss. It is either redirection, protection, or realization.
‎
‎![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYaWnApEziAtLL5Zwv3ZNbDjRfSfG6h5njgTrpyasnE6y/1775569275821.png)
‎

__main__\\.title: FIRST MOUNTAIN HIKE ⛰️🇬🇧 Enjoying the views
__main__\\.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWv9GjJsPBsTHZHrHsZZHddHByWpHEgpZbbqWVRwfWpam/1779426436313.jpg)

[//]:# (!worldmappin 53.10731 lat -2.02189 long  d3scr)

### Hello and welcome! :)

> Witam i zapraszam! :)

I recently went on a very spontaneous trip to the UK, which I planned literally just two days beforehand. During my stay, my boyfriend, his family and I went on a hike in the hills near the town of Leek.

> Ostatnio miał miejsce bardzo spontaniczny wyjazd do Wielkiej Brytanii, który zaplanowałam dosłownie 2 dni wcześniej. Podczas mojego pobytu wraz z moim chłopakiem i jego rodziną wybraliśmy się na wycieczkę po górach znajdujących się niedaleko miasta Leek.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUXVpcdmSukiatJ7fY6DKepbWmwmP9qnJtc5VEfep4ZnV/1779426467722.jpg)

When we arrived, we were greeted by the sight of picturesque fields full of animals, which was absolutely charming.

> Kiedy dojechaliśmy na miejsce, naszym oczom ukazały się malownicze pola pełne zwierząt, co było bardzo urocze.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX9rVqZ4NrkVLdBMkpRQQRhWvLjBG9Q3GVS6d5uPur74N/1779426467790.jpg)

As we climbed the mountain, the weather changed – it grew increasingly grey, as you can also see from the photos.


> Wraz z wchodzeniem na górę zmieniała się pogoda - robiło się coraz bardziej szaro, co można również zauważyć po zdjęciach.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcWT5wHVGqCoGwTFFFwV3zeo8act1KeTEZssprNGFv26U/1779426467861.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbKTWHFGJ5sZ1Xbe2JQhQTGC1CnsST7sKxQt2ymftXu7Z/1779426467917.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPvTjL1ij8bU2neGaViLpkGRA9KtuK3yeV6iwKDyNuzcs/1779426468009.jpg)

By the time we’d climbed quite high, it started to rain. Fortunately, it wasn’t a heavy downpour and after a while it all settled down.

> Kiedy dotarliśmy już dosyć wysoko, zaczęło padać. Na szczęście nie było to obfity deszcz i po jakimś czasie wszystko się uspokoiło.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfBeTE2gPmR1kuhJjdGrAdbqzY9RDLr4uiu8XP7meszkA/1779426535324.jpg)
It was beautiful up there! We took some photos and decided to climb another mountain.

> Na górze było pięknie! Robiliśmy zdjęcia i zdecydowaliśmy się wejść na jeszcze jedną górę.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPfQQuCFk2y3fQRQyS5o8hyZn1dQTEEkn8GLVmvhEeLqW/1779426535396.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUFv1aJN5RQreouoxtBdbD1EMeSkjvzzz4KvABG3TBxPc/1779426535456.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmefAUwR3G1Fmcr1ttpyQyrvUeRV31zcPKgQrAeAHoppiA/1779426535524.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVmvbpRLAEgvKg4RL93pRJ4ieJ1U19c6AFUMpqrxYKJab/1779426535593.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYdG3Q9SKUfHFKuykBtMm1EPKtwDWskN8BBjBA5vcT3Kk/1779426550981.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTBE7ge5AZfXifcqDiKeMfseYjVpgX3XUsNFu8H6wu2Er/1779426551048.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbWUBQvYBhyoSoKwkBEHvg4JRGyftm6cfoZ6Vm3KhXs8K/1779426551111.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmer1X8n3dLSeB4Bak2zKWr8PkYvBAQ95ifEDmNLLkeywG/1779426551176.jpg)
In the photo below, you can see a cottage perched on the slope of the second hill, which was quite interesting. We noticed a sign stating that it was private property, so we simply carried on.

> Na zdjęciu poniżej widać domek stojący u zbocza drugiej góry, co było bardzo ciekawe. Zauważyliśmy napis, który informował, że to teren prywatny, więc po prostu poszliśmy dalej.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaLTfp2dXmAxFUXRHmHP3HvHw3upTVmVNtFMxRnKdveZ8/1779426551240.jpg)

All in all, it was my first time climbing and I really enjoyed it, even despite the sudden change in the weather. The hills weren’t particularly steep and it was a pleasant climb. We’ve arranged another hike in a few weeks’ time, so I’ll definitely be posting about it on my blog :)

> Podsumowując, to był mój pierwszy raz na wspinaczce i bardzo mi się podobało, nawet pomimo nagłej zmiany pogody. Góry nie były mocno strome i wchodziło się na nie przyjemnie. Umówiliśmy się na kolejny hike za kilka tygodni, więc na pewno będzie z tego post na moim blogu:)

#### Stay tuned!
